      "metadata": {
        "displayText": "you're working on sinjoh. read the project documentation to familiarize yourself first. you'll also need to get familiar with kohjoh, pokeplatinum (the original source), pokeplatinum-3ds (the existing new3ds-only port), and coffeepot. we are going to take a very different route. you are going to bootstrap an entirely new source port of pokemon platinum, as a nintendo 3ds homebrew. your end goal is to replicate all of the remaster enhancements of pokeplatinum-3ds, but based on kohjoh's more sane internals, and targeting the original 2011 3ds - not the 2015 new 3ds. some fancy things like scaling might be too much for the original 3ds meager hardware, and that's okay. as it turns out, if we pre-compute wideart at compile/package time, wideart is cheap enough for o3ds - so you must include that too. your goal is to squeeze the remaster/port into the old3ds hardware, not to worry about new3ds enhancements. you only need to get sinjoh-platinum working, forget about sinjoh-diamond or sinjoh-pearl for now. most of the hard work, engineering and research has already been done for you. you should refer heavily to the reference material in the workdir. you will test your own work using an emulator - see how far you can get with lotus v0.0.2. i believe that build currently defaults to always software rendering, so you'll need to find out how to force it to use vulkan. make sure you run lotus in windowed mode, so i can watch what you're doing. if you have too much trouble with lotus, you are permitted to use vanilla azahar instead, which is also available to you. again, read the docs before you start writing code. all the hard work has already been done for you.                 "text": "Read file C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\sinjoh\\README.md, lines 1-108\n1: # Sinjoh\n2: \n3: Performance work for `pokeplatinum-3ds`: **shared New 3DS wins first, an experimental Old 3DS tier as the stretch goal.**\n4: \n5: ## The reframing\n6: \n7: This is not an \"O3DS support\" proposal, and it does not ask the upstream maintainer to own an Old 3DS test lab.\n8: \n9: The upstream project is built for the New 3DS. It already boots on an Old 3DS, but only with the classic display (`remaster off` is the Old 3DS default), and the remastered display is advertised for New 3DS only. Its maintainer has no reason to accept a second hardware support burden. So the plan is framed around costs that are visible on the New 3DS:\n10: \n11: - CPU-transformed, CPU-lighted 3D geometry, including the CPU-built 60 FPS in-between scenes,\n12: - software-rasterized 2D and its handover to the GPU, on the same core as the geometry,\n13: - per-sample ADPCM decoding in the software mixer, on the same core as the game,\n14: - scheduling and present-skip rules tuned around those costs.\n15: \n16: Those costs are worst on an Old 3DS, but they are real on a New 3DS too. Removing them gives the New 3DS more 60 FPS headroom, fewer dropped scenes, and shorter worst frames, and helps New 3DS users stuck in the 64 MB memory mode (issue #188). The Old 3DS is the stress test that tells us whether the work is genuinely efficient, not the justification for asking upstream to change its support policy.\n17: \n18: **Every core PR in this series must be defensible on New 3DS terms alone.** The one exception is the final `perf/o3ds-tier` profile, which is additive, opt-in, and can be dropped without losing the New 3DS improvements.\n19: \n20: ## What this is\n21: \n22: - A sequence of focused, reviewable pull requests against `GabeSud0/pokeplatinum-3ds`.\n23: - An adaptation of specific, measured techniques from `kohjoh`, the HGSS O3DS port: a GPU tile atlas and retained 2D layers, retained object-space 3D geometry with clip-volume culling, CPU-baked lighting for stable lists with PICA lighting for the rest, a decoded-ADPCM cache, and conservative frame pacing.\n24: - A plan for proving each change with deterministic tests and the project's existing `[perf]` lines, and for making the maintainer's own New 3DS check quick.\n25: - An eventual `tier o3ds` profile that makes the remaster worth turning on there: both screens filled, native-resolution 3D, widescreen layout, the bottom-screen menu, crisp 2D, stable 30 FPS, working audio and saves.\n26: \n27: ## What this is not\n28: \n29: - Not a fork, a rewrite, or a replacement of the New 3DS renderer.\n30: - Not a request to make Old 3DS the default target or a supported platform in upstream's README.\n31: - Not a port of every kohjoh feature. The N3DS-only effects stay N3DS-only.\n32: - Not a promise that Old 3DS will run every scene at 30 FPS. The tier ships only if it passes its own gates, and stays experimental until it does.\n33: - Not a reason to commit game content, captured assets, or benchmark saves.\n34: \n35: ## The bet\n36: \n37: `pokeplatinum-3ds` currently pays for two expensive compatibility layers:\n38: \n39: 1. **3D is transformed, lit, and clipped on the CPU**, then handed to the GPU as screen-space triangles. Geometry costs about 20-30 ms a scene in the field, plus 3-9 ms for the 60 FPS in-between scene, on the core engine A's 2D drawer also uses. `[PP]`\n40: 2. **2D is drawn in software**, then upscaled and handed to the GPU as textures. Drawing a picture costs about 16.2 ms, 4.6 ms of it handing the picture over. `[PP]` (The once-dominant 864 KB / 15 ms change check was fixed upstream on 2026-10-30, `313ac80`; what remains of it is measured in step 0, not assumed.)\n41: \n42: kohjoh shows that both can be moved off the CPU on O3DS-class hardware: a tile atlas for 2D, retained object-space meshes with a 16-entry matrix palette and clip-volume culling, and lighting that matches the DS's fixed-point arithmetic on held frames. It also shows the trap: **the GPU is the same 268 MHz PICA200 on both models, and Azahar does not charge for vertex work.** Lighting every map vertex on the PICA took kohjoh's Old 3DS frames from about 36 to 57 ms while Azahar showed 30 FPS; baking stable lighting on the CPU fixed it. So the plan retains and caches on the CPU first, moves to the GPU only what pays, and counts GPU work.\n43: \n44: The plan adopts those techniques behind flags, measures them on New 3DS first, and only then assembles the O3DS tier.\n45: \n46: ## Guiding principles\n47: \n48: 1. **New 3DS benefit is the merge case.** If a PR only helps O3DS, it is the final tier or optional, and it goes last.\n49: 2. **Measure current `main` first.** The `[PP]` numbers are weeks old and upstream moves fast; one of them was fixed before this plan was written. Step 0 replaces them.\n50: 3. **Default behavior stays safe.** New backends are opt-in `remaster.txt` lines until they are pixel-correct and measurably faster. The old path remains selectable.\n51: 4. **The default New 3DS configuration is the one that counts.** `fps60`, `smooth3d`, and stereo are on by default; a backend that only works with them off has no merge case.\n52: 5. **GPU time is not free.** Moving work from an 804 MHz CPU to an unchanged 268 MHz GPU needs GPU work counts, not Azahar times.\n53: 6. **One cost per PR.** Each PR names the cost it removes, the test that proves correctness, and the counter that proves the gain.\n54: 7. **No maintainer benchmarks, but an easy maintainer check.** We provide deterministic tests, Azahar instruction counts, and `[perf]` logs; they test in Azahar and on a New 3DS anyway, so we make that a one-scene check. O3DS hardware validation is our job.\n55: 8. **No support burden by surprise.** The O3DS tier is documented as experimental, defaults off, and never changes New 3DS defaults.\n56: 9. **Measure, then keep or revert.** A change that does not beat noise on the target scenes is reverted, even if it looks elegant.\n57: \n58: ## PR map\n59: \n60: Step 0, before any PR: a baseline of current upstream `main` on a New 3DS, an Old 3DS with `remaster off`, and an Old 3DS with `remaster on`.\n61: \n62: Core sequence (11 PRs):\n63: \n64: | # | Branch | What it removes | Primary benefit | Size | Depends on |\n65: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n66: | 1 | `perf/telemetry` | Averages without tails; no mixer timing | Makes every later claim measurable | S | - |\n67: | 2 | `perf/render2d-change` | The residual shown-VRAM hash and H-blank/bitmap full reads | **Conditional:** only if step 0 shows it still matters | M | 1, step 0 |\n68: | 3 | `perf/audio-adpcm` | Repeated ADPCM decode of looping instruments | Core 0 time back to the game; **first merge candidate** | M | 1 |\n69: | 4 | `perf/g2d-atlas-text` | Software text-BG rasterization and handover | Cheaper changed 2D frames; foundation for GPU 2D | L | 1 |\n70: | 5 | `perf/g2d-layers` | Software affine/extended BGs and sprites | Cheaper menus, battles, and effects | XL (split) | 4 |\n71: | 6 | `perf/g2d-effects` | Software windows, blending, brightness, H-blank spans | Full GPU 2D coverage without fallback | XL | 5 |\n72: | 7 | `perf/g3d-census` | Guesswork about which G3 lists can be retained, baked, or interpolated | A go/no-go gate for retained 3D | M | 1 |\n73: | 8 | `perf/g3d-retained` | Per-vertex CPU transform, clipping, and in-between re-clipping of static meshes | Geometry from 20-30 ms toward 8-12 ms a scene with `fps60` on `[TARGET]` | XL | 7 |\n74: | 9 | `perf/g3d-lighting` | Per-vertex CPU lighting | Baked colours for stable lists; PICA lighting for the rest | XL (split) | 8 |\n75: | 10 | `perf/lowend-schedule` | Pacing and priorities tuned for the old costs | More stable 60 FPS on N3DS; tunes the existing O3DS topology | M | 3-6, 8-9 |\n76: | 11 | `perf/o3ds-tier` | The gap between \"fast enough\" and \"configured\" | Opt-in O3DS profile; N3DS defaults untouched | S | all |\n77: \n78: Optional, after the core track:\n79: \n80: | # | Branch | What it removes | Why optional | Size |\n81: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n82: | 12 | `perf/g3d-fifo` | Repeated G3 command decode and submission | Useful for worst-case logic; may be superseded by retained geometry | M |\n83: | 13 | `perf/game-hotpaths` | Telemetry-selected game-logic hot paths | Small, broad game-logic win; not a renderer change | S |\n84: \n85: The detailed briefs are in [`PR_SERIES.md`](PR_SERIES.md).\n86: \n87: ## How to read the rest\n88: \n89: - [`EVIDENCE.md`](EVIDENCE.md) - what the New 3DS pays today, what kohjoh measured (including what went wrong), and which techniques transfer.\n90: - [`PR_SERIES.md`](PR_SERIES.md) - step 0 and the ordered PR briefs: scope, integration points, tests, gates, risks, rollback.\n91: - [`O3DS_TIER.md`](O3DS_TIER.md) - the eventual Old 3DS target, hardware budget, scene corpus, and internal acceptance gates. This is a stretch goal, not an upstream contract.\n92: - [`UPSTREAM_NOTES.md`](UPSTREAM_NOTES.md) - how to make the work reviewable: the maintainer's actual process, PR shape, evidence pack, CI, provenance, AI disclosure.\n93: \n94: ## Status\n95: \n96: Planning only. No code has been written. The numbers in these documents are either quoted from the two repositories' own documentation or explicitly labelled as planning targets (`[TARGET]`); the full source-tag scheme is in [`EVIDENCE.md`](EVIDENCE.md). The first step is the step 0 baseline; the first PR is `perf/telemetry`; the first merge candidate is `perf/audio-adpcm`. Before any code, the opening issue asks the maintainer whether AI-assisted outside PRs are welcome at all (`AI_DISCLOSURE.md` says \"all new features are created by the developer\").\n97: \n98: ### Revision of 2026-11-15\n99: \n100: Checked against `pokeplatinum-3ds` `c84883d`, `kohjoh` `fb0440a`, and the coffeepot hardware pages. Changed:\n101: \n102: - **The flagship cost was already fixed.** The 864 KB / ~15 ms change check describes the code before `313ac80` (2026-10-30). PR 2 is now conditional on a fresh measurement, and the first merge candidate is the ADPCM cache.\n103: - **The GPU and VRAM are the same on both models** (268 MHz, 6 MB). The old hardware table said 133 MHz and 10 MB. GPU-side PRs now report GPU work counts and gate on the New 3DS display rate.\n104: - **kohjoh's later hardware result** (PICA lighting on every vertex: 36 → 57 ms on O3DS, invisible in Azahar; fixed by CPU baking and clip-volume culling) now shapes PRs 8 and 9.\n105: - **`fps60` is on by default and builds in-between scenes from CPU clip-space polygons.** PR 8 must interpolate retained lists' matrices, or it never runs in the default New 3DS configuration.\n106: - **The Old 3DS already boots, has a 2-core topology, and accepts `remaster on`.** The tier, PR 10, and PR 11 build on that instead of inventing it, and step 0 collects the O3DS baseline the plan said did not exist.\n107: - **Integration details:** switches are `remaster.txt` lines (the 3DS build reads no environment variables); `gpuBgs`/`gpuObjs` are per-frame split fields, not user-facing levels; the existing sprite atlas, `port_gx3d_gpusim.c`, the light cache, and the `[perf]`/`[stall]` lines are reused; the mixer has no timing today; the 2D filter modes must be reproduced by the atlas path.\n108: - **Process:** the maintainer does test performance work on a New 3DS; outside PRs are rebased by them; the \"426 line-ending files\" are a property of this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf=true`), not of the repository."

                "text": "Read file C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\sinjoh\\O3DS_TIER.md, lines 1-322\n1: # Old 3DS tier\n2: \n3: > Stretch goal, not an upstream contract. This document describes the eventual\n4: > opt-in profile and the internal gates it must pass. It does not ask the\n5: > maintainer to support Old 3DS, and it does not change New 3DS defaults.\n6: \n7: ## 1. Status\n8: \n9: The core PR series exists to remove costs that are visible on the New 3DS.\n10: The Old 3DS tier is what those costs look like when the CPU is slower and the\n11: memory is tighter. It is assembled last, from backends that already work on\n12: New 3DS terms.\n13: \n14: What exists today, before any of this work:\n15: \n16: - The port boots on an Old 3DS. `remaster off` (the classic display: the DS's\n17:   pictures centred on the 3DS's screens) is the Old 3DS default.\n18: - An Old 3DS user can write `remaster on` in `remaster.txt`. Nothing blocks\n19:   it; they get the New 3DS profile (`fps60`, 2x2 `smooth3d`, stereo) on\n20:   hardware that cannot carry it, with the compositor's memory fallback.\n21: - The port already has an Old 3DS topology: geometry on core 1's share, one\n22:   drawer for both engines on core 0, the data-pack cache at 4 MB instead of\n23:   16. `[PP]`\n24: \n25: So the tier is not \"make it run on Old 3DS\". It is \"make the remastered\n26: display worth turning on there\".\n27: \n28: The tier is:\n29: \n30: - **additive:** it selects the shared backends and turns off effects that do\n31:   not fit;\n32: - **opt-in:** it is off by default on every model, including Old 3DS;\n33: - **experimental:** it ships only if it passes the internal gates below;\n34: - **droppable:** if it fails, the New 3DS PRs still stand.\n35: \n36: It is not:\n37: \n38: - a new renderer;\n39: - a promise that every scene reaches 30 FPS;\n40: - a request for the maintainer to own Old 3DS testing;\n41: - a change to the project's supported-platform statement.\n42: \n43: ## 2. Target experience\n44: \n45: The tier aims to deliver as much of the remastered experience as the hardware\n46: can hold:\n47: \n48: - [ ] Both screens filled, not the classic centered DS screens.\n49: - [ ] Native-resolution 3D on the upper screen, without stereo.\n50: - [ ] Widescreen layout where the scene supports it.\n51: - [ ] The bottom-screen menu.\n52: - [ ] Crisp 2D: the GPU 2D path, not a blurry upscale.\n53: - [ ] A stable 30 FPS target in the field and in battles.\n54: - [ ] Audio intact: music, effects, and sequencing.\n55: - [ ] Saves intact: read, write, reboot, load.\n56: \n57: \"Stable 30 FPS\" means the game logic still runs at 30 Hz and the picture keeps\n58: up. It does not mean 60 FPS interpolation, which is an N3DS-only feature.\n59: \n60: \"Widescreen\" here means the existing wide-layout path, with the 3D view widened\n61: to the screen's aspect and the 2D layers placed for the wider canvas. It does\n62: not mean the memory-heavy full WideArt pack; the tier uses the reduced layout\n63: that fits. \"Native-resolution 3D\" means the upper screen's 400x240, not the\n64: DS's 256x192 upscaled.\n65: \n66: ## 3. Exclusions\n67: \n68: The tier deliberately excludes:\n69: \n70: | Feature | Why it is out |\n71: | --- | --- |\n72: | 60 FPS interpolation (`fps60`) | Doubles the present work and adds 3-9 ms of CPU a scene (more at 268 MHz); the first goal is a stable 30. |\n73: | Stereo 3D (`stereo`) | Doubles the 3D render and the framebuffer; not affordable on O3DS at this scale. |\n74: | Sun shadows (`shadows`) | Extra passes and vertex work; parked on the 3DS upstream anyway (they hang its GPU). |\n75: | Edge marking (`edges`) | Extra passes and buffers; already off by default upstream. |\n76: | xBRZ (`filter3d xbrz`) | CPU-heavy texture upscaling. |\n77: | 2x2 supersampling (`smooth3d`, default on) | Four times the pixels on a GPU that is the same on both models but must carry more of the work on O3DS; the first goal is native resolution. |\n78: | Full WideArt | Memory and bandwidth; the tier may use a reduced wide layout where the scene supports it. |\n79: | High-resolution 2D textures | The atlas is sized to the memory budget, not to the N3DS's. |\n80: \n81: These are not permanent bans. They are the first tier's scope. A later tier\n82: can add one back if it passes its own gate.\n83: \n84: ## 4. Hardware budget\n85: \n86: Public specifications, not measurements of this port `[SPEC]` (coffeepot\n87: `ctr/hardware/cpu.md`, `gpu.md`, `memory.md`):\n88: \n89: | | Old 3DS | New 3DS |\n90: | --- | --- | --- |\n91: | CPU | 2 x ARM11 MPCore, 268 MHz, no L2 | 4 x ARM11 MPCore, 804 MHz with the speed-up, 2 MB L2 |\n92: | GPU | PICA200, 268 MHz | the same |\n93: | FCRAM | 128 MB | 256 MB |\n94: | Memory for the application | about 64 MB | up to about 124 MB |\n95: | VRAM | 6 MB | the same |\n96: | Upper screen | 400x240 (800x240 for stereo) | the same |\n97: | Lower screen | 320x240 | the same |\n98: \n99: An earlier draft of this table gave the Old 3DS a 133 MHz GPU and the New 3DS\n100: 10 MB of VRAM. Both were wrong: the GPU and VRAM are identical, so **every\n101: GPU-side cost measured on a New 3DS is roughly what the Old 3DS pays too**,\n102: while every CPU-side cost is about three times larger there (more without the\n103: L2). That makes the tier's arithmetic simpler: move CPU work to cached or\n104: GPU paths, and do not add GPU work the New 3DS already finds expensive.\n105: \n106: The application does not get all of the CPU or all of the RAM. On Old 3DS\n107: the application gets about 64 MB; `pokeplatinum-3ds` already has a\n108: smaller-display path for that mode (issue #188, where a New 2DS XL in that\n109: mode had about 16.5 MB of linear heap). `[PP]` The planning assumption for\n110: the tier is **about 64 MB of application memory and 6 MB of VRAM**.\n111: \n112: Frame budget at 30 FPS: **33.3 ms**. At 268 MHz, that is about 8.9 million\n113: cycles per core, before the OS and the display thread take their share. `[SPEC]`\n114: The application gets core 0 and a share of core 1 (30% in practice on the\n115: New 3DS, per `main_3ds.c`), not two whole cores.\n116: \n117: ## 5. Memory ledger\n118: \n119: This is a planning ledger, not an allocation plan. Every row must be replaced\n120: by a measured value from `NitroPort_PicaLogMemory` and the `[perf]` logs before\n121: the tier can ship.\n122: \n123: | Item | Planning budget | Source | Gate |\n124: | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n125: | Game code, data, and heap | Existing 64 MB-mode footprint | `[PP]` | Must boot and save |\n126: | Data-pack cache | 4 MB (already the Old 3DS value) | `[PP]` | No SD stalls on route/town changes |\n127: | Compositor textures (both screens) | Existing small-display path | `[PP]` | Both screens filled, no black screen |\n128: | 2D tile atlas | 512 KB at 512x512 RGBA5551; 2 MB at 1024x1024 | `[TARGET]` | Fits with eviction; no fallback storm |\n129: | 2D layer/vertex buffers | 256-512 KB | `[TARGET]` | Bounded per frame |\n130: | Retained 3D geometry | 1-4 MB, evictable | `[TARGET]` | Scene falls back rather than fails |\n131: | 3D texture cache | Existing budget, reduced | `[PP]` | No thrash in the corpus |\n132: | Decoded ADPCM cache | 64-256 KB | `[TARGET]` | No audio dropouts |\n133: | Framebuffers and depth | Existing, no stereo | `[PP]` | Native resolution |\n134: | Reserve and fragmentation | At least 15% of the linear heap | `[TARGET]` | Boot check passes |\n135: \n136: Rules:\n137: \n138: - The tier checks the budget **before** allocating the compositor. If the check\n139:   fails, it logs the reason once and falls back to the classic display.\n140: - A failed allocation must never leave a black screen or a half-initialized\n141:   remaster.\n142: - VRAM is budgeted by bank, not by summing image sizes. Targets, depth, and\n143:   textures share the 6 MB.\n144: - The atlas and retained geometry are evictable. The tier must survive a full\n145:   atlas and a full geometry cache by falling back, not by crashing.\n146: - The 64 MB mode is the floor. Do not let New 3DS headroom hide an O3DS\n147:   failure.\n148: \n149: ## 6. Scene corpus\n150: \n151: The tier is judged on a fixed corpus, not on a demo. At minimum:\n152: \n153: **Boot and menus**\n154: - Boot to title, load a save, open the options page.\n155: - Lower-screen menu, party screen, summary, bag, Pokédex, PC.\n156: - Save, reboot, load.\n157: \n158: **Field**\n159: - Twinleaf Town, Sandgem Town, Jubilife City.\n160: - Route 202, Route 203, Route 206, Route 215.\n161: - Eterna City, Hearthome City, Solaceon Town, Veilstone City.\n162: - Pastoria City, Canalave City, Snowpoint City, Sunyshore City.\n163: - The Distortion World.\n164: - A rainy route and a route with a sandstorm.\n165: \n166: **Battles and effects**\n167: - Singles battle, doubles battle, a battle-start transition.\n168: - A contest.\n169: - The HM cut-in (Strength, Rock Smash, or Surf).\n170: - A flash/fade transition and a weather transition.\n171: \n172: Each scene runs with a fixed input script, a 10-second warm-up, and a\n173: 60-second capture. Three runs per scene. The same script and corpus are used\n174: for every build.\n175: \n176: ## 7. Internal acceptance gates\n177: \n178: These gates are ours. They are not a request to the maintainer.\n179: \n180: ### G0 - Boot and configuration\n181: \n182: - The tier parses from the config and reports its profile in the log.\n183: - With the tier off, the classic display is unchanged, and its frame times\n184:   are no worse than the step 0 baseline.\n185: - With the tier on, both screens initialize; a forced allocation failure falls\n186:   back cleanly.\n187: - No crash on a cold boot, a warm boot, or a reboot after a save.\n188: \n189: ### G1 - Field traversal\n190: \n191: - Every field scene in the corpus loads and is playable for 5 minutes.\n192: - No black screen, no stuck transition, no missing map, no stuck 3D.\n193: - The picture keeps up at 30 Hz; the log shows no more than 10% dropped\n194:   presents in the first tier `[TARGET]`.\n195: \n196: ### G2 - Towns and menus\n197: \n198: - Towns, the lower-screen menu, the party screen, the summary, the bag, the\n199:   Pokédex, and the PC are usable.\n200: - Text is crisp; no missing glyphs; no wrong palette.\n201: - The menu opens and closes without a frame spike that breaks input.\n202: \n203: ### G3 - Battles\n204: \n205: - Singles and doubles run at the target frame rate.\n206: - Move animations, ability popups, and the battle-start transition are\n207:   correct.\n208: - No missing geometry, no wrong depth order, no transparent surface drawn\n209:   opaque.\n210: \n211: ### G4 - Effects and cutscenes\n212: \n213: - Weather, the HM cut-in, flash/fade, and the Distortion World are correct.\n214: - The documented exclusions are the only visual differences: no shadows, no\n215:   edge marking, no stereo, no interpolation.\n216: - No H-blank effect is silently dropped; if a frame falls back, it is correct.\n217: \n218: ### G5 - Audio\n219: \n220: - Music, effects, and sequencing play for 30 minutes without dropouts.\n221: - No clicks on loop points; no drift against the game's timing.\n222: - The decoded-ADPCM cache is bit-exact against the reference.\n223: \n224: ### G6 - Saves\n225: \n226: - 20 save/load cycles across the corpus.\n227: - No corruption, no truncated save, no change to the save format.\n228: - A save written by the tier loads in the classic path and vice versa.\n229: \n230: ### G7 - Memory and soak\n231: \n232: - A 2-hour soak with scene transitions, battles, menus, and audio.\n233: - Memory does not grow beyond the documented reserve; no progressive\n234:   slowdown.\n235: - The atlas and geometry caches evict correctly under pressure.\n236: - No crash on a forced low-memory boot.\n237: \n238: ### G8 - Visual parity\n239: \n240: - For 2D, the tier matches the New 3DS remaster's 2D exactly on the scenes the\n241:   atlas path covers: zero differing client pixels on held frames. A scene that\n242:   falls back to the software path must produce the same picture as the\n243:   remaster's software path.\n244: - For 3D, the tier matches the same scene's geometry and layout, with the\n245:   documented exclusions. Differences are listed and approved, not hand-waved.\n246: \n247: ## 8. Performance targets\n248: \n249: All of these are `[TARGET]`, not measurements. They are the numbers the tier\n250: must beat to ship, and they are deliberately conservative.\n251: \n252: | Metric | Target | Notes |\n253: | --- | --- | --- |\n254: | Field frame time p50 | ≤ 33.3 ms | Stable 30 Hz |\n255: | Field frame time p95 | ≤ 40 ms in the first tier; ≤ 33.3 ms for exit | Tighten only with evidence |\n256: | Dropped presents | ≤ 10% first tier; ≤ 5% for exit | Counted by telemetry |\n257: | Geometry per scene | ≤ 12 ms | After retained geometry and lighting |\n258: | 2D drawer per picture | ≤ 8 ms | After the change check and GPU 2D |\n259: | Mixer core share | ≤ 6% | After the ADPCM cache |\n260: | Boot time | No more than 2 seconds over classic | The budget check is cheap |\n261: | Memory reserve | ≥ 15% of the linear heap | No fragmentation failure |\n262: \n263: If a target is missed, the tier does not ship. The core PRs still do.\n264: \n265: ## 9. Exit criteria\n266: \n267: The tier exits \"experimental\" only when:\n268: \n269: 1. All G0-G8 gates pass on at least one original 3DS or 2DS, in at least one\n270:    region, with the retail game data path.\n271: 2. The performance targets are met on the corpus, not on a single scene.\n272: 3. The tier is default off and documented as opt-in.\n273: 4. The N3DS build's logs and golden frames are unchanged with the tier off.\n274: 5. The PR series' core changes are merged or accepted; the tier does not carry\n275:    an unmerged renderer.\n276: 6. The maintainer has not been asked to test Old 3DS hardware. The evidence\n277:    pack is self-contained.\n278: \n279: ## 10. Drop criteria\n280: \n281: Drop the tier, or leave it downstream, if any of these happen:\n282: \n283: - The field p95 stays above 50 ms after PRs 3-10, with no clear path to 40 ms.\n284: - The tier is not clearly better than today's O3DS `remaster on` and\n285:   `remaster off` baselines; there is no point shipping a profile that loses\n286:   to the classic display.\n287: - The memory ledger cannot fit the 64 MB mode without starving the game.\n288: - The 2D atlas or retained geometry causes a fallback storm in common scenes.\n289: - The tier requires disabling saves, audio, or a core gameplay feature.\n290: - Upstream objects to the profile's presence. The core PRs are independent;\n291:   the tier can live in a downstream branch without blocking them.\n292: \n293: Dropping the tier is a successful outcome for the core series, not a failure\n294: of the plan. The New 3DS wins are the point.\n295: \n296: ## 11. Relationship to upstream\n297: \n298: - The core PRs are proposed one at a time, on New 3DS terms.\n299: - The tier is proposed last, as an opt-in profile. It does not change the\n300:   supported-platform statement.\n301: - If upstream accepts the core and declines the tier, the tier remains a\n302:   downstream patch or a documented build option. The core work is unaffected.\n303: - If upstream declines both, the work is still a coherent downstream series;\n304:   it is not a fork with a divergent renderer.\n305: \n306: ## 12. Open risks\n307: \n308: - **No baseline yet.** None has been collected, but one is cheap: run the\n309:   corpus on an Old 3DS with `remaster off` and with `remaster on` on current\n310:   `main` (PR_SERIES step 0). Until then every number here is a target or a\n311:   `kohjoh` measurement.\n312: - **Core 0 and a share of core 1, not two cores.** The port already has an\n313:   Old 3DS topology; the scheduling work tunes it for the remaster.\n314: - **VRAM is 6 MB, on both models.** The atlas, retained geometry, and 3D\n315:   textures compete for it. The ledger is a hard constraint.\n316: - **The CPU is a third of the speed; the GPU is the same.** A CPU technique\n317:   that is comfortable on N3DS may be marginal on O3DS. Moving work to the GPU\n318:   helps only while the GPU has room, and Azahar will not tell you whether it\n319:   does (`kohjoh`: 36 → 57 ms on hardware while Azahar held 30 FPS). Measure\n320:   on hardware, do not extrapolate.\n321: - **The tier is a support surface.** Even opt-in and experimental, it will\n322:   attract bug reports. The documentation must say what it is and is not."

The\n172: Old 3DS topology also exists already (section 1.1). But the priorities and the\n173: present-skip rules are tuned around the current costs. This is why `perf/lowend-schedule` exists, and why it comes after the\n177: costs are removed rather than before.\n178: \n179: ## 2. What kohjoh measured\n180: \n181: `kohjoh` is an HGSS port to the Old 3DS. It solved the same class of problems:\n182: DS-era software rendering on PICA200 hardware, with a CPU about a third as\n183: fast as an unlocked New 3DS's and the same GPU. Its techniques transfer; its\n184: game code does not.\n185: \n186: ### 2.1 Retained 2D and the tile atlas\n187: \n188: `kohjoh`'s 2D renderer translates one engine's per-scanline state into ordered\n189: GPU passes:\n190: \n191: - window regions become stencil bits;\n192: - BGs and OBJs are drawn in priority order;\n193: - alpha blending is two draws (blended where the second-target bit is set,\n194:   opaque where not);\n195: - brightness is a pass over target-1 pixels, then a master-brightness pass.\n196: \n197: Crucially, when a frame has no per-line register changes, each text BG and the\n198: OBJ layer keep last frame's quads. The cache is exact: it compares the layer's\n199: palette and the tile bytes it used, with no write tracking and no hashing of\n200: the whole VRAM. `[KJ]`, `src/graphics/g2d/g2d.c`\n201: \n202: The tile atlas is **1024x1024 RGBA5551**, built from 8x8 DS tiles in Morton\n203: order (which is PICA's native tiling). Cache identity is content plus effective\n204: palette, mode, and mapping. Palette changes invalidate dependent tiles, not the\n205: whole atlas. `[KJ]`, `src/graphics/resources/atlas.c`\n206: \n207: `kohjoh`'s local Coffeepot tile benchmark, on Old 3DS, for a 416-tile synthetic\n208: setup: direct citro2d 1.497 ms, manual vertices 1.019 ms, retained chunks\n209: 0.899 ms, cached surface 0.868 ms. `[KJ]`, approximate local benchmark, not a\n210: `pokeplatinum` scene. Cached surfaces also cost extra VRAM and produce redraw\n211: spikes, which is why the proposed baseline is retained chunks plus dynamic\n212: tiles, with surfaces only for static content.\n213: \n214: ### 2.2 Retained 3D, the matrix palette, and lighting\n215: \n216: `kohjoh` retains G3 display lists as object-space geometry and transforms them\n217: on the PICA vertex unit with a **16-entry matrix palette**. The vertex shader\n218: reads a matrix index from the packed vertex and does four `dp4`s against\n219: `palette[64]` (16 matrices x 4 rows). `[KJ]`,\n220: `src/graphics/pica/shaders/g3d.v.pica`\n221: \n222: The display-list cache replays **74% of FIFO words** (`[KJ]`,\n223: `docs/worklog/2026-11-12.md`). On Azahar, the hotpaths A/B (display-list\n224: cache, state-only replay, compact hot loops) cut game logic p50 from\n225: **16.648 ms to 15.430 ms (-7.3%)**. `[KJ]`,\n226: `docs/worklog/2026-11-14-hotpaths.md`. The worklog explicitly warns that the\n227: replay-rate increase includes state-only streams and must not be presented as a\n228: retained geometry hit-rate gain.\n229: \n230: The lighting shader reproduces the DS's fixed-point lighting semantics in\n231: PICA vertex code: **409 instructions, 94 float registers including constants**\n232: (the lit-plans worklog's count, before the later light-skip flags).\n233: On held frames it is pixel-exact against the CPU reference: Ho-Oh frames\n234: 2301/2501 match across the complete dual-screen client crop (801x960 screenshot\n235: pixels), and the Route 34 field matches with zero differing client pixels.\n236: `[KJ]`, `docs/worklog/2026-11-15-lit-plans.md`\n237: \n238: This proves a DS-exact lighting model is achievable on PICA without visible\n239: drift. It does **not** prove that lighting on the PICA is faster, and\n240: `kohjoh`'s own hardware run says it often is not:\n241: \n242: - Sending every list with a NORMAL down the per-vertex PICA-lit path, static\n243:   map scenery included, took Old 3DS captured frames in Goldenrod from about\n244:   **36 ms to 57 ms**. Azahar stayed at 30 FPS throughout, because it does not\n245:   charge for vertex shader work. `[KJ]`, O3DS log,\n246:   `docs/worklog/2026-11-15-hardware-cuts.md`\n247: - The fix (`84d46dc`) **bakes stable lit lists once with exact CPU lighting**\n248:   and replays them as literal-colour blocks through the unlit shader. Only\n249:   lists whose lighting key misses on consecutive calls stay PICA-lit. Azahar\n250:   logic p50 fell from 25.35 to 14.06 ms, with held frames pixel-identical.\n251:   `[KJ]`\n252: - The lit shader now skips disabled lights and lights with no specular\n253:   colour: **101 instructions per one-light vertex instead of 409**\n254:   (`eeb4b37`). Its flags live in the unused `.w` of float uniforms, because\n255:   PICA bool uniforms read false in Azahar. The float uniform file is full: the\n256:   worklog counts \"91 float uniforms plus 7 constants of the 96\", so there is\n257:   no room for a separate flags array. `[KJ]`\n258: - Culling retained blocks wholly outside the clip volume's side planes before\n259:   copying them (`413d0cc`) cut triangles from 5.02M to 1.94M and draws from\n260:   80.3k to 61.7k over 600 frames. `[KJ]`\n261: \n262: So the transferable lesson is: **retain and cache on the CPU first; light on\n263: the PICA only what cannot be baked; count GPU work, not Azahar time.** Fitting\n264: `pokeplatinum-3ds`'s material set is still the census's question.\n265: \n266: ### 2.3 Decoded ADPCM\n267: \n268: `kohjoh` added a decoded-sample cache for voices whose decoder state came from\n269: the data alone (`adpcmClean`). On Azahar, Goldenrod:\n270: \n271: | Build | Ticks per channel-sample | Mixer core share |\n272: | --- | --- | --- |\n273: | Measurement only | 107.6 | 14.8% |\n274: | Decoded-ADPCM cache | 48.0 | 6.6% |\n275: \n276: `[KJ]`, `docs/worklog/2026-11-15-audio.md`. The cache halved the mixer's\n277: instruction count and cut its core share by more than half. A later kernel\n278: flush of wave buffers kept the same numbers.\n279: \n280: `pokeplatinum-3ds` already block-mixes, so the expected win is smaller in\n281: absolute terms, but the decode itself is the same shape of work. `[PP]`/`[KJ]`\n282: \n283: ### 2.4 The Old 3DS reality check\n284: \n285: `kohjoh` is not a blanket 30 FPS guarantee on Old 3DS:\n286: \n287: - At its first profiled O3DS run (2026-11-12), Route 34 was near 30 FPS and\n288:   Goldenrod unplayable; field logic was about 37 ms before the decoder fast\n289:   paths. `[KJ]`, O3DS log, `docs/worklog/2026-11-12.md`\n290: - Goldenrod captured frames later measured about 36 ms, then 57 ms after the\n291:   PICA-lighting change above, before the hardware cuts. `[KJ]`, O3DS log.\n292:   O3DS ran about 2.3x slower than Azahar for logic and publish. A post-cut\n293:   O3DS number is not yet in the worklog.\n294: \n295: This is exactly why the O3DS tier is a stretch goal with its own gates, not a\n296: promise inherited from `kohjoh`. A technique that works does not automatically\n297: produce a playable frame on weaker hardware.\n298: \n299: ## 3. Transfer matrix\n300: \n301: | kohjoh technique | `pokeplatinum-3ds` cost addressed | Expected New 3DS effect | Confidence | First proof |\n302: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n303: | Dirty-generation 2D change check (ours; `kohjoh` compares used tiles instead) | The residual shown-VRAM hash and the H-blank/bitmap full read, size unknown | Unknown until step 0; possibly small after `313ac80` | Low until measured | `perf/render2d-change`: differential fuzz + drawer timing |\n304: | Retained text-BG layers | Re-rasterizing unchanged BGs every frame | Lower drawer time in towns, menus, battles | High | `perf/g2d-atlas-text`: golden frames + timing |\n305: | Tile atlas (512-1024) + palette dependencies | Software tile decode and CPU-to-GPU copy | Fewer bytes moved, fewer draws; foundation for all GPU 2D | High for text, medium for affine/extended | `perf/g2d-atlas-text`, `perf/g2d-layers` |\n306: | Stencil windows + blend/brightness passes | Software windows, blending, brightness, H-blank spans | Full GPU 2D coverage without per-span CPU work | Medium | `perf/g2d-effects`: effect corpus |\n307: | Retained object-space G3 + 16-entry matrix palette + clip-volume cull | 20-30 ms CPU transform/clip per scene, plus 3-9 ms of in-between scenes | Target 8-12 ms geometry per scene `[TARGET]`, only if it also covers `fps60` | Medium | `perf/g3d-retained`: replay A/B + timing + GPU work counts |\n308: | Baked lighting for stable lists; PICA lighting for the rest | Per-vertex CPU lighting | More geometry time returned without new GPU load for static scenery | Medium | `perf/g3d-lighting`: lit-frame pixel compare + GPU work counts |\n309: | Decoded-ADPCM cache | Per-sample decode of looping instruments | Lower mixer CPU; core time back to the game | High | `perf/audio-adpcm`: bit-exact output + tick count |\n310: | Display-list cache / state replay | Repeated G3 decode and submission | Lower logic time in worst-case scenes | Medium | `perf/g3d-fifo` (optional) |\n311: | Present pacing and priorities | Over-eager skip or drawer starvation | More stable frame times once costs drop | Medium | `perf/lowend-schedule`: p95/p99 histograms |\n312: \n313: The matrix follows the 2D, 3D, audio, scheduling grouping, not PR order or\n314: confidence. PR order is chosen so each step makes the next one measurable.\n315: \n316: ## 4. What does not transfer\n317: \n318: - **HGSS game logic, maps, scripts, and assets.** None of it is relevant, and\n319:   none of it may be copied. `kohjoh` is GPL-3.0, like `pokeplatinum-3ds`, but\n320:   game content is never part of the adaptation.\n321: - **`kohjoh`'s citro2d compositor.** `pokeplatinum-3ds` has its own compositor\n322:   and its own PICA command submission. The 2D *technique* transfers; the API\n323:   calls do not.\n324: - **Old 3DS cycle numbers.** `kohjoh`'s Azahar ticks are instruction counts on\n325:   an emulator. They rank changes; they do not predict milliseconds.\n326: - **The assumption that PICA lighting fits every material, or is cheaper.**\n327:   `kohjoh`'s shader is 409 instructions worst case and its float uniform file\n328:   is full (section 2.2). `pokeplatinum-3ds` has more material\n329:   modes, N3DS-only effects, and a different texture pipeline. The census\n330:   decides what fits; GPU work counts decide whether it pays.\n331: - **Azahar as a GPU judge.** It does not charge for vertex work. GPU-side\n332:   changes are judged by vertices, shader instructions per vertex, triangles,\n333:   and draws, and on hardware.\n334: - **Stereo 3D, sun shadows, edge marking, xBRZ, 2x2 supersampling, and full\n335:   WideArt.** These are New 3DS features. They stay on the existing path and\n336:   are never folded into the shared low-end backend. 60 FPS interpolation is\n337:   different: it is on by default on New 3DS, so the shared geometry backend\n338:   has to support it (section 1.4) or it does not help the default\n339:   configuration.\n340: - **A blanket Old 3DS 30 FPS promise.** See section 2.4.\n341: \n342: ## 5. Evidence we can produce without the maintainer\n343: \n344: The maintainer does not need to run benchmarks. The evidence pack has to stand\n345: on its own.\n346: \n347: ### 5.1 Correctness\n348: \n349: - Deterministic host tests: `make test`, plus the host32 suites\n350:   (`make -C 3ds_port/nitro TARGET=host32 test`,\n351:   `make -C 3ds_port/game TARGET=host32 test`). The suites already include\n352:   `test_render`, `test_gx3d`, `test_gx3d_plumbing`, `test_sound_chip`,\n353:   `test_threads`, `test_speed`, and the VRAM/upscale/shadow/lower-menu/options\n354:   suites.\n355: - Golden-frame comparisons: render a fixed scene through the old and new paths\n356:   and compare client pixels. `kohjoh`'s 801x960 dual-screen comparison is the\n357:   model.\n358: - Differential fuzzing for cache invalidation: random writes to VRAM, OAM,\n359:   palettes, and tilemaps; compare the fast change check against the full hash.\n360:   Any disagreement is a failure, not a tolerance.\n361: - Replay: `gx3d_replay FILE` already exists for captured G3 streams. Use it to\n362:   compare CPU and retained paths on the same input.\n363: - GPU stand-in: `port_gx3d_gpusim.c` already draws a scene the way\n364:   `port_gx3d_pica.c` asks the PICA to (same batches, tiled textures, combiner,\n365:   alpha, blend, and depth rules) on a PC. A retained or lit path that is\n366:   mirrored there can be compared against the CPU path in the host suite,\n367:   without hardware. It does not model PICA rasterization exactly, so edge\n368:   pixels need a stated tolerance; held-frame equality stays a hardware check.\n369: - Soak: 30+ minute runs with scene transitions, battles, menus, and saves.\n370: \n371: ### 5.2 Performance\n372: \n373: - `[perf]` logs from our own New 3DS and Old 3DS runs: drawer time, handover\n374:   time, geometry time, mixer time, skip counts, and tail frame times. The New\n375:   3DS runs must confirm the 804 MHz speed-up was accepted (the `[perf] New 3DS\n376:   speed-up` line); a log without it is a compatibility-mode log.\n377: - Azahar instruction counts for A/B builds on the same scene and input script.\n378:   These are CPU comparisons, not absolute predictions, and say nothing about\n379:   GPU cost.\n380: - GPU work counts for any change that moves work to the PICA: vertices,\n381:   shader instructions per vertex, triangles, draws, and texture upload bytes\n382:   per frame.\n383: - Histograms, not averages: p50, p95, p99, missed V-blanks, and the number of\n384:   scenes left out.\n385: - A fixed scene corpus and a fixed input script, so before/after numbers are\n386:   comparable.\n387: \n388: ### 5.3 What we cannot claim\n389: \n390: - We cannot claim an Old 3DS frame rate from Azahar ticks.\n391: - We cannot claim a New 3DS win without a New 3DS log or a deterministic\n392:   counter that the project already trusts.\n393: - We cannot ask the maintainer to validate performance on hardware they do not\n394:   target. (They do test performance-sensitive work on a New 3DS themselves:\n395:   `AI_DISCLOSURE.md`. The evidence pack should make that check quick and\n396:   reproducible, not replace it.)\n397: - We cannot treat \"it looks faster\" as a gate.\n398: \n399: ## 6. Measurement protocol\n400: \n401: Every performance PR uses the same protocol:\n402: \n403: 0. **Baseline on current `main`.** Before the first PR, and again before each\n404:    PR is opened, run the corpus on current upstream `main` on a New 3DS (speed-up\n405:    on), an Old 3DS with `remaster off` (today's O3DS experience), and an Old\n406:    3DS with `remaster on` (today's O3DS remaster, which is not blocked, only\n407:    unsupported). These three logs replace every stale `[PP]` number and give\n408:    the O3DS tier the baseline it currently lacks.\n409: 1. **Scene corpus.** At minimum: title, Twinleaf, Sandgem, Jubilife, Route 202,\n410:    Route 203, Route 206, Eterna, Hearthome, Solaceon, Veilstone, Pastoria, the\n411:    Distortion World, a singles battle, a doubles battle, a contest, the summary\n412:    screen, the PC, and the lower-screen menu.\n413: 2. **Input script.** Fixed movement and menu path per scene; no random walks.\n414:    The same script runs on both builds.\n415: 3. **Warm-up.** 10 seconds discarded, then 60 seconds captured, three runs.\n416: 4. **Counter set.** Frame time p50/p95/p99, drawer time by part (change check,\n417:    draw, handover), geometry time by part (decode, transform, light, clip,\n418:    submit), mixer ticks, skipped presents, missed deadlines.\n419: 5. **Noise floor.** A change is kept only if its median improves by more than\n420:    the run-to-run spread of the measurement, and its p95 does not regress.\n421: 6. **Reporting.** The PR includes the raw log lines, the scene, the build, and\n422:    the hardware. No cherry-picked single frame.\n423: \n424: If a change cannot clear the noise floor, it is reverted. Elegance is not a\n425: gate.\n426: \n427: ## 7. Gaps and open questions\n428: \n429: - **No `pokeplatinum-3ds` Old 3DS baseline has been collected yet.** One is\n430:   cheap: the port boots on Old 3DS today (step 0 above). Until then, any O3DS\n431:   number in these documents is a `[TARGET]` or a `[KJ]` measurement.\n432: - **The N3DS linear-memory floor is tight.** Before the place-name sign's\n433:   textures (2026-11-04), New 3DS logs had about 4.2 MB (4253 KB) of linear\n434:   memory left after the title screen and 2.5 MB (2571 KB) at the fewest\n435:   through a run; after them, 4069 KB. Below `COMPOSE_TEXTURE_ROOM` (now 3 MB)\n436:   the compositor already takes its smaller display. `[PP]` A 1024x1024\n437:   RGBA5551 atlas is 2 MB. Atlas sizing, eviction, and residency are a\n438:   first-class design constraint.\n439: - **The 64 MB memory mode is a New 3DS case too.** Issue #188: a New 2DS XL\n440:   launched in the 64 MB mode had about 16.5 MB of linear heap and fell back to\n441:   the classic display. `[PP]` Memory the shared backends save helps New 3DS\n442:   users in that mode, which is an N3DS merge case for memory work that does not\n443:   depend on the O3DS tier.\n444: - **VRAM is 6 MB on both models.** `[SPEC]`, coffeepot `ctr/hardware/gpu.md`.\n445:   (An earlier draft said the New 3DS has more; its extra memory is FCRAM, not\n446:   VRAM.) For GPU-side changes, add GPU work counts; Azahar does not\n97:   charge for vertex work.\n98: - **How to check it yourself:** the `remaster.txt` line, the scene, and the\n99:   `[perf]` line to compare, so the maintainer's own New 3DS check takes\n100:   minutes.\n101: - **Risks:** what could regress and how the fallback works.\n102: - **Rollback:** the `remaster.txt` line or compile-time switch.\n103: \n104: Rules for evidence:\n105: \n106: - No game content in the PR. No ROMs, saves, captured assets, or screenshots of\n107:   game footage. The repository's rules are strict about game content, and a PR\n108:   that attaches game imagery risks being closed for that alone.\n109: - Use synthetic fixtures, numeric pixel diffs, and logs. If a visual is\n110:   genuinely needed, describe the scene and let the reviewer reproduce it with\n111:   their own data.\n112: - Do not ask the maintainer to benchmark. They will test in Azahar and, for\n113:   performance work, on a New 3DS anyway; make that quick.\n114: - Do not present an emulator instruction count as a hardware frame time.\n115: - Do not lean on an Old 3DS number to justify a core PR. A core PR's merge\n116:   case is the New 3DS. PR 10's Old 3DS tuning is an optional sub-feature, not\n117:   the reason for the PR.\n118: \n119: ## 5. CI and tests\n120: \n121: The project's CI builds the 3DS code and runs the Python tools. A red build\n122: does not merge. `CONTRIBUTING.md` also asks for an Azahar test when possible.\n123: \n124: Every PR should:\n125: \n126: - pass `make test` for the host build, and the host32 suites\n127:   (`make -C 3ds_port/nitro TARGET=host32 test`,\n128:   `make -C 3ds_port/game TARGET=host32 test`);\n129: - pass `make game` for the 3DS build;\n130: - add host tests for new logic, not hardware-dependent tests;\n131: - keep the existing suites green: `test_render`, `test_gx3d`,\n132:   `test_gx3d_plumbing`, `test_sound_chip`, `test_threads`, `test_speed`, and\n133:   the VRAM/upscale/shadow/lower-menu/options suites;\n134: - not add CI that publishes a build containing game code. The artifact\n135:   allow-list in `tools/check_ci_artifacts.py` is not a place to broaden.\n136: \n137: If a test needs a captured G3 stream, use the existing `gx3d_replay` harness\n138: and a small synthetic fixture, not a game capture.\n139: \n140: ## 6. AI disclosure\n141: \n142: Follow `AI_DISCLOSURE.md` exactly:\n143: \n144: - AI-assisted changes arrive as pull requests, never as direct pushes to\n145:   `main`.\n146: - Commits carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude`.\n147: - The PR description says what the AI did and what was verified by a human.\n148: - Every change is built by CI and tested by a human before merge.\n149: - AI is never used to generate, recreate, or \"clean up\" game assets.\n150: - No code from leaked sources and no code from ports that bundle game assets.\n151: \n152: A short disclosure paragraph in the PR is enough:\n153: \n154: > This change was developed with Claude, which helped with the design and wrote\n155: > parts of the code and tests. A human reviewed the change and ran the tests.\n156: > Commits carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude`. No game assets were generated or\n157: > copied.\n158: \n159: Do not over-explain or apologize for AI assistance. The project already has a\n160: policy; follow it.\n161: \n162: One line of that policy needs an answer before any code: under \"What the AI\n163: is not used for\" it says \"all new features are created by the developer\". A\n164: performance backend is arguably a feature. Ask in the opening issue (section\n165: 2) rather than guess; if the answer is no, the plan becomes a design write-up\n166: the maintainer can implement, or a downstream branch.\n167: \n168: ## 7. GPL provenance\n169: \n170: `pokeplatinum-3ds` and `kohjoh` are both GPL-3.0. Adapting a technique or a\n171: small piece of code is compatible, but it needs provenance:\n172: \n173: - State the source repository and the commit or file in the commit message.\n174: - Keep the GPL notice and the original copyright notice in any file that\n175:   contains adapted code.\n176: - Add a file-header note: \"Adapted from kohjoh (GPL-3.0), <commit>, for\n177:   pokeplatinum-3ds; modified for <reason>.\"\n178: - If the adaptation is substantial, add the attribution to `NOTICE.md` as well\n179:   as the file header.\n180: - Do not copy game data, textures, models, scripts, or captured streams from\n181:   either project.\n182: - Do not copy code from leaked sources or from ports that bundle the game's\n183:   assets. `kohjoh` is GPL-3.0, but its license does not make HGSS assets\n184:   usable.\n185: \n186: When in doubt, describe the technique in the PR and write the implementation\n187: against `pokeplatinum`'s own data structures. A described technique is not a\n188: copyright problem; a copied file without attribution is.\n189: \n190: ## 8. Review strategy\n191: \n192: ### Before the first PR\n193: \n194: - Collect the step 0 baseline on current `main` first.\n195: - Open one short issue or discussion with the measured costs and the proposed\n196:   first two steps. Do not paste the whole plan.\n197: - Ask for the maintainer's preferred direction. If they want a different\n198:   order, reorder.\n199: - Ask the two policy questions in section 2.\n200: \n201: ### The first two PRs\n202: \n203: - `perf/telemetry`: small, no behavior change, easy to review. It adds\n204:   percentiles and mixer timing to the existing `[perf]` vocabulary rather\n205:   than inventing a new one.\n206: - `perf/audio-adpcm`: bit-exact, renderer-independent, testable on a PC, on\n207:   the game's core. It should be the first merge candidate.\n208: \n209: Do not open the XL renderer PRs until these two are understood, and do not\n210: open `perf/render2d-change` at all unless the baseline shows the residual\n211: check matters.\n212: \n213: ### The XL PRs\n214: \n215: - Ask for design feedback before writing the full implementation. A short\n216:   design comment with the integration points and the fallback strategy is\n217:   cheaper than a rejected 3,000-line PR.\n218: - Split by cost when possible: affine BGs vs sprites, retained geometry vs\n219:   lighting, windows vs blending.\n220: - Keep the fallback path visible in the diff; it is the reviewer's assurance\n221:   that the old behavior is safe.\n222: - If a PR stalls, reduce scope rather than adding features to justify it.\n223: \n224: ### Handling pushback\n225: \n226: - **\"We don't support O3DS.\"** Agree. The core PRs are N3DS performance work;\n227:   the tier is an optional last step and does not change support policy.\n228: - **\"I can't benchmark this.\"** You are not asking them to. Point to the\n229:   deterministic test and the self-produced log.\n230: - **\"This is a huge renderer rewrite.\"** It is not; it extends the existing\n231:   compositor and keeps the old path. Show the integration points and the\n232:   fallback.\n233: - **\"Why not use citro2d?\"** The project already has a PICA compositor and a\n234:   working 2D path. The plan extends it rather than adding a second renderer.\n235: - **\"The numbers are from an emulator.\"** Correct. They are instruction-count\n236:   comparisons, not frame-time claims. The hardware claims come from our own\n237:   logs and are labelled.\n238: - **\"The GPU is already busy on New 3DS.\"** Agree; that is why GPU-side PRs\n239:   report GPU work counts, bake on the CPU where possible, and gate on the\n240:   `[perf] display` rate with `smooth3d` and stereo at their defaults.\n241: - **\"This breaks 60 FPS / sun shadows.\"** The retained path must support\n242:   `fps60` (its merge case depends on it) and leaves sun shadows on the\n243:   existing path.\n244: \n245: ## 9. Otherwise\n295: state \"No third-party code.\">\n296: ```\n297: \n298: ## 10. What not to do\n299: \n300: - Do not open a single \"O3DS support\" PR. Nothing is ever stretched or mirrored to fill the extra space. |\r\n62: | **A menu on the bottom screen** | In the field, the bottom screen is a menu beside the Pokétch: MAP, POKéMON, BAG, TRAINER, POKéDEX, POKéTCH, SAVE and OPTIONS, a tap away (or X and the D-pad). Two squares hold your registered items: tap one to use it. |\r\n63: | **Sharper 3D** | The overworld and battles are drawn by the 3DS's GPU at the screen's own resolution with smooth (anti-aliased) edges, the game's fog, and a wider view of the world at the sides. The DS's outlines round the 3D are off by default; `edges on` in `remaster.txt` draws them. |\r\n64: | **PIXEL PERFECT** | The overworld at the DS's own pixel size across the whole upper screen, with the people moving smoothly over the ground. |\r\n65: | **The wider view filled in** | Past the edges of the maps, the trees, cliffs, rivers and coasts carry on instead of black, never mirrored (on most routes and towns; still a work in progress). |\r\n66: | **60 frames a second** | The game runs its field at 30; the port draws a frame in between each pair, for a steady 60 in towns, on routes, in the rain and in the HM animations, and drops back to 30 where the GPU can't keep up (still being tuned). |\r\n67: | **Enhancements and cheats** | Optional, from OPTIONS: SPEED up to 4x (menus and battle choices stay at 1x), Exp. Share for the whole party, experience for catches, trade evolutions at level 40, HMs without teaching the moves, auto-run, your first Pokémon following you (FOLLOWER: HeartGold/SoulSilver's sprites, downloaded by the builder; it comes out of the ball it was caught in, and you can talk to it: it reacts, and now and then finds you an item); and cheats (always catch, instant victory, fast eggs, infinite money, wild encounter rate, shiny odds, give items). |\r\n68: | **Small conveniences** | Catch a Pokémon with a full party and you can swap it for one in your party right there in the battle. A new game saves over the old save without erasing it first. L + R + START + SELECT restarts the game from the opening. |\r\n69: | **Crisp pixels** | Even, crisp pixels for the 2D, and optional xBRZ smoothing for the 3D's textures. |\r\n70: | **On the HOME Menu** | Installs as a `.cia`, with your cartridge's icon and an animated 3D banner. It opens the `.3dsx`, so updating the game updates it too. |\r\n71: | **Built from your own cartridge** | The builder makes the game's data on your own computer, from your own dump. No game content is distributed. |\r\n72: \r\n73: ## Status\r\n74: \r\n75: | ✅ Works | 🛠️ Work in progress | 💭 Future wishlist |\r\n76: | :--- | :--- | :--- |\r\n77: | Playable on real hardware, from a new game or a save: exploring, battles, menus, the Underground and saving (it still has some visual and gameplay bugs) | Polishing the bottom screen's UI (the learn-a-move screen) | Wi-Fi |\r\n78: | A new UI for the top screen: menus, text boxes and battles across its full width | Filling the wider view past the maps' edges | Better lighting |\r\n79: | A new UI for the bottom screen: a menu beside the Pokétch, with the bag, party, summary, trainer card, save, options and Town Map in its panel | Better 3D quality | 60 FPS Battles |\r\n80: | Enhancements and cheats from the options (SPEED, Exp. Share for the party, and more) | | Pixel Perfect Battles |\r\n81: | A Pokémon that follows you (FOLLOWER) | | Stereoscopic 3D |\r\n82: | 60 frames a second in the field, and the Pixel Perfect overworld | | |\r\n83: | The New 3DS XL's resolution: both screens filled, the 3D drawn at the screen's resolution | | |\r\n84: | Updated animations for the intro, and new animations for some of the UI | | |\r\n85: \r\n86: \r\n87: > [!IMPORTANT]\r\n88: > **This repository contains no game content.** No ROM, graphics, music,\r\n89: > text or any other data from the game is stored here or in the releases. The\r\n90: > releases carry the port's program; the game's data is made from **your own\r\n91: > cartridge**, on your computer or in your browser, and never leaves it.\r\n92: > Don't share the files you make: they hold your cartridge's data.\r\n93: \r\n94: ## Getting started\r\n95: \r\n96: ### What you need\r\n97: \r\n98: - A **3DS family console** with custom firmware (Luma3DS) and the Homebrew\r\n99:   Launcher (and **FBI** for the HOME Menu version). A New 3DS, New 3DS XL or\r\n100:   New 2DS XL is needed for the remastered display. Setup guide:\r\n101:   <https://3ds.hacks.guide>\r\n102: - Your own dump of **Pokémon Platinum (USA)**, Rev 0 or Rev 1.\r\n103: - A computer with an up-to-date browser. Only to build it yourself:\r\n104:   [devkitPro](https://devkitpro.org/wiki/Getting_Started) with the `3ds-dev`\r\n105:   package group, Python 3.10+ and Git.\r\n106: - Optional: the [Azahar](https://azahar-emu.org) emulator for testing on a PC.\r\n107:   It runs the 3DS's CPU slower than a real New 3DS, so judge performance on\r\n108:   the console.\r\n109: \r\n110: ### 1. Make the game's files\r\n111: \r\n112: **The easy way: [the web builder](https://gabesud0.github.io/pokeplatinum-3ds/).** Choose your ROM, press\r\n113: **Build**, and download a ZIP with every file below, laid out for the SD card.\r\n114: It all happens in your browser: your ROM is never uploaded. It also makes the\r\n115: HOME Menu version, with an animated banner made from your cartridge.\r\n116: \r\n117: **Or build it yourself**, from the source:\r\n118: \r\n119: <details>\r\n120: <summary><strong>Windows</strong></summary>\r\n121: \r\n122: <br>\r\n123: \r\n124: Download [`tools/build_windows_msys2.sh`](tools/build_windows_msys2.sh) and\r\n125: run it in devkitPro's MSYS2 terminal (Start menu → devkitPro → MSYS2). It\r\n126: does everything: installs what the build needs besides devkitPro, clones this\r\n127: repository, builds the game (both versions), makes your data pack, and puts\r\n128: the SD card files in `%USERPROFILE%\\pokeplatinum-sd` (and in Azahar's SD\r\n129: folder, if it finds it):\r\n130: \r\n131: ```sh\r\n132: bash build_windows_msys2.sh 'C:\\path\\to\\your\\platinum.nds'\r\n133: ```\r\n134: \r\n135: </details>\r\n136: \r\n137: <details>\r\n138: <summary><strong>Linux</strong> (including Bazzite and SteamOS-like systems)</summary>\r\n139: \r\n140: <br>\r\n141: \r\n142: Download [`tools/build_linux.sh`](tools/build_linux.sh) into your home folder\r\n143: and run it. Like the Windows script, it does everything: installs devkitPro\r\n144: and the rest of what the build needs, clones this repository, builds the game\r\n145: (both versions), makes your data pack, and puts the SD card files in\r\n146: `~/pokeplatinum-sd` (and in Azahar's SD folder, if it finds it):\r\n147: \r\n148: ```sh\r\n149: bash ~/build_linux.sh ~/path/to/your/platinum.nds\r\n150: ```\r\n151: \r\n152: On **Bazzite** and other immutable systems (Fedora Silverblue, Kinoite,\r\n153: Aurora, Bluefin...), it works inside a distrobox it creates once\r\n154: (`pokeplatinum-3ds`, from devkitPro's own image, the one CI builds with), so\r\n155: your system isn't changed; keep the ROM in your home folder. On **Ubuntu or\r\n156: Debian** it runs directly. Run it again to update and rebuild.\r\n157: \r\n158: </details>\r\n159: \r\n160: <details>\r\n161: <summary><strong>By hand</strong> (Linux or macOS)</summary>\r\n162: \r\n163: <br>\r\n164: \r\n165: 1. **Fetch the decompilation and SDKs and build the game:**\r\n166: \r\n167:    ```sh\r\n168:    python tools/bootstrap.py\r\n169:    make game                                   # -> 3ds_port/game/build/3ds/pokeplatinum.3dsx\r\n170:    make game-cia ROM=/path/to/platinum.nds     # -> .../pokeplatinum.cia (HOME Menu version)\r\n171:    ```\r\n172: \r\n173: 2. **Make your data pack** from your own dump\r\n174:    ([`builder/`](builder/README.md)):\r\n175: \r\n176:    ```sh\r\n177:    python builder/verify_rom.py /path/to/platinum.nds    # checks it's a supported dump\r\n178:    python builder/extract_rom.py /path/to/platinum.nds   # -> data_pack/\r\n179:    python builder/pack.py data_pack/                     # -> platinum3ds.pak\r\n180:    ```\r\n181: \r\n182: </details>\r\n183: \r\n184: ### 2. Copy to the SD card\r\n185: \r\n186: The web builder's ZIP has these in its `3ds` and `cia` folders: copy both to\r\n187: the root of the SD card.\r\n188: \r\n189: ```\r\n190: sdmc:/3ds/pokeplatinum/platinum3ds.pak\r\n191: sdmc:/3ds/pokeplatinum/manifest.json      (from data_pack/)\r\n192: sdmc:/3ds/pokeplatinum.3dsx               (for the Homebrew Launcher)\r\n193: sdmc:/cia/pokeplatinum.cia                (for the HOME Menu, optional: it opens the .3dsx)\r\n194: ```\r\n195: \r\n196: In Azahar, these go in its emulated SD card folder.\r\n197: \r\n198: ### 3. Play\r\n199: \r\n200: - **Homebrew Launcher:** run `pokeplatinum.3dsx`, or open it in Azahar.\r\n201: - **HOME Menu:** in FBI, go to **SD → cia → pokeplatinum.cia → Install CIA**.\r\n202:   It opens `sdmc:/3ds/pokeplatinum.3dsx` the way the Homebrew Launcher does\r\n203:   (it needs Luma3DS and the Homebrew Launcher Loader, both from the hacking\r\n204:   guide's setup), so keep the `.3dsx` there: updating it updates the HOME\r\n205:   Menu version too. It closes from the HOME Menu like any other title.\r\n206: - **Updating:** build the new version with the web builder and copy its files\r\n207:   over the old ones. When a version reads its data the same way, its page\r\n208:   says so: then copying the new `pokeplatinum.3dsx` is enough. Coming from\r\n209:   the first alpha (v0.1.0-alpha.1), replace all three: the `.pak`, the\r\n210:   `.3dsx`, and install the new `.cia` once (from then on it opens the\r\n211:   `.3dsx`).\r\n212: \r\n213: The game saves to `sdmc:/3ds/pokeplatinum/platinum.sav`, a raw 512 KB save\r\n214: like emulators keep, so you can copy your cartridge's save there.\r\n215: \r\n216: ### While playing\r\n217: \r\n218: Every button is the game's; in the field, the bottom screen is a menu you can\r\n219: tap. L + R + START + SELECT (the game's own soft reset) restarts the game\r\n220: from the opening. The port writes a log to\r\n221: `sdmc:/3ds/pokeplatinum/log.txt` (send it along when you report a\r\n222: problem; the session before's is kept as `log_prev.txt`, for when the game's\r\n223: been started again since); it comes up on screen by itself if something goes\r\n224: wrong.\r\n225: \r\n226: The game's options, 60 FPS, smooth 3D, and the enhancements and cheats are\r\n227: on the bottom screen's **OPTIONS** page; the port keeps its own in\r\n228: `sdmc:/3ds/pokeplatinum/options.txt`, beside the save. The display has more\r\n229: settings in `sdmc:/3ds/pokeplatinum/remaster.txt`; the defaults are what most\r\n230: people want. See [`docs/REMASTER.md`](docs/REMASTER.md).\r\n231: \r\n232: Where the port's own layout for the wider screen doesn't look right, you can\r\n233: draw the bands yourself with the **WideArt** editor (the pictures drawn so far,\r\n234: like the evolution's background, are built into the game): see\r\n235: [`docs/WIDE_ART.md`](docs/WIDE_ART.md).\r\n236: \r\n237: > [!TIP]\r\n238: > **Need help?** Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/YjyA5ygpC) or open an\r\n239: > issue, and include your console or emulator, your ROM's revision and\r\n240: > `log.txt`.\r\n241: \r\n242: ## For developers\r\n243: \r\n244: <details>\r\n245: <summary><strong>How it works</strong></summary>\r\n246: \r\n247: <br>\r\n248: \r\n249: ```\r\n250: your ROM ──► builder/ ──► platinum3ds.pak (stays on your computer / SD card)\r\n251: \r\n252: pret/pokeplatinum @ pinned commit ──► + patches/ ──► + 3ds_port/ ──► .3dsx / .cia\r\n253: ```\r\n254: \r\n255: - The game's original C is compiled with GCC for the 3DS's CPU. The\r\n256:   decompilation is pinned in [`upstream.lock`](upstream.lock); the port's\r\n257:   changes to it live as patch files, small and easy to rebase onto a newer\r\n258:   upstream.\r\n259: - Nintendo's DS libraries (NitroSDK and NitroSystem) are built for the 3DS too\r\n260:   ([`3ds_port/nitro`](3ds_port/nitro), [`3ds_port/nitrosystem`](3ds_port/nitrosystem)).\r\n261:   The DS hardware they talk to is provided by the port: a 2D renderer, a 3D\r\n262:   geometry engine that hands scenes to the 3DS's GPU, a software DS sound chip,\r\n263:   and the services of the DS's second CPU (save chip, clock, power, touch\r\n264:   screen).\r\n265: - The game reads its files from your data pack, by their original file IDs\r\n266:   ([`docs/PAK_FORMAT.md`](docs/PAK_FORMAT.md)).\r\n267: - The work is spread over the New 3DS's cores: the game, the geometry engine\r\n268:   and the drawing each run on their own.\r\n269: \r\n270: </details>\r\n271: \r\n272: <details>\r\n273: <summary><strong>Building and testing</strong></summary>\r\n274: \r\n275: <br>\r\n276: \r\n277: ```sh\r\n278: python tools/bootstrap.py   # once: fetch the decompilation and SDKs, apply patches\r\n279: make test                   # build for the PC and run every test suite\r\n280: make game                   # the game for the 3DS\r\n281: make game-cia ROM=...       # the same, as a HOME Menu .cia\r\n282: ```\r\n283: \r\n284: The same game code also builds as **`pokeplatinum-pc`**, a PC runner without\r\n285: a screen, for finding quickly how far the game gets and where it stops\r\n286: ([`3ds_port/game/README.md`](3ds_port/game/README.md), which also covers\r\n287: debugging crashes and audio).\r\n288: \r\n289: To build the original DS ROM from the decompilation as a sanity check, follow\r\n290: pret's [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/pret/pokeplatinum/blob/main/INSTALL.md)\r\n291: inside `build/upstream/`.\r\n292: \r\n293: </details>\r\n294: \r\n295: <details>\r\n296: <summary><strong>What this repository holds</strong></summary>\r\n297: \r\n298: <br>\r\n299: \r\n300: - the port's own code (`3ds_port/`),\r\n301: - patches applied on top of the decompilation and SDKs (`patches/`),\r\n302: - tools that fetch the decompilation and build the port (`tools/`),\r\n303: - the builder that turns **your own legally dumped cartridge** into the game's\r\n304:   data, on your own computer (`builder/`).\r\n305: \r\n306: CI builds and tests everything on every push but uploads only text reports\r\n307: and tools with no game code in them (`tools/check_ci_artifacts.py` fails the\r\n308: build otherwise). Never commit a ROM, an extracted asset, or a build of the\r\n309: game. The `.gitignore` blocks the common cases, but check `git status` before\r\n310: you commit.\r\n311: \r\n312: ```\r\n313: 3ds_port/          3DS-side code\r\n314:   game/            the game: the 3DS program, the PC runner, the display, sound, input\r\n315:   nitro/           NitroSDK built with GCC, the DS hardware layer, PC unit tests\r\n316:   nitrosystem/     NitroSystem's Fnd/G2d/G3d/Gfd/Snd libraries and host tests\r\n317:   pak/             the data pack reader\r\n318:   common.mk        shared host, host32 and devkitARM toolchain flags\r\n319: builder/           turns your own ROM into the data pack (Python)\r\n320: docs/              the remaster display, wide art, the data pack\r\n321: patches/           changes applied on top of the decompilation and SDKs\r\n322: tools/             bootstrap, build helpers, the WideArt editor (Python)\r\n323: web/               the web builder's website (GitHub Pages; tools/build_site.py)\r\n324: wideart/           hand-drawn bands for the wider screen, built in (none of the game's pixels)\r\n325: Makefile           `make game`, `make game-cia`, `make test`, ...\r\n326: LICENSE            GPL-3.0, for this project's own code\r\n327: upstream.lock      the exact pret/pokeplatinum commit we build against\r\n328: ```\r\n329: \r\n330: </details>\r\n331: \r\n332: ### Roadmap\r\n333: \r\n334: - **Done:** the toolchain; the game's code built and running on the 3DS; 2D,\r\n335:   3D, sound, input, saving; the game fully playable; the new UI for the top\r\n336:   screen; the bottom screen as a menu, with the bag, party, summary, trainer\r\n337:   card, save, options and Town Map in its panel; enhancements and cheats; the\r\n338:   New 3DS XL's resolution; updated intro and UI animations; the HOME Menu\r\n339:   version; a Pokémon that follows you; 60 frames a second in the field; the\r\n340:   Pixel Perfect overworld; the Underground.\r\n341: - **Work in progress:** filling the wider view past the maps' edges, better\r\n342:   3D quality, polishing the bottom screen's UI, better lighting.\r\n343: - **Future wishlist:** Wi-Fi.\r\n344: - **Later:** SoulSilver / HeartGold on the same backend.\r\n345: \r\n346: ### Contributing\r\n347: \r\n348: See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how changes are made and tested,\r\n349: and [`AI_DISCLOSURE.md`](AI_DISCLOSURE.md) for how AI assistance is used.\r\n350: \r\n351: ## Community\r\n352: \r\n353: Join the **[Discord server](https://discord.gg/YjyA5ygpC)** to follow\r\n354: development, share screenshots and get help. Correctness and performance acceptance\n32: \n33: ### Objective performance contract\n34: \n35: - On a real 2011 O3DS at baseline clock and memory configuration, the game completes each ordinary gameplay frame before its next two-refresh deadline (roughly 33.4 ms). Target **≤25 ms active critical-path work** where practical, leaving headroom. `GameRuntime` runs the original HGSS state machine and calls Nitro-compatible services. It does not own PICA GPU handles or know about 3DS save paths.\n99: - `GraphicsCapture` consumes original G2/G3 operations and produces coherent immutable **frame/scene commands**. All CPU/DMA VRAM writes, palette/OBJ changes, bank mapping, register effects and display-capture dependencies must be tracked. Do not hash live mutable memory and draw later from another version.\n100: - `RenderBackend` translates those commands into PICA200 resources and ordered draws. It owns GPU synchronization and can detect unsupported operations, but **cannot select a software rasterizer**.\n101: - `AssetProvider` supplies stable logical game file IDs over a readonly indexed pack. Neither game code nor renderer knows whether this pack is on SD or inside RomFS.\n102: - `SaveStore` reads/writes **original-format HGSS save payloads**, with a transaction wrapper and backend-specific commitment. No mode switch inside game save serialization.\n103: - `Presentation` handles frame pacing, top/bottom invalidation and APT restore, without advancing game ticks or holding a render lock through IO.\n104: \n105: No monolithic GPU compatibility file, ad hoc global state or multiple competing frame loops. Dual installation and storage contract — implement early\n108: \n109: ### 4.1 Common user-ROM asset pack\n110: \n111: A host-only `rompack` tool takes the user's original HG/SS `.nds` and produces a versioned, indexed **`game.pak`**. No Nintendo ROM data, copyrighted fonts, artwork or fully prepared packs in public source distributions or CI logs/artifacts.\n114: \n115: Two products use the **same generated pack bytes**; compatibility and renderer output should not depend on installation mode.\n116: \n117: ### 4.2 Homebrew Launcher `.3dsx`\n118: \n119: Distribution/installation directory:\n120: \n121: ```text\n122: sdmc:/3ds/hgss-remaster/\n123:   hgss-remaster.3dsx\n124:   hgss-remaster.smdh\n125:   data/\n126:     heartgold.pak           # produced by the user, or soulsilver.pak\n127:     soulsilver.pak          # optional second edition\n128:   config.ini\n129:   saves/\n130:     heartgold_a.bin\n131:     heartgold_b.bin\n132:     soulsilver_a.bin\n133:     soulsilver_b.bin\n134:   logs/                     # optional; never synchronous in a frame\n135: ```\n136: \n137: - The `.3dsx` itself contains no user ROM data; install the user's pack alongside it.
