Rendering architecture: GPU-only by construction\n164: \n165: ### 5.1 Frame ownership\n166: \n167: The DS game may change emulated graphics memory/registers during callbacks. Build a coherent immutable GPU-facing command/state view for each scene, with content generations for VRAM tiles, palettes, OAM, DMA writes and register-dependent effects. Track live memory aliasing and VRAM bank remaps. Keep source buffers and GPU resources immutable until GPU completion; scanout availability is a separate ownership condition. Use bounded double buffers or a ring if hardware measures a benefit.\n168: \n169: **Never** use CPU pixel output as a substitute for a missing PICA200 mode. A missing effect is a tracked renderer blocker; the host oracle can render it to support debugging, but the 3DS executable cannot quietly do so.\n170: \n171: ### 5.2 Native 2D\n172: \n173: - **BG tiles**: retain 4bpp/8bpp tiles as palette-expanded GPU atlas entries, keyed by tile data + effective palette + bank mapping + generations; only dirty entries are regenerated. Keep visible map geometry/chunks and scroll via UV/transform; don't rebuild full images on camera movement.\n174: - **OBJ sprites**: retain atlases and ordered quads; respect OAM index/priority, affine transform, object window, mosaic, flip, transparency and tie behavior. Do not reorder overlapping translucent objects just to reduce texture binds.\n175: - **Priority**: faithfully position engine-A 3D as one BG-priority participant and compose it against BG/OBJ. Preserve equal-priority and blend behavior using ordered passes and tested depth/stencil rules, not a single approximate depth sort.\n176: - **Windows, clipping, fades and special blends**: scissor, stencil, alpha hardware, TEV and targeted render passes, with per-feature fixtures and an explicit supported-mode table. Handle unusual bitmap/capture modes with tested GPU-specific techniques.\n177: - **HBlank effects**: execute required callbacks in original order, collect effective per-scanline state and merge only adjacent identical spans. Do not arbitrarily group different lines. Specialize recurring effects only after equivalence tests.\n178: - **Display capture**: use two GPU-owned targets, never sample the target currently being written or download it to a CPU buffer. Validate feedback, prior-frame contents and ordering.\n179: - **Lower screen**: draw independently; do not clear/rebuild/transfer unchanged lower display layers. Invalidate cursor, touch states, animation, palette and window changes correctly.\n180: \n181: ### 5.3 Native HGSS text and UI\n182: \n183: Keep `TextPrinter`/`RenderText` interpretation, callbacks, delays, control codes, centering and original glyph advances. Hook the point where `RenderText` has decided a glyph and the original path calls `CopyGlyphToWindow`. Emit **font ID, glyph ID, logical x/y, palette/color, shadow, clip/window ID and reveal generation** to a retained GPU text model.\n184: \n185: Build the font data offline from **the user's original font NARC**. Produce native-resolution 400/320-display glyph atlases using carefully grid-fitted Pokémon-style bitmap shapes, plus original DS advance/width metrics and per-variant mapping. Do not use a generic 3DS system font for game dialogue; use citro2d custom BCFNT as an implementation benchmark, and prefer a compact dedicated citro3d glyph-quad backend where original text semantics make it simpler or faster. Batch compatible glyphs into few atlas/material runs; no per-character texture bind or full-window upload. Precompute common foreground/shadow variants and compare mask-based colouring on hardware before committing.\n186: \n187: **Scaling rule**: cumulative logical character positions map to native output coordinates, then snap consistently; never round each advance separately and accumulate visual drift. Compare nearest, carefully pre-scaled, and hand-tuned native glyphs on actual 3DS LCDs, preserving readable strokes. Reflow/anchor windows intentionally in the new 320×192 logical top-screen canvas. Test multiline, battle messages, Bag, Pokégear, Japanese/other supported language glyph coverage, inline colour, arrows, text erasure, scrolling and backgrounds with non-text pixel writes.\n188: \n189: A general HGSS `Window` can receive non-text pixel mutations. Intercept those too. For a pure text window render retained glyphs; for mixed-content windows implement a GPU-owned surface and ordered drawing operations. Audit `CopyWindowToVram`, `FillWindowPixelBuffer`, `ScrollWindow`, `BlitBitmapRect` and readback-like callers. Do not globally no-op original window writes without proving all consumers.\n190: \n191: One previously reported O3DS battle dialogue GPU path mirrored text horizontally. Make that a mandatory regression capture, not a known acceptable defect.\n192: \n193: ### 5.4 Native 3D\n194: \n195: - Decode G3 display lists into object-space **retained meshes** when immutable, with versioned dependencies and inherited matrix/material state. Use specialized fast paths for common geometry while retaining a **GPU-based** general command translator for unusual supported geometry.\n196: - Put ordinary transforms in PICA200 vertex shaders; pack vertices and retain textures. Avoid repeated CPU transform, per-triangle clipping and reconstruction wherever an equivalent PICA path is verified. DS fixed-point/lighting/clipping differences require explicit test cases, not blind fast-math.\n197: - Culling starts with object/chunk bounds and the actual widened 320×192 logical camera, including shadows/particles extending beyond their owners; never drop newly visible side content.\n198: - Treat alpha-test, translucent, polygon-ID, depth, fog, shadow and edge cases as distinct material contracts; state batching may cross only proven-safe boundaries. Audit the old duplicated-NPC and halo regressions.\n199: - Render directly at 400×240; 2D effects/text are positioned for native output. Preserve original scaling/layout of image-only cutscenes by deliberate framing or remaster side artwork, not stretching or mirroring.\n200: \n201: ### 5.5 GPU resource and memory strategy\n202: \n203: - Use O3DS VRAM (6 MiB) and normal application memory budgets from the start; enumerate every target and pool, including double buffers, depth and pending uploads. Start with a single 400×240 top plus 320×240 bottom and no compulsory stereo/right-eye target.\n204: - Investigate RGB565/RGBA5551/A8/LA8 vs RGBA8 where fidelity permits. PICA200 texture layout is tiled; texture swizzles are done offline or on **dirty** updates only. Use ETC1 only for assets whose image quality is acceptable.\n205: - Batch geometry by compatible material/texture and draw order. Cache only resources whose full dependencies are tracked. Keep hot ARM11 loops compact (Coffeepot measured a severe instruction-fetch cliff beyond ~16 KiB of hot code).\n206: - Use targeted GPU transfers/fills for supported copies, clears and output conversions. Never do a routine GPU→CPU→GPU compose cycle.\n207: - Start with conservative citro3d cache flushing, then measure explicit dirty-range flushing and `GX_CMDLIST_FLUSH` **only when every modified GPU-visible buffer is flushed correctly**. Treat `C3D_FrameEnd`/queue timings as asynchronous; beware in-flight buffer overwrites.\n208: - Treat core 1 as a *shared system core*. Don't rely on worker completion within the active frame. Add one bounded throughput worker (assets/audio) only when A/B testing improves total frame deadlines and doesn't slow services. N3DS-specific core 2 is outside the baseline.\n209: \n210: **Core references:** [Coffeepot renderer architecture](https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot/blob/main/ctr/engineering/PICA200/renderer-architecture.md), [tile renderer and O3DS measurements](https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot/blob/main/ctr/engineering/PICA200/2d-tile-renderer.md), [PICA200 2D semantics](https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot/blob/main/ctr/engineering/PICA200/rendering-2d.md), [HGSS original font](https://github.com/pret/pokeheartgold/blob/master/src/font_data.c), [original printer](https://github.com/pret/pokeheartgold/blob/master/src/render_text.c), [GPU command pipeline](https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot/blob/main/ctr/engineering/PICA200/pica200-command-pipeline.md).\n211: \n212: ## 6. Game timing, audio and app lifecycle\n213: \n214: The game source's main loop processes simulation tasks and waits for VBlank in a way that normally yields a 30 Hz field. Maintain those semantics for timing-sensitive code, callbacks, interrupts, RNG and audio; don't simply call update twice per frame. `C3D_FrameRate(30.0f)` with `C3D_FRAME_SYNCDRAW` is an available presentation mechanism, but **must not be layered on top of an additional independent pair of DS VBlank waits** that halves the rate. Implement one explicit scheduling bridge mapping emulated DS events to physical presentation events, and count **game ticks, produced frames, queued frames, GPU-complete frames and actually presented distinct frames** separately. Validate the DS's ~59.826 Hz native refresh discrepancy and drift.\n215: \n216: Audio: port the corrected baseline mixer/SDAT logic, queue output through `ndsp`, keep DSP buffer ownership and flushing correct, and make audio independent of GPU waits. Only then benchmark ARMv6 packed-SIMD mixing or compatible direct DSP channel operations; compare actual samples and event timing before adopting hardware-channel mapping. No frame-synchronous SD logging or audio decode. Use bounded prefetch and queues.\n217: \n218: Integrate APT suspend/resume, sleep/wake, HOME, low-memory failures, input/touch, RTC and controlled exit. Stop new work, finish ongoing GPU use, drain queues in dependency order, persist committed saves before services shut down, then free resources. Invalidate potentially lost GPU resources after restore. Test 3DSX return-to-Homebrew-Menu separately from CIA HOME behavior.\n219: \n220: ## 7. Preserve the source's original gameplay logic.\n231: \n232: **Milestone F — Uncommon graphics and correctness.** Complete remaining DS visual contracts (capture/feedback, HBlank effects, windows, mosaic, fades, battle intro, cutscenes, animated fonts, special sprite palettes). Eliminate every known unsupported mode in the test corpus with GPU implementations. Maintain hardware/reference regression tests and release-time guards against software rasterization or GPU image readback.\n233: \n234: **Milestone G — Both full installation products.** Build `dist/3dsx/` containing executable/metadata and example empty directory structure; require user-built `.pak`. Build a HeartGold CIA and SoulSilver CIA from supplied personal packs in the same invocation. Validate Title IDs, RomFS, first-run archive, commits, reboots, edition separation, CIA update and file migration/export/import. The public artifacts contain no ROM-derived content; user-local builds do.\n235: \n236: **Milestone H — Integrated profiling and Azahar hardening.** Use deterministic scripted scenes on a pinned Azahar build. Capture comparison screenshots, framebuffer differences, queue accounting, p50/p95/p99 stage times, memory peaks, resource counts and failures. Profile cold and warm loads. Build a hardware-ready profiler that can run without a debugger and write aggregates asynchronously. Stop only after attempting all feasible steps, with documented remaining obstacles and exact reproduction instructions.\n237: \n238: **Milestone I — Physical O3DS acceptance (owner hardware gate).** On 2011 O3DS, at baseline speed/memory: run both packaging modes, all prepared scripts, 10-minute sustained tests, suspend/restart, save fault tests, gameplay correctness, and worst-case resource stress. Compare against the 25 ms headroom objective and ~33.4 ms deadline. An O3DS miss is a hard regression to diagnose; no N3DS speedup or software fallback workaround. Iterate architecture until hardware passes. This gate cannot be completed by Azahar-only testing.\n239: \n240: ## 8. Scene corpus and mandatory regressions\n241: \n242: Create scene IDs, original reference captures, deterministic input scripts, fixed save files and expected graphics-state coverage:\n243: \n244: | Scene | Primary stress |\n245: | --- | --- |\n246: | Goldenrod standing/walking, nighttime and crowded | 3D reuse, camera, culling, UV animation, texture residency |\n247: | Dense town/interior/route, area boundary | wide culling, asset streaming, transitions |\n248: | Following Pokémon plus many NPCs | billboard/mesh and priority, animated resources |\n249: | Wild/trainer battle + message box | 3D/2D priority, battle text horizontal-mirror regression |\n250: | Status effects, weather, encounter transition | HBlank, blending, stencil, capture/feedback |\n251: | Bag, party, Pokégear, PC and Save menu | font metrics, windows, touch, bottom-screen invalidation |\n252: | Title, cinematic and credits | bitmap/special modes, artwork framing and long-duration playback |\n253: | Large-font/Unown/non-Latin text samples | full glyph atlas and control-code coverage |\n254: | Save/load, full card, interrupted write, suspend | both storage backends, no data loss |\n255: \n256: For every graphics capture, include all effective dependencies: VRAM and palette contents/generations, OAM, layer ordering, bank mapping, HBlank state, relevant prior frame and render-target contents. Record unexpected render modes as blocking omissions, not zeros.\n257: \n258: ## 9. Profiler, tests and build gates\n259: \n260: Capture per-frame `logic_ms`, `g2_decode_ms`, `g2_batch_ms`, `g3_decode_ms`, `g3_build_ms`, `gpu_record_ms`, `C3D_FrameEnd_ms`, `gpu_time_ms`, GPU clear/transfer timings when available, frame-begin wait, queued/completed/presented counts, VBlank periods, audio refills, SD read/decode, atlas misses/updates/uploads, geometry cache hits, command/vertex bytes, VRAM/FCRAM high-water, unsupported operation count and invalid GPU ownership events. All nested counters must state whether they overlap; never double-add parent and child spans.\n261: \n262: Instrument work in bounded in-memory structures, export aggregated logs outside the hot frame, and create an explicit low-overhead production profiling mode. Do not assume emulator timing resembles real O3DS. Compare optimized and reference versions from matching inputs and pinned binaries.\n263: \n264: **CI/automation gates:** clean builds of both targets; host tests for pack parsing, original-save checksums, corruption recovery, font metric layout, VRAM dirty dependencies and geometry-cache invalidation; no forbidden graphics backend symbols in shipping outputs; no accidental ROM-derived files in version control/artifacts; reproducible pack hash; Azahar smoke tests when executable environment supports them; file size and memory-budget reports. Preserve known-good binary after every passed integration gate.\n265: \n266: ## 10. Builder interface and install UX\n267: \n268: Implement a simple reproducible command-line builder (syntax illustrative; the implementer owns the final tested interface):\n269: \n270: ```sh\n271: # User-supplied original ROM; create homebrew SD pack\n272: python tools/build/pack.py --rom /path/to/HeartGold.nds --edition hg --out build/user/hg.pak\n273: python tools/build/build.py --target 3dsx --pack build/user/hg.pak --out dist/3dsx\n274: \n275: # Personal full CIA containing assets in its RomFS\n276: python tools/build/build.py --target cia --pack build/user/hg.pak \\\n277:   --title-id <persistent-user-chosen-id> --out dist/private/hg.cia\n278: ```\n279: \n280: The builder must validate dependencies and title metadata, print source edition/region and hash, calculate pack/installed size, reject duplicate/colliding Title IDs where detectable, record the save identity in a reusable manifest and show installation instructions. No GUI, online account or ROM-download feature is needed. CLI errors should explain how to fix an unsupported ROM or missing tool.\n281: \n282: `3dsx` instructions: copy executable and pack to the app folder under `/3ds/`; run through Homebrew Launcher.  \n283: `cia` instructions: provide own source ROM; build/install the CIA on a homebrew-enabled 3DS; use HOME to launch; game data comes from RomFS and save/config from the title archive. Back up/export original progress before uninstalling or changing Title ID.\n284: \n285: ## 11. Deliverables at end of the one-shot implementation\n286: \n287: 1. **Source tree** with reproducible build, pinned upstream dependencies, patch ledger and clear license/provenance records.\n288: 2. **ROM packer** supporting verified HeartGold/SoulSilver input revisions, deterministic game assets and user instructions.\n289: 3. **Bootable `.3dsx` and user-buildable `.cia`** with correct storage adapter behavior, save imports/exports and no ROM contents in public distributables.\n290: 4. **Integrated playable native game as far as the implementation reaches**, without a disguised CPU renderer; clearly identify incomplete modes.\n291: 5. **GPU renderer and native font** with capture/image-diff regression tests, resource ceilings and diagnostic counters.\n292: 6. **Automated Azahar tests and real-O3DS test kit**, including scripts and saved scenario states.\n293: 7. **Status report**: concrete files/commits, commands run, scenes passed, screenshots/diffs, timing counters, failure codes, known blockers and a ranked next-action list. Claims must be tied to exact evidence.\n294: \n295: ### Hard prohibitions\n296: \n297: No claiming full 30 FPS on O3DS from Azahar; no N3DS-only 'temporary' optimization path; no CPU renderer fallback, GPU framebuffer download or CPU full-screen conversion as a runtime crutch; no relabelled/interpolated frames presented as native updates; no silent object drops; no stale-input hash cache; no unauthorized bundled ROM/font/assets in public output; no save writes without error handling and, in CIA mode, commit; no changing Title ID on upgrade; no repeated low-value 'test-only' loops or architecture rewrites without measured evidence.\n298: \n299: ### Final acceptance statement\n300: \n301: **“O3DS full-speed remaster” is earned only when the actual 2011 console runs the verified release, both 3DSX and CIA builds work, both editions' tested content works, saves persist across restart, GPU output is correct, and the measured 30 FPS deadline is met across the acceptance corpus.** An Azahar-only implementation can be a strong release candidate but is not a certified O3DS performance result.\n302: \n303: ---\n304: \n305: ## Primary reference index\n306: \n307: -                 "text": "Read file C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\nds-to-3ds-pica200-porting-engineering-report.md, lines 1-150\n1: # Nintendo DS → Nintendo 3DS: Graphics Pipeline Porting Engineering Report\n2: \n3: **Research date:** 2026-11-12  \n4: **Scope:** Native ARM11 applications on Nintendo 3DS, including original 2011 hardware; source-available Nintendo DS games and engines; GPU-driven rendering rather than emulation.  \n5: **Reference quality:** Hardware facts are linked to GBATEK, 3dbrew, Nintendo/devkitPro source, and published architecture research. Proposed adaptations and performance advice are explicitly engineering recommendations, not guaranteed hardware behavior.  \n6: **Important qualification:** This is a design and source-research report, not the result of a compiled, hardware-tested implementation. Any cycle counts or performance claims require measurement on an original 3DS.\n7: \n8: ## 1. Decision in brief\n9: \n10: **Do not translate DS graphics registers into equivalent 3DS graphics registers: there are no equivalents for most of the DS's 2D pipeline.** Retain the game's logical render state, translate that state into native scene descriptions, and submit well-batched PICA200 geometry. Distinguish three contracts:\n11: \n12: 1. **Game contract:** what the game asks the graphics system to display—tile maps, sprites, materials, camera, priority, windows, effects, timing.\n13: 2. **DS hardware contract:** exactly how the DS's 2D engines, scanline mixer, and 3D geometry/rasterizer interpreted those requests.\n14: 3. **3DS backend contract:** GPU buffers, PICA render targets, textures, fixed-function fragment combiners, depth/stencil, synchronization and presentation.\n15: \n16: Keeping these contracts distinct is what makes native rendering scalable, testable and maintainable. For simple games, direct conversion of tiles to GPU quads may suffice. For mixed 2D/3D games, translucent sprites, per-scanline effects and rendering based on VRAM capture, a dedicated compatibility compositor is necessary. **The compositor should usually remain GPU-driven**, with rare, explicit compatibility exceptions rather than a hidden full-frame software renderer.\n17: \n18: ## 2. The hardware mismatch\n19: \n20: ### 2.1 Comparative specification\n21: \n22: | Axis | Nintendo DS | Original Nintendo 3DS / PICA200 | Porting consequence |\n23: | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n24: | Screens | Two independent 256 × 192 images | Top 400 × 240 per eye, bottom 320 × 240 | Separate viewport, camera and UI policies |\n25: | Main 2D path | Two scanline BG/OBJ engines | No DS-style BG or OAM hardware in native 3DS mode | Convert tiles/sprites into graphics primitives |\n26: | BG layers | Up to four per engine, mode-dependent | Render arbitrary GPU layers | Rebuild DS layer priority and palette behavior |\n27: | OBJ | Up to 128 OAM entries per engine, affine params | GPU textured quads/triangles | Stable priority sort, transform and batching |\n28: | DS 3D | Geometry-command FIFO, fixed matrices and lighting, scanline rasterization | Programmable vertex/geometry stages, fixed-function fragment stage | Parse/render DS display lists, migrate matrices/materials |\n29: | 3D into 2D | DS 3D output appears through main engine BG0 | No automatic 3D-as-BG0 | Render-to-texture or controlled compositing |\n30: | Special effects | 2D windows, brightness, two-target blend, mosaic; 3D toon/edge/fog | Depth/stencil, blend/alpha test, six TEV combiners, fog/lighting LUT | Multiple implementation strategies; some exact cases are multi-pass |\n31: | GPU memory | 656 KiB banked DS VRAM | 6 MiB SoC VRAM plus GPU-addressable main/linear memory | Reallocate buffers, cache converted content; no bank-as-VRAM assumption |\n32: | Graphics submission | OAM/BG register updates; 3D GXFIFO | C3D/C2D drawing commands, vertex/index buffers | Optimize command and state-change count |\n33: | Output representation | Per-scanline composition; DS 3D uses small scanline cache | Color/depth render targets → display transfer → LCD | Presentation and graphics-cache scheduling matter |\n34: \n35: Sources: [GBATEK DS video and 3D](https://oafc.anod.cc/man), [3dbrew Hardware](https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/Hardware), [3dbrew PICA registers](https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/GPU/Internal_Registers), [Copetti, Nintendo DS](https://www.copetti.org/writings/consoles/nintendo-ds/), [Copetti, Nintendo 3DS](https://www.copetti.org/writings/consoles/nintendo-3ds/).\n36: \n37: **Important:** A retail 3DS contains DS-compatible hardware for running DS titles in the system's legacy mode; it is **not** a convenient substitute for native PICA200 graphics inside a normal ARM11 homebrew process. The plan here is a native port, not switching to compatibility mode or forwarding DS register writes to the legacy PPUs. See Copetti's 3DS discussion of LgyFB and legacy display handling.\n38: \n39: ### 2.2 DS pipeline, reconstructed\n40: \n41: ```text\n42: ARM9 game and rendering code                 ARM7 and DMA support\n43:   ├─ BG tile maps, tile data, palettes ──┐\n44:   ├─ OAM sprite attributes and pixels ───┼─> 2D engine A ──┐\n45:   ├─ window/blend/mosaic/scroll regs ────┘                │\n46:   │                                                       ├─> final 256×192 main image\n47:   └─ geometry and material commands ──> DS 3D engine ────┘   (BG0 3D, where enabled)\n48:                                                        \n49:   └─ other BG/OAM/palette state ───────> 2D engine B ────────> final 256×192 sub image\n50: \n51:                                 line-timed effects / VRAM banks / capture / LCD swap\n52: ```\n53: \n54: The four BGs are not layers of precomposited images. The DS fetches tiles and sprite pixels while assembling the visible image, resolves priorities and transparencies, then applies selected color effects. The main 2D engine can place the 3D image into BG0. A DS game may change the meaning of the next scanline by writing registers during HBlank; that does not require rewriting the visible pixels in a CPU framebuffer.\n55: \n56: The 3D part is also unusual: the geometry engine processes a FIFO and holds vertex/polygon lists, swaps those lists with the rasterizer, and the rasterizer works ahead of display using a **48-scanline cache**, not a normal full-resolution framebuffer. This is materially different from the PICA's render-target model. GBATEK specifies a nominal DS display refresh of about **59.8261 Hz**; do not assume the DS's VBlank is an exact 60.000 Hz clock.\n57: \n58: ### 2.3 PICA200 pipeline, reconstructed\n59: \n60: ```text\n61: ARM11 game logic\n62:   └─ native rendering frontend\n63:        ├─ persistent textures and atlases\n64:        ├─ vertex/index buffers (GPU-accessible memory)\n65:        ├─ shader binaries / uniforms\n66:        └─ command buffers + fixed-function state\n67:                  ↓\n68:              PICA200\n69:        vertex/geometry processing\n70:                  ↓\n71:              rasterizer\n72:                  ↓\n73:        texture fetch, lighting, TEV combiners\n74:                  ↓\n75:        depth/stencil/alpha/blend and color target\n76:                  ↓\n77:        GPU display-transfer / LCD framebuffer\n78:                  ↓\n79:            top and bottom LCD\n80: ```\n81: \n82: PICA has **programmable vertex processing**, and its primitive engine can serve geometry processing; it does **not** have ordinary programmable fragment shaders of the kind expected on desktop OpenGL/Vulkan. Only three of its four texture units handle conventional 2D texture sampling; the fourth is specialized for procedural textures. Six configurable texture environment stages provide color/alpha operations. Consequently a rendering plan requiring arbitrary per-pixel conditionals, texture indirection or custom fragment code cannot simply be implemented as a GLSL fragment shader. Prefer ordinary hardware blending, multipass textures, alpha-test/stencil/depth, TEV combinations, LUT-based features and precomputed resources.\n83: \n84: The PICA shader floating point format and special-value behavior also differ from ordinary IEEE arithmetic (documented by 3dbrew). Expect deviations for extremely small values, singular transforms and exact emulation of DS fixed-point operations.\n85: \n86: Sources: [3dbrew shader ISA](https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/Shader_Instruction_Set), [3dbrew GPU internal registers](https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/GPU/Internal_Registers), [3dbrew programming guide](https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/GPU/Programming_Guide), [Copetti 3DS](https://www.copetti.org/writings/consoles/nintendo-3ds/).\n87: \n88: ## 3. Port the representation, not the registers\n89: \n90: ### 3.1 Inventory source code before conversion\n91: \n92: Search the source tree for **every** direct or indirect graphics hardware dependency. Typical DS source interfaces include:\n93: \n94: - `videoSetMode`, `videoSetModeSub`, `bgInit`, `bgInitSub`, `bgSetScroll`, `bgUpdate`, `bgGetMapPtr`, `bgGetGfxPtr`, `bgSetPriority`.\n95: - `oamInit`, `oamSet`, `oamSetAffineIndex`, `oamRotateScale`, `oamUpdate`, `oamUpdateSub` and OAM memory writes.\n96: - `glBegin`, `glEnd`, `glVertex*`, `glTexCoord*`, `glMaterial*`, `glPolyFmt`, `glBindTexture`, `glFlush`, Nintendo Nitro/NNS_G3d wrappers, and raw writes to `GXFIFO`/`GXSTAT`.\n97: - `REG_DISPCNT`, `REG_BGxCNT`, `REG_BGxHOFS/VOFS`, `REG_BLDCNT`, `REG_BLDALPHA`, `REG_BLDY`, `REG_MASTER_BRIGHT`, `REG_DISPCAPCNT`, palette/OAM/VRAM pointers and `VRAM_*` bank macros.\n98: - `irqSet(IRQ_HBLANK/IRQ_VBLANK/IRQ_VCOUNT)`, `swiWaitForVBlank`, `dmaCopy*`, `dmaFill*`, `DC_FlushRange`, `DC_InvalidateRange`, line-timed callbacks.\n99: - Asset compressors, tile/bitmap formats, DS model display-list interpreters, Nitro resource IDs, 2D screen mapping assumptions and text rasterization code.\n100: \n101: Also find implicit dependencies: pointer equality comparisons into VRAM, hardcoded texture base offsets, assumptions about sprite visibility/overflow, and animation code that modifies tile graphics while a screen is being scanned out. Automated grep is a starting point, not a complete inventory; inspect macros, generated code and assembler.\n102: \n103: Classify each operation as **persistent state change**, **pixel content update**, **draw declaration**, **timing-sensitive update**, **render feedback**, or **readback**. Their migration costs differ sharply.\n104: \n105: ### 3.2 Suggested intermediate representation\n106: \n107: ```c\n108: // Schematic API; not a drop-in replacement for libnds/citro3d.\n109: typedef enum {\n110:     SURFACE_TILED_BG, SURFACE_AFFINE_BG, SURFACE_BITMAP_BG,\n111:     SURFACE_SPRITE, SURFACE_MESH, SURFACE_3D_LAYER\n112: } SurfaceKind;\n113: \n114: typedef struct {\n115:     SurfaceKind kind;\n116:     uint8_t engine;        // DS main or sub: logical screen identity\n117:     uint8_t priority;      // original DS priority, not arbitrary z\n118:     uint16_t stable_id;    // original OAM/draw order for tie breaking\n119:     uint32_t palette_id;\n120:     uint32_t texture_id;\n121:     int32_t x_fp, y_fp;    // source-space fixed-point coordinates\n122:     uint32_t flags;        // flip/affine/window/mosaic/blend flags\n123:     // source-specific transform, image region, mesh, and window data\n124: } RenderItem;\n125: \n126: typedef struct {\n127:     RenderItem *items;\n128:     size_t item_count;\n129:     // per-screen backdrop, 4 BG configurations, OBJ state, window\n130:     // regions, transparency selectors, scanline events, 3D layer\n131: } DsVisualFrame;\n132: ```\n133: \n134: Do **not** bake arbitrary DS behavior into `C2D_DrawImage` calls scattered through gameplay modules. Use an explicit extraction pipeline:\n135: \n136: ```text\n137: DS game state/assets\n138:   → source-specific adapters / register-state recorder\n139:   → stable DS visual frame\n140:   → priority + window + effects compiler\n141:   → texture/mesh cache and render pass planner\n142:   → citro3d/citro2d commands\n143: ```\n144: \n145: Advantages: preserve the original logic, unit-test priority and coordinate rules without hardware, swap backend implementations, support accurate and enhanced rendering modes, and record per-frame reproducible traces.\n146: \n147: ### 3.3 Choose the right boundary\n148: \n149: 1. **High-level DS source available:** Replace the calls that construct tilemaps, sprites, camera, text and 3D meshes. Highest performance potential, least semantic guesswork.\n150: 2. **Only low-level register-oriented source:** Introduce a narrow virtual DS graphics-state adapter that records writes to virtual registers/VRAM and emits render operations at frame boundaries. This is a state translator, **not** a cycle-accurate emulator; exceptional HBlank cases may need an event timeline.\n[Output truncated. Continue reading with offset: 151]"

                "text": "# Build on Windows\r\n\r\nVerified 2026-11-12 on Windows 11 with a **from-scratch** bootstrap and build\r\n(empty `build/upstream`, empty `build/kj`): 91 patches applied, 0 errors,\r\n`.3dsx` packaged in about 6 minutes, and the title screen checked in Azahar.\r\nOutput: a HeartGold `.3dsx`. SoulSilver and CIA are not built yet.\r\n\r\n## Requirements\r\n\r\n| Tool | Where | Notes |\r\n| --- | --- | --- |\r\n| devkitPro | `C:\\devkitPro` | Packages: devkitARM, libctru, citro3d, 3dstools, picasso. Versions are pinned in [`upstream.lock`](../upstream.lock). Its MSYS2 (`C:\\devkitPro\\msys2`) supplies `bash`, `make` and Python 3.14 (`/usr/bin/python`). |\r\n| Git for Windows | `C:\\Program Files\\Git` | **Required for bootstrap.** devkitPro MSYS2's own `git` cannot fetch over HTTPS (see [pitfalls](#pitfalls)). |\r\n| Azahar | `C:\\Program Files\\Azahar\\azahar.exe` | Testing only (`tools/azahar/run.ps1`). |\r\n| PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) | | Runs the Azahar harness. |\r\n| ROM | your own verified US dump | Only needed for the data pack. Never commit ROMs, packs, saves or extracted data. |\r\n\r\n## Build\r\n\r\nRun every build step **inside devkitPro's MSYS2 login shell**\r\n(`C:\\devkitPro\\msys2\\usr\\bin\\bash.exe -lc \"...\"`). The login profile\r\n(`/etc/profile.d/devkit-env.sh`) sets `DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro` and\r\n`DEVKITARM=/opt/devkitpro/devkitARM`, which the build reads to find\r\n`arm-none-eabi-gcc`. Use absolute `/c/...` paths throughout.\r\n\r\nFrom Git Bash or PowerShell:\r\n\r\n```sh\r\nC:/devkitPro/msys2/usr/bin/bash.exe -lc '\r\n  export PATH=\"/c/Program Files/Git/cmd:$PATH\"    # Git for Windows first (HTTPS)\r\n  K=/c/Users/<you>/workdir/kohjoh\r\n  cd $K\r\n  python tools/game/bootstrap.py                   # pinned decomp + every patch in patches/\r\n  python tools/game/check_patches.py               # fails if build/upstream lacks a patch\r\n  python tools/game/hgss_game.py --root $K/build/upstream --target 3ds --out $K/build/kj -j 32\r\n' > build/kj-build.log 2>&1\r\n```\r\n\r\n**`--target 3ds` is required.** The default is `host32`, a PC build for tests.\r\n\r\nA build succeeded only if the log ends with\r\n`packaged .../pokeheartgold.3dsx` **and** has no `error:` lines. If the\r\nvendored SDK/NitroSystem library fails to compile, the build prints\r\n`warning: the vendored library build failed; linking with libnitrosystem.a,\r\nlibnitro.a ...` and **still packages a `.3dsx` from stale libraries**. Any\r\nSDK or NitroSystem change is then silently absent. Check for it:\r\n\r\n```sh\r\ngrep -E \"error:|vendored library build failed\" build/kj-build.log   # must print nothing\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Outputs (`--out build/kj`)\r\n\r\n| Path | Contents |\r\n| --- | --- |\r\n| `pokeheartgold.3dsx` | the program |\r\n| `pokeheartgold-3ds.elf` | symbols, linked at 0x00100000 (`arm-none-eabi-addr2line -e` for crash addresses) |\r\n| `pokeheartgold.build-info.txt` | commit, dirty flag, sha256, the state of every legacy flag |\r\n| `obj/`, `app/`, `ctr/`, `sdk/`, `gen/` | incremental objects and generated headers |\r\n| `link.log`, `link-<utc>.log` | linker output; unresolved symbols are reported here |\r\n\r\nThe shared vendored-library trees are `build/hgss-sdk`, `build/hgss-nns`, and\r\n`build/NitroSDK` / `build/NitroSystem` (links into `build/upstream/lib`).\r\n\r\n### Timing and incremental builds\r\n\r\n- Bootstrap � 1 min (shallow fetch + `git am` of the patch stack).\r\n- First build � 5 min at `-j 32`. A rebuild after a kohjoh-side change takes\r\n  about 2 min. Game objects are skipped when they are newer than their source\r\n  and every `-MMD` dependency and their flags match; the Nitro libraries are\r\n  re-made by `make`.\r\n- Build each variant into its own `--out` (e.g. `--out $K/build/kjz\r\n  --define KJ_G3_ZERO_TRACE`) so variants never mix objects.\r\n\r\n### Four variants (gold/silver x normal/prof)\r\n\r\n`tools/game/build_variants.py` builds the four shipping configurations in\r\nsequence and prints the `.3dsx` paths:\r\n\r\n```sh\r\npython tools/game/build_variants.py            # all four\r\npython tools/game/build_variants.py --only gold-prof\r\npython tools/game/build_variants.py --list\r\n```\r\n\r\n| Variant | `--game` | `HGSS_PROFILE` | `--out` |\r\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\r\n| `gold-normal` | heartgold | unset | `build/kj-gold-normal` |\r\n| `gold-prof` | heartgold | `on` | `build/kj-gold-prof` |\r\n| `silver-normal` | soulsilver | unset | `build/kj-silver-normal` |\r\n| `silver-prof` | soulsilver | `on` | `build/kj-silver-prof` |\r\n\r\nRun them **one at a time**. The variants share `build/hgss-sdk`,\r\n`build/hgss-nns` and the headers generated under `build/upstream`, so\r\nconcurrent variants race on the shim junctions and on header generation; the\r\ndriver serialises them. As with a single build, a variant counts only if its\r\nlog ends with `packaged ... .3dsx` and has no `error:` or\r\n`vendored library build failed` line. Per-variant logs are\r\n`build/kj-<variant>-build.log`.\r\n\r\n"

A handful of common distributions are listed below for\n275: > convenience.\n276: \n277: Once you have installed all of the listed dependencies, proceed to [downloading\n278: the repository](#2-downloading-the-repository).\n279: \n280: #### Debian (and derivatives, e.g., Ubuntu, Mint)\n281: \n282: 1. Install the following packages via `apt`:\n289: \n290:     ```bash\n291:     sudo apt install bison flex g++ gcc-arm-none-eabi git make ninja-build pkg-config wget python3 xz-utils nasm libc6:i386 libpng-dev\n292:     ```\n293: \n294: #### Arch Linux (and derivatives, e.g., Manjaro, Endeavour)\n295: \n296: 1. Enable the [multilib repository](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Multilib).\n297: \n298: 2. Install dependencies via `pacman`:\n299: \n300:     ```bash\n301:     sudo pacman -S arm-none-eabi-gcc bison flex gcc git make ninja python wget xz lib32-glibc libpng\n302:     ```\n303: \n304: #### Fedora (and derivatives, e.g., AlmaLinux, Red Hat Enterprise Linux)\n305: \n306: ```bash\n307: sudo dnf install arm-none-eabi-gcc-cs bison flex gcc-c++ git make ninja-build python3 wget2 xz glibc32 libpng\n308: ```\n309: \n310: ## 2. Downloading the Repository\n311: \n312: From your terminal, navigate to the path in which you will store the repository.\n313: Users of WSL 1 should ensure that their target is on the Windows file drive.\n314: \n315: ```bash\n316: git clone https://github.com/pret/pokeplatinum\n317: cd pokeplatinum\n318: ```\n319: \n320: ## 3. Building the Repository\n321: \n322: To build the ROM, run:\n323: \n324: ```bash\n325: make\n326: ```\n327: or to skip the checksum if you want to modify the code:\n328: ```\n329: make rom\n330: ```\n331: \n332: If everything works, then the following ROM should be built:\n333: \n334: - [build/pokeplatinum.us.nds](https://datomatic.no-intro.org/index.php?page=show_record&s=28&n=4997) `sha1: 0862ec35b24de5c7e2dcb88c9eea0873110d755c`\n335: \n336: Optionally, the repository can be configured to build a [\"revision 0\"\n337: ROM](https://datomatic.no-intro.org/index.php?page=show_record&s=28&n=3541)\n338: (`sha1: ce81046eda7d232513069519cb2085349896dec7`). This revision matches the\n339: original retail version that was shipped in North America; it contains an error\n340: in the GTS code where the game will not display the level range of a wanted\n341: Pokémon. This error was patched as part of a second shipment of cartridges for\n342: the North American release; it is not present in any other localization.\n343: \n344: To build this revision, instead of the above command, run the following:\n345: \n346: ```bash\n347: ROM_REVISION=0 make\n348: ```\n349: \n350: If you need further assistance, feel free to ask a question in the `#pokeplatinum`\n351: channel of the `pret` Discord (see `README.md` for contact information) or [open\n352: an issue](https://github.com/pret/pokeplatinum/issues/new).\n353: \n354: ## 4.       "id": "msg_1e59f8df1001Jmtf4d4cxzyIWn",
      "metadata": {
        "displayText": "you're working on sinjoh. read the project documentation to familiarize yourself first. you'll also need to get familiar with kohjoh, pokeplatinum (the original source), pokeplatinum-3ds (the existing new3ds-only port), and coffeepot. we are going to take a very different route. you are going to bootstrap an entirely new source port of pokemon platinum, as a nintendo 3ds homebrew. your end goal is to replicate all of the remaster enhancements of pokeplatinum-3ds, but based on kohjoh's more sane internals, and targeting the original 2011 3ds - not the 2015 new 3ds. some fancy things like scaling might be too much for the original 3ds meager hardware, and that's okay. as it turns out, if we pre-compute wideart at compile/package time, wideart is cheap enough for o3ds - so you must include that too. your goal is to squeeze the remaster/port into the old3ds hardware, not to worry about new3ds enhancements. you only need to get sinjoh-platinum working, forget about sinjoh-diamond or sinjoh-pearl for now. most of the hard work, engineering and research has already been done for you. you should refer heavily to the reference material in the workdir. you will test your own work using an emulator - see how far you can get with lotus v0.0.2. i believe that build currently defaults to always software rendering, so you'll need to find out how to force it to use vulkan. make sure you run lotus in windowed mode, so i can watch what you're doing. if you have too much trouble with lotus, you are permitted to use vanilla azahar instead, which is also available to you. again, read the docs before you start writing code. all the hard work has already been done for you. ",

        "attachments": [],

                "text": "Read file C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\LOTUS-v0.0.2-windows-x64\\docs\\06-ipc-and-session-contract.md, lines 1-105\n1: # 06 — IPC, session protocol, safe points and lifecycle\n2: \n3: ## Purpose\n4: \n5: The IPC contract must survive Azahar upgrades, debug feature additions, replacement of the C++ worker and future non-Azahar execution engines. Treat IPC as a *product boundary*, not an easy way to expose Azahar classes.\n6: \n7: ## Transport\n8: \n9: - Windows: private named pipe by default. Linux/macOS: Unix-domain socket. Authenticate via OS filesystem/pipe permissions and a supervisor-created random capability token in handshake; token is a defense-in-depth measure, not a substitute for OS access rules.\n10: - Frame format: length-delimited binary Protocol Buffers (proposal), explicit max message size, request ID, session ID, epoch, protocol major/minor, payload, response status; async events have monotonically increasing per-worker sequence.\n11: - Reject oversized frames before allocating memory; no unbounded recursion/arrays or untrusted length fields. Define a maximum for every request, including reads, captures and event batches.\n12: - No host-facing public TCP/UDP listener in normal mode. If remote control is added later, require explicit opt-in, TLS, strong authentication and per-session authorization.\n13: \n14: ## Proposed envelope\n15: \n16: ```text\n17: Request { version, request_id, session_id, expected_epoch,\n18:           deadline_ms, method, body }\n19: Reply   { version, request_id, session_id, actual_epoch,\n20:           status, body, error_detail }\n21: Event   { version, session_id, epoch, seq, guest_tick?,\n22:           host_ns?, kind, body }\n23: ```\n24: \n25: Schema fields are **proposals**, not verified Azahar wire structures. Maintain machine-readable schema in `specs/` and generate Rust/C++ code with reproducible tools. C ABI and public RPC structs use fixed-width types; no cross-language C++ STL objects.\n26: \n27: ### Critical statuses\n28: \n29: `OK`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `UNSUPPORTED`, `NOT_READY`, `NOT_PAUSED`, `BUSY`, `TIMEOUT`, `STALE_EPOCH`, `UNMAPPED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `RESOURCE_LIMIT`, `INCONSISTENT_SNAPSHOT`, `WORKER_EXITED`, `INTERNAL`. Do not answer `OK` because a request was queued; distinguish `ACCEPTED` (pending) from committed completion.\n30: \n31: ## Handshake example\n32: \n33: ```\n34: client -> worker: HELLO(protocol=1.0, session_uuid, nonce,\n35:                         requested_features=[cpu_debug,gpu_capture,frame_ring])\n36: worker -> client: CAPABILITIES(protocol=1.0, worker_sha,\n37:                         azahar_sha, model=old3ds,\n38:                         backends=[software,vulkan], max_read=..., ...)\n39: client -> worker: CONFIGURE(instance_root, output_buffers, audio_policy, deterministic_seed)\n40: worker -> client: READY(epoch=1)\n41: ```\n42: \n43: Every session advertises **actual** capabilities. Never promise features based solely on the branch name. Handshake failure cannot leave a live orphan worker or a partially writable save root.\n44: \n45: ## Epoch and sequencing\n46: \n47: Increment state epoch after load, reset, restore/rewind or any operation invalidating address-space/resource identity. A request referencing an older epoch is rejected, except immutable historical-capture reads that specify an artifact ID. GPU draw/resource references include `(epoch, frame_seq, draw_seq)`; a plain register index is not sufficient context to reconstruct past state.\n48: \n49: All mutating requests (memory writes, breaks, input injection, clock changes) are serialized through the emulation thread. Query commands may use a published immutable snapshot or schedule a safe-point read.\n50: \n51: ## Safe-point queue\n52: \n53: Existing Azahar's `System::ProcessPendingWork()` runs GDB and scripting operations on the emulation thread and is invoked between slices/while waiting in the frame limiter. Add the worker's request queue here or a similarly clearly defined place; follow the same wakeup strategy via `NotifyPendingWork()` when new work arrives. Source: https://github.com/azahar-emu/azahar/blob/master/src/core/core.cpp\n54: \n55: Rules:\n56: 1. The IPC receiving thread **does not read mutable `Core::System`, GPU or kernel objects directly**.\n57: 2. It validates framing, enqueue bounded command, returns pending/request ID if long-running.\n58: 3. The emulation thread reaches a safe point, validates epoch and required run state, performs operation, emits final completion.\n59: 4. Screenshot/GPU readback may finish on a renderer worker; the control operation remains pending until the requested consistency contract is met.\n60: 5. Safe-point operations have a budget; a massive memory read runs in bounded chunks or deliberately stops emulation. Long tasks should never leave a half-applied guest mutation.\n61: 6. A pause request transitions through `PAUSING`, then completes only once requested CPU state is quiescent. Avoid claiming GPU is quiescent unless a separate barrier completed.\n62: \n63: ## Stepping contract\n64: \n65: Avoid ambiguous `step`. Define:\n66: \n67: - `step_cpu_instruction(core_id, thread_id?)`: exactly one retired guest instruction on the selected core/thread or return `UNSUPPORTED` if backend cannot honor it. Test against Azahar's `SingleStep()` semantics; it currently delegates to `RunLoop(false)` and is not proven to target one selected core.\n68: - `step_to_event(event_filter)`: stop at next selected callback or guest event; may execute arbitrary instructions.\n69: - `step_frame(boundary=top_vblank_start|bottom_vblank_start|presented_frame)`: explicit boundary, record skipped/duplicate presentation.\n70: - `run_until(breakpoint|guest_tick|frame_count|event|timeout)`: bounded by both guest goal and host timeout, with stop reason and final state.\n71: - `pause(mode=cpu_only|capture_consistent)`: stronger mode may wait for renderer synchronization.\n72: \n73: ## Shared-memory image ring\n74: \n75: Descriptor per ring: magic, schema, session/epoch, slot_count, width, height, stride, pixel format, screen/eye identity, handle/lifetime token. Slot metadata: atomic state, generation, sequence, guest frame seq, capture host timestamp, bytes valid, hash. Writer must never overwrite a leased slot; use bounded drop/backpressure policy. Ring reallocation increments generation, requires consumer acknowledgement and does not reuse an old OS handle while clients still reference it. Stale access becomes a typed error.\n76: \n77: Nominal 3DS native screens: top 400x240, bottom 320x240; RGB(A) output must identify stereoscopic eye. Hardware often stores rotated framebuffers; define whether published pixels are normalized to display orientation. Do not rely on shape alone.\n78: \n79: ## Control / observation surface\n80: \n81: | Method group | Commands | Minimum info returned |\n82: |---|---|---|\n83: | Session | load, run, pause, reset, stop, status | state, epoch, stop reason, config hash |\n84: | CPU | regs, disasm, step, breakpoints | core, thread, mode, PC, validity |\n85: | Memory | map, read, write, search, watch | process, space, range, epoch, errors |\n86: | Kernel | process/thread list, IPC trace, wait graph | IDs, scheduling/wait states, event seq |\n87: | GPU | external/internal regs, command lists, draw, textures, frame | draw/frame identity, capture consistency |\n88: | DSP | state, audio ring/underrun metrics | sample time, emulation status, backend |\n89: | Trace | arm, start, stop, flush, export | filters, counts, dropped, artifact hash |\n90: | Input | inject, set script ownership, touch | accepted boundary, effective sample tick |\n91: \n92: ## Cancellation and idempotency\n93: \n94: - `get_*` reads are idempotent with snapshot/epoch identities; live reads may differ across calls.\n95: - `load`, `reset`, `write_memory` and `run_until` are **not** automatically idempotent. Replayed request IDs return recorded result within a bounded retention window, not reapply mutation.\n96: - Cancellation interrupts waiting/pending operations and reports whether effect was already committed; cannot rewind a half-frame by fiat.\n97: - `stop` attempts graceful shutdown, then terminates worker at deadline; report unflushed output and preserve crash logs.\n98: \n99: ## Artifacts\n100: \n101: Export a manifest and content-addressed files, not opaque log text. `manifest.json` includes worker/branch hashes, GPUI/protocol version, game hash (not ROM bytes), model, graphics backend, selected test, input seed, time domains, capture feature flags, timestamps, dropped-event counters, storage snapshot ID and host environment. Large binary files have SHA-256 checksums and explicit schema IDs.\n102: \n103: ## Security and privacy\n104: \n105: MCP is not allowed to supply arbitrary absolute worker paths. Supervisor allocates roots under its own managed workspace; reads/writes are by object handles or normalized virtual-relative paths. Memory writes/patches and firmware access are privileged tool categories that require explicit session capabilities. Retain a local audit trail of mutating commands. Avoid collecting screenshots or saves unless requested by user/test scenario; provide retention/deletion controls."

                "text": "Read file C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\kohjoh\\docs\\lotus.md, lines 1-219\n1: # Running kohjoh in LOTUS\n2: \n3: LOTUS is a second integration debugger beside Azahar. It runs the same\n4: Azahar-derived core as `tools/azahar/run.ps1` but drives it from a native worker\n5: process over a local MCP server, so frames are advanced deterministically\n6: instead of being screenshotted at wall-clock times. It is **not** an O3DS timing\n7: authority either: every result from it is EMULATOR-only evidence\n8: ([kohjoh.md 1](../kohjoh.md)).\n9: \n10: Installed at `C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\LOTUS-v0.0.1-windows-x64` (portable ZIP,\n11: v0.0.1). Its own documentation is in that folder's `docs/`; the relevant pages\n12: are `20`-`26`, especially `21-native-control.md` (worker protocol) and\n13: `23-local-mcp.md` (the stdio MCP surface).\n14: \n15: ## Fixed configuration\n16: \n17: The native worker runs Old 3DS, software rendering, HLE services, HLE/muted DSP,\n18: guest ticks 0 and guest time 2000-01-01 UTC, with no window. Nothing here is\n19: configurable through MCP; the host JSON is trusted startup input that the model\n20: cannot change.\n21: \n22: ## Backend\n23: \n24: Both backends run kohjoh. They are the same Azahar core at the same pin\n25: (`05773bbb5`); the only build difference is `-DCTR_BACKEND_NAME`, which changes\n26: the reported `backend_name` and nothing else. `LOTUS.cmd`/`CITnLO` is the\n27: default; `LOTUS-AZAHAR.cmd`/`--backend AZAHAR` is the upstream-tracking one.\n28: \n29: Two things look like failures and are not:\n30: \n31: - **`Failed to find title id for ROM (Error 0)`** is logged by *every* `.3dsx`\n32:   load, including sessions that then run for thousands of frames, so it is not a\n33:   usable failure signal. kohjoh's `.3dsx` has no SMDH (`header_size = 0x20`, no\n34:   `SMDH` magic, because `make_smdh` finds no icon), which is what the\n35:   `SelfNCCH ... might be a 3dsx file` warning refers to; neither backend needs\n36:   the banner. The Homebrew Launcher on real hardware does not either.\n37: - **A session that ends with an 8-line worker log and an empty `sdmc/`** was\n38:   usually created and then abandoned: sessions die with the MCP server, and\n39:   `lotus_create_session` has by then loaded and paused the guest, so closing the\n40:   server immediately leaves no guest log at all. Confirm with\n41:   `lotus_session_status` before concluding the load failed.\n42: \n43: ## Sessions and the private SD card\n44: \n45: Each session is its own worker process with its own root:\n46: \n47: ```text\n48: <lotus>/data/<profile>/sessions/<handle>/\n49:   sdmc/            # guest SD card: sdmc:/ maps here\n50:   nand/  sysdata/  log/  cheats/\n51: ```\n52: \n53: `lotus_create_session` loads the approved asset **immediately** and pauses, so\n54: kohjoh starts before its data pack exists unless the pack is already there. The\n55: sequence is therefore:\n56: \n57: 1. create the session (kohjoh boots, reports no pack, idles),\n58: 2. copy the pack, manifest, save and input script into that session's `sdmc`,\n59: 3. `reset` — the worker reloads the same content with the new SD contents.\n60: \n61: Sessions belong to the MCP server process that created them and cannot be\n62: re-attached later: closing the server (or OpenCode restarting it) ends them, and\n63: each new session needs its own staged copy of the pack (125 MB, a few seconds on\n64: local disk).\n65: \n66: Guest paths kohjoh uses:\n67: \n68: ```text\n69: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/data/<edition>.pak\n70: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/data/<edition>.manifest.json\n71: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/saves/<edition>.sav\n72: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/script.txt\n73: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/logs/<edition>.log\n74: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/dumps/\n75: ```\n76: \n77: ## Harness: `tools/lotus/run.py`\n78: \n79: The equivalent of `tools/azahar/run.ps1` for LOTUS. It creates a session,\n80: stages the requested files, resets, advances frames in chunks, presses buttons\n81: and writes PNG captures plus the guest log location.\n82: \n83: ```sh\n84: python tools/lotus/run.py --pack build/prepare-test/heartgold.pak \\\n85:   --manifest build/prepare-test/heartgold.manifest.json \\\n86:   --artifact build/kj-gold-normal/pokeheartgold.3dsx \\\n87:   --frames 3000 --shots 1200,1800,2400,3000 --tag boot\n88: \n89: python tools/lotus/run.py --artifact build/kj-gold-normal/pokeheartgold.3dsx \\\n90:   --pack build/prepare-test/heartgold.pak --manifest build/prepare-test/heartgold.manifest.json \\\n91:   --frames 1200 --press 600:START --shots 1200 --tag title\n92: ```\n93: \n94: | Option | Effect |\n95: | --- | --- |\n96: | `--artifact` | `.3dsx` to run (default `build/kj/pokeheartgold.3dsx`) |\n97: | `--edition` | `heartgold` (default) or `soulsilver`, selects the SD file names |\n98: | `--pack`, `--manifest` | stage the data pack into this session's SD card |\n99: | `--save path` / `--fresh-save` | install a save / delete the session's save |\n100: | `--script file` | scripted input (`tests/inputs/*.txt`); absent, none is staged |\n101: | `--frames`, `--chunk` | total frames, and frames per native request (default 60) |\n102: | `--shots 10,30` | capture at those frame numbers (the last frame always captured) |\n103: | `--press FRAME:KEYS` | hold keys over a frame boundary, e.g. `900:DOWN+A`, `600:START` |\n104: | `--touch FRAME:X,Y` | touch the bottom screen at native `320x240` coordinates, e.g. `5000:160,120` |\n105: | `--hold` | pause before each capture |\n106: | `--backend`, `--lotus` | `AZAHAR` (default) or `CITnLO`; LOTUS install root |\n107: | `--tag`, `--out-dir` | output folder: `build/lotus/<tag>/` |\n108: \n109: Captures are written as `f<frame>-top.png` (400x240) and `f<frame>-bottom.png`\n110: (320x240), converted from the worker's normalized BGRA8 output. Each capture's\n111: SHA-256 is printed, so pictures can be compared with Azahar or melonDS runs.\n112: \n113: ## MCP from OpenCode\n114: \n115: `C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\opencode.json` registers the server, so this session and\n116: any future one get the `lotus_*` tools:\n117: \n118: ```json\n119: {\n120:   \"mcp\": {\n121:     \"servers\": {\n122:       \"lotus\": {\n123:         \"type\": \"local\",\n124:         \"command\": [\n125:           \"C:\\\\Users\\\\terezi\\\\workdir\\\\LOTUS-v0.0.1-windows-x64\\\\bin\\\\lotus-mcp.exe\",\n126:           \"C:\\\\Users\\\\terezi\\\\workdir\\\\LOTUS-v0.0.1-windows-x64\\\\data\\\\azahar\\\\host.json\"\n127:         ]\n128:       }\n129:     }\n130:   }\n131: }\n132: ```\n133: \n134: Re-register with `opencode mcp add lotus -- <lotus-mcp.exe> <host.json>` and\n135: check with `opencode mcp list`. The host JSON at the path above is the server's\n136: whole configuration:\n137: \n138: ```json\n139: {\n140:   \"worker\": \".../runtimes/azahar/ctr-worker.exe\",\n141:   \"storage_root\": \".../data/azahar/sessions\",\n142:   \"assets\": {\"homebrew\": \".../build/kj-gold-normal/pokeheartgold.3dsx\"},\n143:   \"allow_control\": true\n144: }\n145: ```\n146: \n147: `launch.ps1 -Backend AZAHAR -Mode MCP -Fixture <3dsx>` rewrites it with absolute\n148: paths, which is the supported way to point the server at a different artifact\n149: (do not run it with `-Mode MCP` while the server is connected: it starts a\n150: second, competing stdio server).\n151: \n152: | Tool | Use |\n153: | --- | --- |\n154: | `lotus_status` | protocol, owned sessions, approved asset handles |\n155: | `lotus_create_session` | load `homebrew` (the only asset) into a new private session |\n156: | `lotus_run_until` | advance 1-600 frames, 20 host-second deadline |\n157: | `lotus_control` | `pause`, `reset`, `stop` |\n158: | `lotus_input` | complete buttons/touch state; owner `live` |\n159: | `lotus_capture` | two `lotus://artifact/...` resource links (BGRA8) |\n160: | `lotus_session_status` | frames, audio counters, last error |\n161: | `lotus_read_memory` | 1-4096 mapped bytes at a safe point |\n162: \n163: An agent driving kohjoh by hand:\n164: \n165: 1. `lotus_create_session {\"asset\": \"homebrew\"}` - note the session handle.\n166: 2. Copy the pack and manifest into\n167:    `data/azahar/sessions/<handle>/sdmc/3ds/kohjoh/data/`.\n168: 3. `lotus_control {\"session\": ..., \"operation\": \"reset\"}`.\n169: 4. `lotus_run_until` in chunks of ~60 frames; read `frames` from the reply.\n170: 5. `lotus_capture`, then read each URI from `resources/read` (base64 blob).\n171: \n172: The worker enforces four sessions, 600 frames and a 20 host-second deadline per\n173: call, and 128 retained captures; a call that hits the deadline still reports the\n174: frames it reached (`last_error: host_deadline`), so retry from that number.\n175: \n176: ## Limits and what LOTUS cannot show\n177: \n178: - **Speed**: the software renderer runs far slower than real time for kohjoh's\n179:   3D scenes; a 60-frame request can hit its 20-second deadline mid-intro. Do not\n180:   read host frame rates as guest frame rates.\n181: - **Audio**: no DSP firmware is supplied, so kohjoh logs\n182:   `audio unavailable (is the DSP firmware dumped?); continuing silent` and\n183:   `audio_samples` stays 0. Use Azahar with `sdmc/3ds/dspfirm.cdc` for anything\n184:   audio.\n185: - **No profiler**: LOTUS exposes registers and bounded memory reads only. Use\n186:   Azahar's GDB stub (`tools/azahar/gdbprof.py`) and `[perf]`/`[gamecpu]` logs\n187:   for hotspots.\n188: - **No save-state or rewind**, no breakpoints, no trace capture: re-run from\n189:   frame 0 instead.\n190: - **Guest time is fixed** (2000-01-01) and ticks start at 0, which is\n191:   reproducible but not a real console's RTC.\n192: \n193: ## Evidence so far\n194: \n195: Observed on 2026-11-16, LOTUS v0.0.1 (AZAHAR backend, worker source\n196: `05773bbb5`), artifact `build/kj-gold-normal/pokeheartgold.3dsx`\n197: (`fb0440a-dirty`, sha256 `b3b14a4d…b212ed4`) with\n198: `build/prepare-test/heartgold.pak`:\n199: \n200: - **Run (emulator)**: the guest boots to the intro and plays it. The `Failed to find title\n216:   id` line is present in both and carries no information about success.\n217: - **Not verified**: gameplay past the first-run info screen, saves, and\n218:   `KJ_SND_*`/audio behaviour (no DSP firmware in a LOTUS session). Do not add a\n219:   hardware or timing claim from any of this."

Replies echo identity, request number and epoch. Unknown fields/methods,\n25: incompatible versions, malformed/truncated/oversized frames and unexpected\n26: reply identities are rejected. A mutable client owns the single outstanding\n27: exchange. Deadlines cover writes as well as reads. On transport failure or\n28: ambiguous timeout the child is killed/reaped; mutations are never retried.\n29: Stderr remains under the supplied private root. Clean stop requires both the\n30: completion reply and successful child exit.\n31: \n32: ## Reproduction\n33: \n34: ```powershell\n35: cargo test -p lotus-protocol -p lotus-session -p lotus-cli\n36: cargo build -p lotus-cli -p lotus-session\n37: .\\target\\debug\\ctr-cli.exe mock .\\target\\debug\\lotus-mock-worker.exe\n38: ```\n39: \n40: Tests cover clean exit and second launch, four simultaneous children, sibling\n41: failure, handshake crash/hang/stale epoch, crash after handshake and framing\n42: limits. stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, encoding=\"utf-8\", bufsize=1,\n        )\n        self.next_id = 1\n        self.lines = []\n        self.lock = threading.Lock()\n        self.pending: self.notify(\"notifications/initialized\")\n        return reply\n\n    def tools(self) -> list[dict]:\n        return self.request(\"tools/list\", {}).get(\"result\", {}).get(\"tools\", [])\n\n    def call(self, name: str, args: dict, timeout: float = 300.0) -> dict:\n        return self.request(\"tools/call\", {\"name\": name, \"arguments\": args}, timeout)\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        try:\n            self.request(\"shutdown\", {}, timeout=2.0)\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n        self.proc.terminate()\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    ap = Each variant needs its own --out directory:\r\nthe game objects differ, and both programs must not share an object tree.\r\n\r\nThis is the Phase 2 harness: it compiles the game as the port compiles the\r\nSDK, builds the port's libnitro/libnitrosystem, generates the overlay table\r\nand the Wi-Fi stand-ins, and links pokeheartgold-pc/pokesoulsilver-pc\r\n(host32) or pokeheartgold-3ds.elf/pokesoulsilver-3ds.elf (3ds, through the\r\nlibctru/citro3d shell in hgss/game/app/main_3ds.c).\r\n\r\nThe source lists come from tools/game_sources.py (game src/ C/C++ and the\r\nARM9 .s data), the overlay ids and table from tools/game_overlays.py, the\r\ngenerated .naix/msg/fx headers from tools/prepare_game_headers.py, and the\r\nSDK libraries from tools/hgss_nitro.py. Nothing here writes outside --out\r\nand the generated headers under build/upstream (the decomp's build does the\r\nsame).\r\n\r\nNot every source compiles under GCC yet; --keep-going compiles what it can,\r\nprints the error count per file, then links the objects that were produced\r\nand prints the unresolved symbols. That list is the work queue for the next\r\nslice. The link targets are deliberately named -pc/-3ds.elf, not .3dsx:\r\npackaging (3dsxtool, the SMDH) is Phase 5. Exit status is 0 only when every\r\nobject compiled and the link succeeded; 1 means the run reached the link but\r\nthere were errors (the useful case).\r\n\"\"\"\r\n\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport argparse\r\nimport concurrent.futures\r\nimport datetime\r\nimport hashlib\r\nimport json\r\nimport os\r\nimport re\r\nimport shutil\r\nimport struct\r\nimport subprocess\r\nimport sys\r\nfrom pathlib import Path\r\n\r\nREPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent\r\nTOOLS = REPO / \"tools\" / \"game\"\r\nDEFAULT_ROOT = REPO / \"build\" / \"upstream\"\r\n\r\nsys.path.insert(0, str(TOOLS))\r\nimport game_sources as gs  # noqa: E402\r\nimport hgss_nitro as nitro  # noqa: E402\r\n\r\n# The libraries the game's own build compiles from lib/ but the port's\r\n# libnitro.a/libnitrosystem.a do not contain: NitroCrypto (lib/src) and the\r\n# syscall helpers (lib/syscall/src). Everything else under lib/ is either in\r\n# one of those archives, replaced by newlib (MSL_C) or stubbed\r\n# (NitroDWC/NitroWiFi/libCPS/libVCT/dsprot).\r\nGAME_LIB_PREFIXES = (\"lib/src/\", \"lib/syscall/src/\")\r\n\r\n# Port-replaced or stubbed SDK trees, and MSL_C, must not be compiled a\r\n# second time next to the archives.\r\nSKIP_LIB_PREFIXES = (\"lib/NitroSDK/\", \"lib/NitroSystem/\", \"lib/MSL_C/\",\r\n                     \"lib/NitroDWC/\", \"lib/NitroWiFi/\", \"lib/libCPS/\",\r\n                     \"lib/libVCT/\", \"lib/dsprot/\")\r\n\r\n# Objects that must not be linked into the single host/3DS program:\r\n# Metrowerks' C library data (the host libc/newlib owns errno, ctype, ...),\r\n# the stubbed Wi-Fi/DWC/CPS/VCT/dsprot libraries, and MSL's C++ runtime data\r\n# (3ds_port/nitro's port_misc.c owns the destructor chain). They are still\r\n# assembled/compiled, so the conversion is checked; the missing symbols they\r\n# would provide show up in the link's unresolved list.\r\nLINK_EXCLUDED_PREFIXES = (\"lib/MSL_C/\", \"lib/NitroDWC/\", \"lib/NitroWiFi/\",\r\n                          \"lib/libCPS/\", \"lib/libVCT/\", \"lib/dsprot/\",\r\n=== game_sources head ===\r\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\r\n\"\"\"Print the HGSS game sources as the original build lists them.\r\n\r\nUsage:\r\n    python tools/game_sources.py --root build/upstream --game-sources\r\n    python tools/game_sources.py --root build/upstream --c-sources\r\n    python tools/game_sources.py --root build/upstream --cpp-sources\r\n    python tools/game_sources.py --root build/upstream --asm-sources\r\n    python tools/game_sources.py --root build/upstream --lib-sources\r\n    python tools/game_sources.py --root build/upstream --port-lib-sources\r\n    python tools/game_sources.py --root build/upstream --overlay-map\r\n    python tools/game_sources.py --root build/upstream --json\r\n\r\nHGSS builds with make, not meson: common.mk derives the source lists from\r\nthe checkout with wildcards (src/**/*.c, src/**/*.cpp, asm/*.s, and one\r\n*.c/*.cpp wildcard per lib source directory), and main.lsf assigns every\r\nlinked object to Static main, an Autoload section, or one of the 129\r\noverlays. This tool reads those same files in --root (default\r\nbuild/upstream) so the port compiles exactly what the ROM links:\r\n\r\n* --c-sources / --cpp-sources / --game-sources: every game .c / .cpp file\r\n  under src/ (common.mk C_SRCS / CXX_SRCS).\r\n* --asm-sources: the .s data/assembly files (common.mk ASM_SRCS plus\r\n  LIB_ASM_SRCS): asm/*.s, lib/asm/*.s, lib/NitroSDK/asm/*.s,\r\n  lib/MSL_C/asm/*.s, lib/NitroDWC/asm/*.s.\r\n* --lib-sources: the lib/ C/C++ sources the ROM links (common.mk\r\n  LIB_SRC_SUBDIR plus lib/dsprot/src and lib/syscall/src, which build\r\n  separately: dsprot through its overlay, syscall as -lsyscall).\r\n* --port-lib-sources: --lib-sources minus what the port does not compile\r\n  from HGSS sources: the SDK files tools/hgss_nitro.py lists as\r\n  port-replaced, the stubbed Wi-Fi/DWC/VCT/CPS/dsprot libraries, and the\r\n  MSL_C files newlib replaces.\r\n* --overlay-map: for every object in main.lsf (Static main, Autoload ITCM,\r\n  Autoload DTCM, each Overlay), its source file in the checkout (null for\r\n  build-generated objects such as lib/dsprot's *_encrypted.o) and the\r\n  section/overlay it belongs to.\r\n* --json: the same information as JSON, for the Makefile.\r\n\r\nWith no output flag, prints --game-sources (one path per line, sorted).\r\nEach --*-sources flag prints its bare list; --overlay-map prints the\r\nmapping as text. --json overrides the text formats.\r\n\"\"\"\r\n\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport argparse\r\nimport json\r\nimport re\r\nimport sys\r\nfrom pathlib import Path\r\n"

              "content": "# sinjoh\n\nA native Nintendo 3DS source port of **Pokémon Platinum**, built for the\n**original 2011 3DS** (and 2DS) at stock clock and 64 MB application memory.\n\nSinjoh is a new runtime, not a fork of `pokeplatinum-3ds`. Its internals are\n**kohjoh's**: the HGSS Old-3DS port's single game-owned frame loop, GPU-native\n2D tile atlas, object-space retained 3D with a PICA matrix palette, baked CPU\nlighting for stable lists, decoded-ADPCM cache, and conservative pacing. The\ngame itself is the pinned `pret/pokeplatinum` decompilation, compiled for the\n3DS's ARM11 against a NitroSDK compatibility layer, exactly as kohjoh compiles\nHeartGold.\n\nThe target experience is the `pokeplatinum-3ds` remaster on hardware that\nproject does not support:\n\n- both screens filled, native-resolution 3D at 400x240 on the top screen;\n- the widened field camera and layout (25% more world at the sides);\n- the lower screen as a menu in the field;\n- crisp GPU-rendered 2D from a tile atlas;\n- WideArt bands, **precomputed at package time** so O3DS only uploads them;\n- stable 30 Hz presentation, no interpolation, no stereo, no sun shadows,\n  no 2x2 supersampling, no xBRZ.\n\nThose exclusions are deliberate. The GPU is the same 268 MHz PICA200 on both\nmodels; the New 3DS's advantage is CPU and RAM. Sinjoh spends the O3DS budget\non CPU work removed (retained geometry, atlas 2D, ADPCM cache) and keeps GPU\nwork flat.\n\n## Status\n\nFoundation. The engine is in place under `engine/`; the game source, the\nNitroSDK and NitroSystem decompilations bootstrap reproducibly; the LOTUS MCP\nharness drives windowed sessions. The game-side patch stack and the\nengine/game link are the current work (see `docs/STATUS.md`).\n\nNothing here is certified on O3DS hardware. LOTUS and Azahar are integration\ndebuggers, not timing authorities.\n\n## Layout\n\n```\nengine/        kohjoh's runtime and GPU renderer, adapted (GPL-3.0)\n  app/         entry, lifecycle, pacing\n  runtime/     the DS/3DS bridge, G3 interpreter, frame publisher\n  graphics/    g2d atlas, g3d retained geometry, textures, renderer\n  audio/       sound-chip host, mixer, ADPCM cache\n  content/     indexed data pack\n  storage/     save store\n  diagnostics/ perf ring, crash handler\ntools/\n  game/        bootstrap, source inventory, overlay map, build driver\n  lotus_mcp.py MCP client for windowed LOTUS\nwideart/       hand-drawn wide-view bands (no game pixels)\npatches/       sinjoh patch stacks (pokeplatinum, NitroSDK, NitroSystem)\ndocs/          architecture, porting plan, LOTUS findings, provenance\n```\n\n## Build\n\nPrerequisites: devkitPro (`devkitARM`, `libctru`, `citro3d`, `3dstools`,\n`picasso`) and Git for Windows on PATH ahead of MSYS2's git.\n\n```sh\npython tools/game/bootstrap.py        # pinned decomp + SDKs, apply patches\npython tools/game/platinum_game.py --target 3ds --out build/kj\n```\n\nThe user's own Platinum dump is only needed to build the data pack; no game\ndata is stored in this repository.\n\n## Provenance and licence\n\nSinjoh's own code is GPL-3.0. The engine is adapted from\n[`kohjoh`](https://github.com/estyseesghosts/kohjoh) (GPL-3.0). The game-side\ncompatibility work is derived from the patch stack of\n[`pokeplatinum-3ds`](https://github.com/GabeSud0/pokeplatinum-3ds) (GPL-3.0);\nits renderer is **not** imported. See `PROVENANCE.md` and `NOTICE.md`.\n\nNo ROM, extracted asset, save or captured game image belongs in this\nrepository or its artifacts.\n",

              "content": "# Architecture\n\nSinjoh compiles the original game for the 3DS's ARM11 and gives it a presentable\nframe, the way kohjoh does for HeartGold. The renderer never rasterizes a single\npixel on the CPU in the shipping path.\n\n## Two halves, one bridge\n\n| Half | Compiled with | Contents |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| DS side | NitroSDK types, 4-byte enums | `build/upstream` (game), `engine/runtime`, `engine/compat/nitro`, `engine/compat/nitrosystem` |\n| 3DS side | libctru/citro3d, short enums | `engine/app`, `engine/graphics`, `engine/audio`, `engine/content`, `engine/storage`, `engine/diagnostics` |\n\nThey meet only at `engine/runtime/kj_bridge.h`: fixed-width types, plain\nstructs, `kj_ds_*` implemented on the DS side and `kj_ctr_*` on the 3DS side.\nNo enums cross the line, and no NitroSDK or libctru header is included there.\nThe boundary is kohjoh's and is kept unchanged; sinjoh's work goes into what is\non each side of it.\n\n## Frame flow\n\n1. The game's own main loop runs on the main thread (`kj_game_main`).\n2. Every emulated DS V-blank (`OS_Halt`) calls `kj_ctr_vblank`: APT, input,\n   audio service, then a wait locked to the physical V-blank count. A late\n   frame does not wait, so the game never loses DS time against real-time\n   audio; a stall over 30 V-blanks resynchronises.\n3. After the V-blank callback and vwait tasks, `engine/runtime/kj_frame.c` walks\n   any H-blank effect and publishes one coherent snapshot: registers, palettes,\n   OAM, VRAM banks, per-line registers and the last swapped 3D scene.\n4. `engine/graphics/renderer.c` waits for the previous GPU frame, records both\n   screens and submits. Nothing reads DS memory after it returns. If the game\n   is two or more refreshes behind, the presentation is skipped and counted;\n   the game tick is not.\n\nThere is one frame loop: the game's. O3DS is the design floor: the program\nnever enables the New 3DS clock or L2, and it runs in the ordinary 64 MB\napplication memory mode.\n\n## 2D\n\nDS tiles are palette-expanded into a 1024x1024 RGBA5551 atlas, one DS 8x8 tile\nper PICA tile. A slot is reused only when its tile bytes are byte-identical and\nits palette version unchanged: no write tracking, no hashing of VRAM. Layers\ndraw in DS priority order, with the 3D scene at BG0's slot. Stencil bits carry\nblend-target membership and window regions; BLDY and master brightness are\nfull-screen passes. Text-BG and OBJ layers are retained when their inputs\n(registers, palette, map/OAM, ext palettes, the character bytes read) are\nbyte-identical; an unchanged screen is not redrawn or transferred.\n\nFor sinjoh this is also the 2D remaster path: the top screen's 2D is drawn on a\n320-pixel-wide logical canvas at 1.25x, not upscaled from 256x192. The class\n\"crisp 2D\" in the O3DS tier is this atlas, not a software surface.\n\n## 3D\n\n- The DS side interprets matrix stacks (20.12 fixed), texgen, and readable\n  box/position/vector tests on the CPU. NORMAL latches its transformed normal\n  and immutable lighting inputs; the PICA evaluates DS diffuse/specular,\n  shininess, ambient and emission with exact fixed-point rounding.\n- Vertices stay in object space. Each batch carries a palette of up to 16 clip\n  matrices; the 3DS side multiplies each by one fixup matrix (viewport,\n  widescreen x-scale, screen rotation, depth range) and the vertex shader\n  transforms on the GPU. Lit draws use six clip matrices to leave uniform\n  space for four lights and the shininess table; the vertex ABI stays 16 bytes.\n- The prior publish selects capture before the next scene starts, so field and\n  title producers can skip discarded geometry traversal and FIFO submission\n  while preserving game updates, animation and resource retirement.\n- Retained object-space meshes, the literal-colour baked block cache, and the\n  clip-volume side-plane cull are kohjoh's O3DS wins and are kept.\n- The box test is widened for widescreen so side content is not culled. That\n  widening is also the remaster's \"wider view\" for Platinum.\n\nNot implemented yet, and counted rather than silently dropped: fog, toon\nhighlight, edge marking, shadow volumes, wireframe, display capture, bitmap\nBGs. The O3DS tier excludes sun shadows, edge marking, stereo, interpolation\nand xBRZ by design.\n\n## Audio, content, storage\n\n- The vendored ARM7 sequencer and DS sound chip mix 32768 Hz stereo on an\n  audio thread (core 0, above the game), fed by NDSP. The decoded-ADPCM cache\n  is kohjoh's `adpcmClean` cache: voices whose decoder state comes from data\n  alone are decoded once.\n- The data pack is an indexed, versioned file keyed by original game file IDs.\n  The renderer, game and pack never know whether the pack is on SD or in RomFS.\n- Saves are two-generation raw payloads with a checked header, on SD for the\n  `.3dsx` and in the title archive for a `.cia`.\n\n## Remaster feature map\n\n| Feature | Where it lives | O3DS cost |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Both screens filled | renderer viewports (2D 1.25x, 3D native 400x240) | flat |\n| Native-resolution 3D | g3d fixup + 400-wide targets | flat (GPU bound) |\n| Wider field view | g3d fixup x-scale + widened box test | few CPU tests |\n| Lower-screen menu | sinjoh game glue (`menu/`), not the renderer | 2D only |\n| Crisp 2D | g2d atlas | replaces software drawer |\n| WideArt | package-time bands loaded as textures | upload once |\n| Stable 30 Hz | pacing in `app/main.c`, present skip | measurement |\n| Pixel-perfect overworld | layout mode in the game glue | optional |\n\nExcluded on O3DS: 60 FPS interpolation, stereo, smooth3d 2x2, sun shadows,\nedge marking, xBRZ, full WideArt packs. The layout uses the reduced wide\ncanvas; WideArt bands are precomputed, not synthesized per frame.\n\n## What is deliberately different from pokeplatinum-3ds\n\n- No CPU transform/light/clip of 3D scenes, no software 2D rasterizer, no\n  GPU-to-CPU readback, no per-frame compositor upload.\n- No N3DS thread topology. The game owns the main thread; audio is the only\n  worker. Core 1 is treated as a shared system core, not a second full core.\n- No interpolation path to satisfy: the O3DS tier is 30 Hz by contract.\n- The patch stack is re-derived against the `kj_*` bridge instead of carrying\n  a second renderer's `NitroPort_*` API.\n",
