              "content": "# LOTUS v0.0.2: what works, what does not\n\nVerified 2026-11-16 against `LOTUS-v0.0.2-windows-x64` on Windows 11, worker\nsources pinned in the release's `runtimes/*/build-manifest.json`\n(AZAHAR `5a3c702f…`, CITnLO `6361ddc3…`).\n\n## MCP works, windowed or headless\n\nBoth launchers serve the same MCP tools:\n`lotus_status`, `lotus_create_session`, `lotus_load`, `lotus_control`,\n`lotus_run_until` (1-600 frames), `lotus_input`, `lotus_capture`,\n`lotus_session_status`, `lotus_read_memory`, `lotus_registers`,\n`lotus_debug`, `lotus_focus_session`, `lotus_list_cards`,\n`lotus_list_sessions`, `lotus_gdb`, `lotus_trace`,\n`lotus_validate_scenario`.\n\n`lotus_focus_session` is what makes a run watchable: the window shows that\nsession while the harness drives it. `tools/lotus_mcp.py` is a small stdio\nclient used for exactly this.\n\n```sh\n# Rewrite host.json for the windowed AZAHAR worker and approve a fixture.\npowershell -File launch.ps1 -Backend AZAHAR -Mode Desktop -Fixture app.3dsx -ConfigureOnly\n\n# Drive it from a script while the window shows the focused session.\npython tools/lotus_mcp.py --config <lotus>/data/azahar/host.json status\npython tools/lotus_mcp.py --config <lotus>/data/azahar/host.json \\\n    call lotus_create_session '{\"asset\":\"homebrew\",\"kind\":\"secondary\"}'\n```\n\nA session handle expires when the MCP server exits. A `secondary` card is\ndisposable; a `primary` card persists. Sessions can run in parallel (the\nworker limit is four), which is why renderer speed matters here.\n\n## Vulkan cannot be forced in v0.0.2\n\nThe worker binaries are built with `-DENABLE_VULKAN=ON` and\n`-DENABLE_SOFTWARE_RENDERER=ON`, and the worker reports\n`worker supports software and Vulkan`. The frontend still pins the session\nprofile:\n\n- `native-manifest.json` records\n  `\"backend\": \"azahar_native_software\"` and\n  `\"profile\": \"old3ds/software/hle/dsp-muted/ticks-0/time-2000-01-01\"`\n  for every session, before and after any setting change.\n- The only renderer-like setting exposed over MCP is `graphics_api`\n  (`choices [0, 1, 2]`). Its consumer source is\n  `src/core/rpc/rpc_server.cpp:170` - the capture RPC - not\n  `src/core/frontend/emu_window.cpp`. Setting it to 1 is rejected with\n  `InvalidArgument: worker supports software and Vulkan`; 0 and 2 are accepted\n  and both still produce the `azahar_native_software` backend.\n- The pinned profile string in `lotus-desktop.exe`/`lotus-mcp.exe` contains\n  only `old3ds/software`.\n\nSo the portable v0.0.2 release cannot switch its worker to Vulkan without\nrebuilding the worker from its integration branch. That is out of scope for\nthis repository.\n\nConsequence for sinjoh:\n\n- **Vulkan and visual/performance observation:** vanilla Azahar\n  (`C:\\Program Files\\Azahar\\azahar.exe`), windowed, `graphics_api = Vulkan`.\n  This is the only accelerated renderer available on this machine.\n- **Deterministic frame-driven runs and parallel sessions:** LOTUS over MCP,\n  accepting that it is software and therefore slow. Use short frame counts\n  and bound each request to the 600-frame limit.\n\n## Guest layout\n\nA session root is `data/<backend>/sessions/<handle>/` (`scratch/<handle>/`\nalso appears); `sdmc/` maps to `sdmc:/`. For sinjoh the expected paths are:\n\n```\nsdmc:/3ds/sinjoh/data/platinum.pak\nsdmc:/3ds/sinjoh/data/platinum.manifest.json\nsdmc:/3ds/sinjoh/saves/platinum.sav\nsdmc:/3ds/sinjoh/script.txt\nsdmc:/3ds/sinjoh/logs/sinjoh.log\n```\n\nA session created with an asset loads it paused, so pack staging is:\ncreate, copy pack/manifest into `sdmc/`, `reset`, then run.\n\n## Not authoritative\n\nNeither LOTUS nor Azahar certifies O3DS timing. LOTUS's software renderer is far\nslower than the console; Azahar charges nothing for PICA vertex work. `[perf]`\ncounters and instruction counts rank changes; hardware claims need hardware.\n",

              "content": "# Porting plan\n\nThe order is chosen so each milestone is provable before the next one depends\non it. \"Built\" and \"runs\" and \"verified in an emulator\" are separate claims.\n\n## M0 - foundation (done)\n\n- New tree, provenance, licence.\n- Pinned `pret/pokeplatinum` at `c248fb3`, plus the NitroSDK and NitroSystem\n  decompilations at the revisions in its `subprojects/*.wrap`.\n- `tools/game/bootstrap.py` reproduces the checkout on Windows.\n- Engine imported from kohjoh under `engine/`.\n- LOTUS MCP harness and its renderer limits documented.\n\nAcceptance: `python tools/game/bootstrap.py` prints the three checkouts and\n`build/upstream/platinum.us/main.lsf` exists.\n\n## M1 - source inventory and overlay map\n\n- Enumerate the game's C/C++/asm sources from the decomp's meson files, not a\n  glob, so conditional and excluded sources are visible.\n- Read `platinum.us/main.lsf` for every object's link section and every\n  overlay's ID, region and `After` chain.\n- Emit the same tables kohjoh's build driver needs (`overlay.map`,\n  `overlay_ids.ld`, `overlay_table.c`).\n\nAcceptance: every object in `main.lsf` maps to a source or is marked\nbuild-generated; the overlay table lists 122 overlays in link order; no\nduplicate object assignment.\n\n## M2 - game-side compatibility stack\n\n- Adapt the compiler/ABI/correctness patches from pokeplatinum-3ds's patch\n  stack against this decomp pin. These are independent of the renderer:\n  Metrowerks-to-GCC type widths, static/const mismatches, MSL runtime, overlay\n  static initializers, CRC and math helpers.\n- Port kohjoh's NitroSDK/NitroSystem compatibility implementation to the APIs\n  pokeplatinum actually calls. The bridge stays `kj_*`; no `NitroPort_*` layer\n  is introduced.\n- Implement the game entry (`kj_boot.c` analogue): cartridge/firmware state,\n  file system IDs, overlay loader, save chip, RTC.\n\nAcceptance: the game compiles with no errors and links; the host32 build\n(`TARGET=host32`) runs its first frames headless and logs a boot.\n\n## M3 - boot on 3DS with 2D only\n\n- Build the data pack from the user's own Platinum dump.\n- Render engine B (bottom) and engine A (top) through the atlas path.\n- Boot the Game Freak logo, title, and the first field map in LOTUS.\n- 3D scenes are counted as unsupported until M4; no CPU rasterizer is added.\n\nAcceptance: windowed LOTUS shows the boot sequence and a field 2D frame; the\nlog names the pack and the renderer; unsupported 3D counts are non-zero and\nreported, not hidden.\n\n## M4 - retained 3D\n\n- Feed the game's G3 FIFO through `engine/runtime/kj_g3.c`.\n- Retained object-space batches, 16-entry matrix palette, baked literal\n  colours, clip-volume cull, PICA lighting only for lists that cannot bake.\n- Native 400x240 top screen and the widened camera/box test.\n\nAcceptance: field and battle 3D draw; held frames match the reference in the\nDS 256x192 region; unsupported material modes are counted.\n\n## M5 - audio, save, input\n\n- DS sound chip host and decoded-ADPCM cache on the audio thread.\n- Two-generation save store; raw 512 KiB payload import/export.\n- Input and touch, APT suspend/resume.\n\nAcceptance: 30 minutes of music/effects without dropouts; 20 save/load cycles;\nHOME/sleep/return.\n\n## M6 - remaster features\n\n- Lower-screen field menu implemented in sinjoh's game glue.\n- Wide camera layout for the field, 2D wide canvas, health-box/window geometry.\n- WideArt: package-time band generation, runtime upload only. The reasoning, provenance and exclusions are in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/PORTING.md`, `PROVENANCE.md`.\n\n## LOTUS\n\nI drove it over MCP, windowed. `tools/lotus_mcp.py` speaks the stdio protocol; `lotus_focus_session` puts the session in the window so you can watch it.       "summary": "## Objective\n- Bootstrap an entirely new native 3DS source port of Pokémon Platinum (\"sinjoh-platinum\") for the original 2011 3DS, built on kohjoh's internals and replicating pokeplatinum-3ds's remaster enhancements, including WideArt precomputed at package time.\n\n## Requirements\n- Target O3DS (2011 3DS/2DS), stock clock, 64 MB app memory; do not optimize for New 3DS.\n- Base on kohjoh's \"more sane internals\", not a fork of pokeplatinum-3ds; quality over speed is acceptable.\n- Include all pokeplatinum-3ds remaster features that fit O3DS; ignore Diamond/Pearl variants.\n- Test using LOTUS v0.0.2 windowed, with Vulkan if possible; vanilla Azahar permitted if LOTUS fails.\n- Drive LOTUS over MCP; parallel sessions matter, so software rendering is painfully slow.\n- Read project/reference docs before writing code; use vanilla Azahar for Vulkan and LOTUS MCP for deterministic software runs.\n\n## Work State\n### Completed\n- Created sinjoh repo tree with `engine/` copied from kohjoh `src/`; docs: `README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/PORTING.md`, `docs/LOTUS.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `PROVENANCE.md`, `NOTICE.md`, `.gitignore`; generated overlay IDs/table skeleton (122 overlays, `dummy1`..`dw_warp`, 0..121).\n- Wrote `tools/lotus_mcp.py`; drove windowed LOTUS over MCP: create/focus/load/run 60 frames/settings/stop.\n- Two commits: `d98dba7` (kohjoh-based start), `a636567` (inventory + overlay table). Working tree clean, not pushed.\n\n### Active\n- M2: writing `patches/pokeplatinum`, `patches/NitroSDK`, `patches/NitroSystem` and porting NitroSDK/NitroSystem compat to the `kj_*` bridge.\n\n### Blocked\n- No sinjoh build/boot yet; game-side patch stack and engine/game link do not exist.\n- LOTUS Vulkan unavailable in v0.0.2 (worker profile pinned to `old3ds/software`); needs vanilla Azahar for Vulkan.\n\n## Next Move\n1.                 "text": "# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n# Settings shared by everything the port compiles from Nintendo's and the\r\n# decompilation's C: libnitro (NitroSDK), libnitrosystem (NitroSystem) and,\r\n# later, the game. Included by those Makefiles; not run on its own.\r\n#\r\n# Defines, for the including Makefile:\r\n#   TARGET       host (PC, for tests), host32 (32-bit PC, for tests that need\r\n#                the 3DS's 4-byte pointers) or 3ds (default: host)\r\n#   IS_HOST      yes for host and host32\r\n#   ROOT         repository root\r\n#   SDK, NNS     build/NitroSDK, build/NitroSystem (fetched by tools/bootstrap.py)\r\n#   CC, AR, NM, OBJCOPY  the toolchain for TARGET\r\n#   PORT_CFLAGS  flags every file is compiled with\r\n#   SDK_INCLUDES include paths for NitroSDK (and the libnitro port headers)\r\n#   NNS_INCLUDES include paths for NitroSystem\r\n#   LDFLAGS      link flags for test programs (host only)\r\n#   NNS_INLINE_SYMS  NitroSystem's header inline functions (built by\r\n#                3ds_port/nitrosystem); every object that includes NitroSystem\r\n#                headers must be passed through $(WEAKEN_NNS_INLINE)\r\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\nTARGET ?= host\r\nROOT   := $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST)))..)\r\nSDK    := $(ROOT)/build/NitroSDK\r\nNNS    := $(ROOT)/build/NitroSystem\r\nNITRO  := $(ROOT)/3ds_port/nitro\r\n\r\nifeq ($(wildcard $(SDK)/include/nitro.h),)\r\n$(error NitroSDK not found at $(SDK). Run: python tools/bootstrap.py)\r\nendif\r\n\r\n# The same SDK configuration pokeplatinum builds with, minus the Metrowerks\r\n# compiler (SDK_CW), plus SDK_PORT_3DS which turns on our patches.\r\nPORT_DEFINES := -DSDK_ARM9 -DSDK_TS -DSDK_4M -DSDK_CODE_ARM -DSDK_FINALROM \\\r\n                -DNNS_FINALROM -DSDK_PORT_3DS\r\n\r\n# Matching how Metrowerks compiled the originals:\r\n#   gnu89 inline rules match how the SDK's .c files use `inline`.\r\n#   No strict aliasing: the SDK reinterprets memory through casts on purpose.\r\n#   Enums are always 4 bytes (\"-enum int\"); ARM GCC would otherwise shrink\r\n#   them and break structure layouts.\r\n#   char is signed (\"-char signed\"); on ARM, GCC's char is unsigned by\r\n#   default, which silently changes comparisons like `c < 0`.\r\n#   Overflow, out-of-range indexes and null pointers do what the DS's code\r\n#   did: signed arithmetic wraps, and GCC doesn't drop loop iterations or\r\n#   null checks on the grounds that the code can't rely on them. Metrowerks\r\n#   made no such assumptions, and the game has places that would be\r\n#   affected (GCC warns about a few loops in battle_lib.c).\r\nPORT_CFLAGS := -std=gnu99 -fgnu89-inline -fno-strict-aliasing -fno-short-enums \\\r\n               -fsigned-char -fwrapv -fno-aggressive-loop-optimizations \\\r\n               -fno-delete-null-pointer-checks -O2 -g \\\r\n               -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Wno-unused-variable -Wno-missing-braces \\\r\n               -Wno-unknown-pragmas -Wno-unused-but-set-variable -Wno-parentheses \\\r\n               -Wno-switch -Wno-multichar \\\r\n               $(PORT_DEFINES)\r\n\r\n# Not wl_arm7's headers: that's the ARM7's wireless library, which no ARM9\r\n# code uses, and its System.h and Font.h would stand in for the game's\r\n# system.h and font.h on Windows, where file names ignore case.\r\nSDK_INCLUDES := -I$(NITRO)/include -I$(NITRO)/build/$(TARGET)/gen -I$(SDK)/include \\\r\n                $(foreach d,$(filter-out %/wl_arm7/include,$(wildcard $(SDK)/libraries/*/include)),-I$(d))\r\nNNS_INCLUDES := -I$(NNS)/include \\\r\n                $(foreach d,$(wildcard $(NNS)/libraries/*/include),-I$(d))\r\n\r\nifeq ($(TARGET),3ds)\r\n  ifeq ($(strip $(DEVKITARM)),)\r\n    $(error Set DEVKITARM (install devkitPro with 3ds-dev))\r\n  endif\r\n  PREFIX := $(DEVKITARM)/bin/arm-none-eabi-\r\n  CC     := $(PREFIX)gcc\r\n  AR     := $(PREFIX)gcc-ar\r\n  NM     := $(PREFIX)nm\r\n  OBJCOPY := $(PREFIX)objcopy\r\n  # The 3DS's ARM11 MPCore, with its VFP floating-point unit.\r\n  PORT_CFLAGS += -march=armv6k -mtune=mpcore -mfpu=vfp -mfloat-abi=hard -mtp=soft \\\r\n                 -mword-relocations -ffunction-sections -D__3DS__\r\nelse ifneq ($(filter host host32,$(TARGET)),)\r\n  IS_HOST := yes\r\n  CC     ?= cc\r\n  AR     ?= ar\r\n=== port dirs ===\r\n3ds_port\\game\r\n3ds_port\\nitro\r\n3ds_port\\nitrosystem\r\n3ds_port\\pak\r\n3ds_port\\game\\app\r\n3ds_port\\game\\cia\r\n3ds_port\\game\\forwarder\r\n3ds_port\\game\\include\r\n3ds_port\\game\\tests\r\n3ds_port\\nitro\\include\r\n3ds_port\\nitro\\src\r\n3ds_port\\nitro\\tests\r\n3ds_port\\nitro\\third_party\r\n3ds_port\\nitro\\src\\platform\r\n3ds_port\\nitrosystem\\tests\r\n3ds_port\\pak\\include\r\n3ds_port\\pak\\src\r\n3ds_port\\pak\\tests\r\n"
              }

                "type": "text",
                "text": "\r\n\u001b[32;1mCount\u001b[0m\r\n\u001b[32;1m-----\u001b[0m\r\n  124\r\n=== diff kohjoh vs p3ds NitroSDK 0001 ===\r\nFrom bf2112354b815301c22741518b84c0e62e0461e3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001\r\nFrom: pokeheartgold-3ds <bootstrap@invalid>\r\nDate: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 03:32:18 +0000\r\nSubject: [PATCH] sdk: port hooks for IRQ flag clear, software DMA and matrix\r\n result sync (SDK_PORT_3DS)\r\n\r\nThree SDK_PORT_3DS edits in lib/NitroSDK/src, each reproducing a DS behaviour\r\nthe port cannot get from its plain memory. Every new line is under\r\n#ifdef SDK_PORT_3DS, and the DS build's preprocessed output is unchanged\r\n(gcc -E -P of each touched file, with and without -DSDK_ARM9, identical to HEAD).\r\nPorted from pokeplatinum-3ds NitroSDK patches 0017, 0009 and 0026, rebased onto\r\nHGSS's sources. Differences from Platinum are noted per part.\r\n\r\n(a) IRQ requests are cleared by bits, not by storing a mask (Platinum 0017)\r\n    The DS's IF is write-1-to-clear: a store of a mask clears the bits set in\r\n    it and leaves the rest. In the port IF is plain memory, so a store would\r\n    set the bits of the mask and drop every other pending request.\r\n    - os/os_interrupt.c:115-121 OS_ResetRequestIrqMask: reg_OS_IF &= ~newMask.\r\n    - os/os_tick.c:64-68 OS_SetTick: reg_OS_IF &= ~OSi_TICK_IE_TIMER.\r\n    No other write to reg_OS_IF exists in lib/NitroSDK/src (checked). Platinum's\r\n    patch matches these two sites; HGSS names the parameter newMask.\r\n\r\n(b) DMA register writes start the port's software DMA (Platinum 0009)\r\n    NitroPort_DmaStart runs the transfer and clears the busy bit. The hook is\r\n    called once per control-register write, after the write:\r\n    - mi/mi_dma.c:19-21 MIi_DmaSetParams (covers MI_DmaCopy32Async, MI_HBlank*,\r\n      MIi_CardDmaCopy32, MI_SendGXCommand and the async GX path, which all write\r\n      through it), :52-54 MIi_DmaSetParams_wait (MI_DmaCopy32, MI_DmaCopy16),\r\n      :62-64 MIi_DmaSetParams_noInt, :98-100 MIi_DmaSetParams_wait_noInt\r\n      (MI_DmaFill32, MI_DmaFill32Async, via the static inline wrappers in\r\n      mi/dma.h), and :234-236 MI_StopDma.\r\n    - The channel-0 dummy transfer (if (!dmaNo) writing 0x81400001) is not\r\n      written under the port: at :39-50, :81-96, :191-200 and :221-232.\r\n      Platinum keeps it. On the port it would replace the real transfer's\r\n      registers before the start (lost DMA0 copies in the _wait variants) and\r\n      leave channel 0 busy in MI_WaitDma with nothing to clear it. HGSS has no\r\n      MIi_DUMMY_DMA_NO macro; the inline dummy is the equivalent Platinum\r\n      guards in its header.\r\n    - MI_WaitDma (:186) gets no start: under the port it writes no control\r\n      register. MI_StopDma's start is a no-op (it just cleared ENABLE); it is\r\n\r\n"

                "type": "text",
                "text": "From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001\r\nFrom: pokeplatinum-3ds <noreply@users.noreply.github.com>\r\nDate: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 12:38:06 -0700\r\nSubject: [PATCH] Tell the port when the V-blank work is done (SDK_PORT_3DS)\r\n\r\nAfter V-blank the game updates the display for the next picture: screen\r\nfades, the V-blank callback (OAM, palettes, VRAM transfers, BG updates)\r\nand the post-V-blank tasks. On the DS all of that happens before the\r\nscreen starts drawing the picture. The port draws the screens on other\r\nthreads, so it needs to know when the game is done: NitroPort_VBlankWorkDone\r\nafter the main loop's V-blank work, and after WaitFrame's.\r\n---\r\n src/main.c | 16 ++++++++++++++++\r\n 1 file changed, 16 insertions(+)\r\n\r\ndiff --git a/src/main.c b/src/main.c\r\n--- a/src/main.c\r\n+++ b/src/main.c\r\n@@ -35,6 +35,16 @@\r\n \r\n #define RESET_COMBO (PAD_BUTTON_START | PAD_BUTTON_SELECT | PAD_BUTTON_L | PAD_BUTTON_R)\r\n \r\n+#ifdef SDK_PORT_3DS\r\n+// The port draws the screens on other threads (other CPU cores on a 3DS),\r\n+// from the registers, palettes, OAM and VRAM as they are. After V-blank the\r\n+// game changes them all for the next picture (the V-blank callback, screen\r\n+// fades, the post-V-blank tasks); on the DS that happens before the screen\r\n+// starts drawing it. This tells the port when it's done, so a screen isn't\r\n+// drawn halfway through (3ds_port/nitro/include/nitro_port.h).\r\n+extern void NitroPort_VBlankWorkDone(void);\r\n+#endif\r\n+\r\n FS_EXTERN_OVERLAY(game_start);\r\n FS_EXTERN_OVERLAY(game_opening);\r\n \r\n@@ -158,6 +168,9 @@ void NitroMain(void)\r\n \r\n         SoundSystem_Tick();\r\n         SysTaskManager_ExecuteTasks(gSystem.postVBlankTaskMgr);\r\n+#ifdef SDK_PORT_3DS\r\n+        NitroPort_VBlankWorkDone();\r\n+#endif\r\n     }\r\n }\r\n \r\n@@ -216,6 +229,9 @@ static void WaitFrame(void)\r\n     if (gSystem.vblankCallback != NULL) {\r\n         gSystem.vblankCallback(gSystem.vblankCallbackData);\r\n     }\r\n+#ifdef SDK_PORT_3DS\r\n+    NitroPort_VBlankWorkDone();\r\n+#endif\r\n }\r\n \r\n static void TrySystemReset(enum OSResetParameter resetParam)\r\n-- \r\n2.43.0\r\n\r\n=== 0012 ===\r\nFrom 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001\r\nFrom: pokeplatinum-3ds <noreply@users.noreply.github.com>\r\nDate: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 02:00:00 -0700\r\nSubject: [PATCH] Tell the port where the game's windows are (SDK_PORT_3DS)\r\n\r\nThe 3DS remaster draws the upper screen wider than the DS's and moves the\r\ngame's windows (text boxes, menus, the place name sign) to the nearer edge\r\nof it. Window_Add, Window_Remove and Windows_Delete tell the port\r\n(NitroPort_WindowAdded/NitroPort_WindowRemoved) which BG a window is on and\r\nwhere.\r\n---\r\n src/bg_window.c | 18 ++++++++++++++++++\r\n 1 file changed, 18 insertions(+)\r\n\r\ndiff --git a/src/bg_window.c b/src/bg_window.c\r\nindex bd3dd8ff..dc6e78d7 100644\r\n--- a/src/bg_window.c\r\n+++ b/src/bg_window.c\r\n@@ -5,6 +5,15 @@\r\n \r\n #include \"constants/graphics.h\"\r\n \r\n+#ifdef SDK_PORT_3DS\r\n+// The 3DS remaster draws the upper screen wider than the DS's, and moves the\r\n+// game's windows (text boxes, menus, the place name sign) to the nearer\r\n+// edge of it: it needs to know where they are on their BG\r\n+// (3ds_port/nitro/include/nitro_port_wide.h).\r\n+extern void NitroPort_WindowAdded(const void *window, int bgLayer, int left, int top, int width, int height);\r\n+extern void NitroPort_WindowRemoved(const void *window);\r\n+#endif\r\n+\r\n #include \"gx_layers.h\"\r\n #include \"heap.h\"\r\n #include \"math_util.h\"\r\n@@ -1639,6 +1648,9 @@ void Window_Add(BgConfig *bgConfig, Window *window, u8 bgLayer, u8 tilemapLeft,\r\n     window->baseTile = baseTile;\r\n     window->pixels = pixels;\r\n     window->colorMode = (bgConfig->bgs[bgLayer].colorMode == GX_BG_COLORMODE_16) ? BG_COLOR_MODE_4BPP : BG_COLOR_MODE_8BPP;\r\n+#ifdef SDK_PORT_3DS\r\n+    NitroPort_WindowAdded(window, bgLayer, tilemapLeft, tilemapTop, width, height);\r\n+#endif\r\n }\r\n \r\n void Window_AddToTopLeftCorner(BgConfig *bgConfig, Window *window, u8 width, u8 height, u16 baseTile, u8 fillVal)\r\n@@ -1676,6 +1688,9 @@ void Window_AddFromTemplate(BgConfig *bgConfig, Window *window, const WindowTemp\r\n \r\n void Window_Remove(Window *window)\r\n {\r\n+#ifdef SDK_PORT_3DS\r\n+    NitroPort_WindowRemoved(window);\r\n+#endif\r\n     Heap_Free(window->pixels);\r\n \r\n     window->bgConfig = NULL;\r\n@@ -1692,6 +1707,9 @@ void Window_Remove(Window *window)\r\n void Windows_Delete(Window *window, u8 winCount)\r\n {\r\n     for (u16 i = 0; i < winCount; i++) {\r\n+#ifdef SDK_PORT_3DS\r\n+        NitroPort_WindowRemoved(&window[i]);\r\n"

                "text": "# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n# Settings shared by everything the port compiles from Nintendo's and the\r\n# decompilation's C: libnitro (NitroSDK), libnitrosystem (NitroSystem) and,\r\n# later, the game. Included by those Makefiles; not run on its own.\r\n#\r\n# Defines, for the including Makefile:\r\n#   TARGET       host (PC, for tests), host32 (32-bit PC, for tests that need\r\n#                the 3DS's 4-byte pointers) or 3ds (default: host)\r\n#   IS_HOST      yes for host and host32\r\n#   ROOT         repository root\r\n#   SDK, NNS     build/NitroSDK, build/NitroSystem (fetched by tools/bootstrap.py)\r\n#   CC, AR, NM, OBJCOPY  the toolchain for TARGET\r\n#   PORT_CFLAGS  flags every file is compiled with\r\n#   SDK_INCLUDES include paths for NitroSDK (and the libnitro port headers)\r\n#   NNS_INCLUDES include paths for NitroSystem\r\n#   LDFLAGS      link flags for test programs (host only)\r\n#   NNS_INLINE_SYMS  NitroSystem's header inline functions (built by\r\n#                3ds_port/nitrosystem); every object that includes NitroSystem\r\n#                headers must be passed through $(WEAKEN_NNS_INLINE)\r\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\nTARGET ?= host\r\nROOT   := $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST)))../..)\r\nSDK    := $(ROOT)/build/NitroSDK\r\nNNS    := $(ROOT)/build/NitroSystem\r\nNITRO  := $(ROOT)/src/compat/nitro\r\n\r\nifeq ($(wildcard $(SDK)/include/nitro.h),)\r\n$(error NitroSDK not found at $(SDK). Run: python tools/bootstrap.py)\r\nendif\r\n\r\n# The same SDK configuration pokeplatinum builds with, minus the Metrowerks\r\n# compiler (SDK_CW), plus SDK_PORT_3DS which turns on our patches.\r\nPORT_DEFINES := -DSDK_ARM9 -DSDK_TS -DSDK_4M -DSDK_CODE_ARM -DSDK_FINALROM \\\r\n                -DNNS_FINALROM -DSDK_PORT_3DS\r\n\r\n# Matching how Metrowerks compiled the originals:\r\n#   gnu89 inline rules match how the SDK's .c files use `inline`.\r\n#   No strict aliasing: the SDK reinterprets memory through casts on purpose.\r\n#   Enums are always 4 bytes (\"-enum int\"); ARM GCC would otherwise shrink\r\n#   them and break structure layouts.\r\n#   char is signed (\"-char signed\"); on ARM, GCC's char is unsigned by\r\n#   default, which silently changes comparisons like `c < 0`.\r\n#   Overflow, out-of-range indexes and null pointers do what the DS's code\r\n#   did: signed arithmetic wraps, and GCC doesn't drop loop iterations or\r\n#   null checks on the grounds that the code can't rely on them. Metrowerks\r\n#   made no such assumptions, and the game has places that would be\r\n#   affected (GCC warns about a few loops in battle_lib.c).\r\nPORT_CFLAGS := -std=gnu99 -fgnu89-inline -fno-strict-aliasing -fno-short-enums \\\r\n               -fsigned-char -fwrapv -fno-aggressive-loop-optimizations \\\r\n               -fno-delete-null-pointer-checks -O2 -g \\\r\n               -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Wno-unused-variable -Wno-missing-braces \\\r\n               -Wno-unknown-pragmas -Wno-unused-but-set-variable -Wno-parentheses \\\r\n               -Wno-switch -Wno-multichar \\\r\n               $(PORT_DEFINES)\r\n\r\n# Not wl_arm7's headers: that's the ARM7's wireless library, which no ARM9\r\n# code uses, and its System.h and Font.h would stand in for the game's\r\n# system.h and font.h on Windows, where file names ignore case.\r\nSDK_INCLUDES := -I$(NITRO)/include -I$(NITRO)/build/$(TARGET)/gen -I$(SDK)/include \\\r\n                $(foreach d,$(filter-out %/wl_arm7/include,$(wildcard $(SDK)/libraries/*/include)),-I$(d))\r\nNNS_INCLUDES := -I$(NNS)/include \\\r\n                $(foreach d,$(wildcard $(NNS)/libraries/*/include),-I$(d))\r\n\r\nifeq ($(TARGET),3ds)\r\n  ifeq ($(strip $(DEVKITARM)),)\r\n    $(error Set DEVKITARM (install devkitPro with 3ds-dev))\r\n  endif\r\n  PREFIX := $(DEVKITARM)/bin/arm-none-eabi-\r\n  CC     := $(PREFIX)gcc\r\n  AR     := $(PREFIX)gcc-ar\r\n  NM     := $(PREFIX)nm\r\n  OBJCOPY := $(PREFIX)objcopy\r\n  # The 3DS's ARM11 MPCore, with its VFP floating-point unit.\r\n  PORT_CFLAGS += -march=armv6k -mtune=mpcore -mfpu=vfp -mfloat-abi=hard -mtp=soft \\\r\n                 -mword-relocations -ffunction-sections -D__3DS__\r\nelse ifneq ($(filter host host32,$(TARGET)),)\r\n  IS_HOST := yes\r\n  CC     ?= cc\r\n  AR     ?= ar\r\n  NM     ?= nm\r\n  OBJCOPY ?= objcopy\r\n  # The SDK stores addresses in 32-bit integers. On a 64-bit PC that only\r\n  # works if our data sits below 4 GB, which a non-PIE executable guarantees.\r\n  PORT_CFLAGS += -fno-pie -Wno-pointer-to-int-cast -Wno-int-to-pointer-cast\r\n  # -pthread: the port's threads are POSIX threads on a PC (nitro/src/platform/host.c).\r\n  LDFLAGS += -no-pie -pthread\r\n  ifeq ($(TARGET),host32)\r\n    # Nintendo's file formats hold 4-byte pointers that the libraries fix up\r\n    # in place, so those parts only work with 32-bit pointers, as on the 3DS.\r\n    # -malign-double aligns 64-bit values to 8 bytes like ARM (x86 uses 4).\r\n    # Needs 32-bit C libraries (Ubuntu: gcc-multilib).\r\n    PORT_CFLAGS += -m32 -malign-double\r\n    LDFLAGS += -m32\r\n  endif\r\nelse\r\n  $(error TARGET must be host, host32 or 3ds)\r\nendif\r\n\r\n# NitroSystem's headers define small functions as plain `inline`. Metrowerks\r\n# kept one copy of each; GCC exports one from every file that includes the\r\n# header, and those files then can't be linked together. Metrowerks\r\n#   made no such assumptions, and the game has places that would be\r\n#   affected (GCC warns about a few loops in battle_lib.c).\r\nPORT_CFLAGS := -std=gnu99 -fgnu89-inline -fno-strict-aliasing -fno-short-enums \\\r\n               -fsigned-char -fwrapv -fno-aggressive-loop-optimizations \\\r\n               -fno-delete-null-pointer-checks -O2 -g \\\r\n               -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Wno-unused-variable -Wno-missing-braces \\\r\n               -Wno-unknown-pragmas -Wno-unused-but-set-variable -Wno-parentheses \\\r\n               -Wno-switch -Wno-multichar \\\r\n               $(PORT_DEFINES)\r\n\r\n# Not wl_arm7's headers: that's the ARM7's wireless library, which no ARM9\r\n# code uses, and its System.h and Font.h would stand in for the game's\r\n# system.h and font.h on Windows, where file names ignore case.\r\nSDK_INCLUDES := -I$(NITRO)/include -I$(NITRO)/build/$(TARGET)/gen -I$(SDK)/include \\\r\n                $(foreach d,$(filter-out %/wl_arm7/include,$(wildcard $(SDK)/libraries/*/include)),-I$(d))\r\nNNS_INCLUDES := -I$(NNS)/include \\\r\n                $(foreach d,$(wildcard $(NNS)/libraries/*/include),-I$(d))\r\n\r\nifeq ($(TARGET),3ds)\r\n  ifeq ($(strip $(DEVKITARM)),)\r\n    $(error Set DEVKITARM (install devkitPro with 3ds-dev))\r\n  endif\r\n  PREFIX := $(DEVKITARM)/bin/arm-none-eabi-\r\n  CC     := $(PREFIX)gcc\r\n  AR     := $(PREFIX)gcc-ar\r\n  NM     := $(PREFIX)nm\r\n  OBJCOPY := $(PREFIX)objcopy\r\n  # The 3DS's ARM11 MPCore, with its VFP floating-point unit.\r\n  PORT_CFLAGS += -march=armv6k -mtune=mpcore -mfpu=vfp -mfloat-abi=hard -mtp=soft \\\r\n                 -mword-relocations -ffunction-sections -D__3DS__\r\nelse ifneq ($(filter host host32,$(TARGET)),)\r\n  IS_HOST := yes\r\n  CC     ?= cc\r\n  AR     ?= ar\r\n  NM     ?= nm\r\n  OBJCOPY ?= objcopy\r\n  # The SDK stores addresses in 32-bit integers. build the library for the 3DS's ARM11 (needs devkitARM)\r\n#   make clean\r\n#\r\n# The SDK sources come from build/NitroSDK (run tools/bootstrap.py first).\r\n# Our changes to them are in by src/ctrdg.c instead), prc (gesture recognition),\r\n# wvr, env, ext, os/src/os_china.c (China-edition boot screen) and\r\n# math/src/qsort.c. pad and exi are ARM7-only. utest is built because the\r\n# SDK's own self-tests (in os_thread.c) refer to it.\r\n#\r\n# Replaced by our own C in src/:\r\n#   mi/src/mi_memory.c, mi_swap.c, mi_uncompress.c  (Metrowerks assembly only)\r\n#   os/src/os_cache.c, os_tcm.c, os_protection*.c   (DS CPU setup: nothing to do) -> port_os.c\r\n#   os/src/os_exception.c, os_reset.c               (mostly assembly)            -> port_os.c\r\n#   pxi/src/pxi_fifo.c, pxi_init.c                  (the ARM7 link)              -> pxi.c\r\n#   dgt/prebuilt/libdgt.a                           (MD5/SHA-1, a binary)        -> dgt.c\r\n#   the divider/square-root hardware                                             -> port_cp.c\r\n# Not built: mi/src/mi_uncomp_stream.c (streaming decompression; assembly only,\r\n# and the game doesn't use it).\r\n\r\n# A second, genuine ARM7 build of the pinned SDK sound driver. These objects\r\n# are compiled with SDK_ARM7, not SDK_ARM9, then ALL their global definitions\r\n# and cross-object references are renamed with objcopy --redefine-syms. This\r\n# avoids duplicate SND_Init/SNDi_Work/etc and retains the exact ARM7 engine.\r\nARM7_SOUND_SRCS := \\\r\n snd/src/ARM7/snd_global.c \\\r\n snd/src/ARM7/snd_channel.c \\\r\n snd/src/snd_util.c \\\r\n snd/src/snd_main.c \\\r\n snd/src/ARM7/snd_capture.c \\\r\n snd/src/ARM7/snd_exchannel.c \\\r\n snd/src/ARM7/snd_seq.c \\\r\n snd/src/ARM7/snd_midiplayer.c \\\r\n snd/src/snd_bank.c \\\r\n snd/src/snd_work.c \\\r\n snd/src/snd_alarm.c \\\r\n snd/src/snd_command.c \\\r\n snd/src/snd_data.c\r\nARM7_RAW := $(ARM7_SOUND_SRCS:%.c=$(OUT)/arm7_raw/%.o)\r\nARM7_OBJS := $(ARM7_SOUND_SRCS:%.c=$(OUT)/arm7_renamed/%.o)\r\nARM7_MAP := $(GEN)/arm7_sound_redefine.syms\r\n\r\nPORT_SRCS := $(wildcard src/*.c)\r\n\r\n# Threads, signals and the clock come from the machine (src/port_platform.h).\r\nifeq ($(TARGET),3ds)\r\nPORT_SRCS += src/platform/3ds.c\r\nelse\r\nPORT_SRCS += src/platform/host.c\r\nendif\r\n\r\nSDK_OBJS  := $(SDK_SRCS:%.c=$(OUT)/sdk/%.o)\r\nPORT_OBJS := $(PORT_SRCS:src/%.c=$(OUT)/port/%.o)\r\n# Embed the *same* portable libpak implementation in libnitro.a. NitroSDK\r\n# callers already link libnitro, so we don't force a new linker dependency on\r\n# every native game/smoke-test target while still using the C libpak API.\r\nPAK_READER_OBJ := $(OUT)/port/pak_reader.o\r\nPORT_OBJS += $(PAK_READER_OBJ)\r\nLIB       := $(OUT)/libnitro.a\r\n\r\n# --- Flags -----------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n# Compiler, target and SDK configuration: see ../common.mk.\r\nCFLAGS := $(PORT_CFLAGS) $(SDK_INCLUDES) -I../pak/include\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_PALETTE_HASH),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DHGSS_PALETTE_HASH=1\r\nendif\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_GX3D_HOTLOOP),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DHGSS_GX3D_HOTLOOP=1\r\nendif\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_GX3D_LISTCACHE),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DHGSS_GX3D_LISTCACHE=1\r\nendif\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_GX3D_STATEDEDUP),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DHGSS_GX3D_STATEDEDUP=1\r\nendif\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_GX3D_FUSEHASH),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DHGSS_GX3D_FUSEHASH=1\r\nendif\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_GX3D_LAZYINSERT),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DHGSS_GX3D_LAZYINSERT=1\r\nendif\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_GX3D_BG3SLOT),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DHGSS_GX3D_BG3SLOT=1\r\nendif\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_SND_ADPCM),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DHGSS_SND_ADPCM=1\r\nendif\r\n# Decoded-ADPCM cache verify mode: every cached block also decoded live and\r\n# compared ([sndcache] verify_mismatch in profile builds).\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_SND_VERIFY),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DNITRO_SOUND_ADPCM_VERIFY=1\r\nendif\r\nifeq ($(HGSS_A0_DIAG),1)\r\n  CFLAGS += -DHGSS_A0_DIAG=1\r\nendif\r\n\r\n# --- Rules -----------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n.PHONY: all lib test clean replay\r\n\r\nifeq ($(IS_HOST),yes)\r\nall: test\r\nelse\r\nall: lib\r\nendif\r\n\r\nlib: $(LIB)\r\n\r\n$(GEN)/nitro/fx/fx_const.h: $(SDK)/gen/nitro/fx/fx_const.csv $(SDK)/gen/nitro/fx/gen_fx_const.py\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\tpython3 $(SDK)/gen/nitro/fx/gen_fx_const.py $< $@\r\n\r\n$(OUT)/sdk/%.o: $(SDK)/libraries/%.c $(GEN)/nitro/fx/fx_const.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t@echo \"  CC  $(notdir $<)\"\r\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@\r\n\r\n$(OUT)/port/%.o: src/%.c $(GEN)/nitro/fx/fx_const.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t@echo \"  CC  $(notdir $<)\"\r\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -MMD -MP -c $< -o $@\r\n\r\n# The port's sources rebuilt when a header they include changes (a struct\r\n# that changes size must not leave objects built with the old one).\r\n-include $(PORT_OBJS:.o=.d)\r\n\r\n# The 3DS platform layer uses libctru (and none of the SDK's headers).\r\nDEVKITPRO ?= /opt/devkitpro\r\n$(OUT)/port/platform/3ds.o: src/platform/3ds.c src/port_platform.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t@echo \"  CC  platform/3ds.c\"\r\n\t@$(CC) $(PORT_CFLAGS) -I$(DEVKITPRO)/libctru/include -c $< -o $@\r\n\r\n$(PAK_READER_OBJ): ../pak/src/pak.c ../pak/include/pak.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t@echo \"  CC  libpak reader\"\r\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@\r\n\r\n# Compile the ARM7 driver *without* the ARM9 flags used everywhere else.\r\n# The port patches redirect its sound registers and avoid the ARM9 scheduler.\r\n$(OUT)/arm7_raw/%.o: $(SDK)/libraries/%.c $(GEN)/nitro/fx/fx_const.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t@echo \"  ARM7 CC $(notdir $<)\"\r\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -USDK_ARM9 -DSDK_ARM7 -include nitro/misc.h -include stdint.h -c $< -o $@\r\n\r\n# Produce one shared mapping from every ARM7 definition, not a na�ve\r\n# --prefix-symbols (which would rename libc/OS references too).\r\n$(ARM7_MAP): $(ARM7_RAW)\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t@$(NM) -g --defined-only $(ARM7_RAW) | awk 'NF == 3 && $$2 ~ /^[TDBRCSG]$$/ { print $$3 \" N7_\" $$3 }' | sort -u > $@\r\n\r\n$(OUT)/arm7_renamed/%.o: $(OUT)/arm7_raw/%.o $(ARM7_MAP)\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t@cp $< $@\r\n\t@$(OBJCOPY) --redefine-syms=$(ARM7_MAP) $@\r\n\r\n$(LIB): $(SDK_OBJS) $(PORT_OBJS) $(ARM7_OBJS)\r\n\t@rm -f $@\r\n\t@$(AR) rcs $@ $^\r\n\t@echo \"built $@\"\r\n\r\n# Pure-C chip tests link no NitroSDK or platform code.\r\nSOUND_CHIP_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_sound_chip\r\n$(SOUND_CHIP_TEST_BIN): tests/test_sound_chip.c tests/sound_chip_reference.c src/port_sound_chip.c include/nitro_port_sound_chip.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t$(CC) $(PORT_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -Iinclude tests/test_sound_chip.c tests/sound_chip_reference.c src/port_sound_chip.c -o $@\r\n\r\n# Original ARM9 API to the renamed ARM7 driver through the virtual PXI\r\n# protocol, with a synthetic SSEQ/SBNK/SWAR fixture (no game content).\r\nSOUND_SEQ_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_sound_sequence\r\n$(SOUND_SEQ_TEST_BIN): tests/test_sound_sequence.c $(LIB)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(LIB) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# Measurement tool, not a test: plays one sequence of a retail SDAT through the\r\n# port's audio stack (tests/sdat_render.c) and writes a WAV and mixer diagnostics.\r\n# Host32 only, and it needs NitroSystem's archive: SDAT_NNS_LIB=<libnitrosystem.a>.\r\n# `python3 tools/hgss_nitro.py sdat-render --out DIR` builds both archives first.\r\n# sdat_render has the diagnostics (NITRO_SOUND_STATS compiles port_sound_chip.c\r\n# with the frame hook); sdat_render_release has the port's own mixer, for timing.\r\nSDAT_RENDER_BIN := $(OUT)/sdat_render\r\nSDAT_RENDER_RELEASE_BIN := $(OUT)/sdat_render_release\r\nSDAT_NNS_LIB ?=\r\n.PHONY: sdat_render sdat_render_release\r\nsdat_render: $(SDAT_RENDER_BIN)\r\nsdat_render_release: $(SDAT_RENDER_RELEASE_BIN)\r\n\r\n# The game's NitroSystem volume table (_0210D750) is the port's own object, which\r\n# tools/hgss_game.py links into the game; the renderers link the same one, or\r\n# NNS_SndMain has no definition for it.\r\nSDAT_VOLUME_TABLE := $(ROOT)/src/compat/hgss/src/nns_volume_table.c\r\n\r\n$(SDAT_RENDER_BIN): tests/sdat_render.c src/port_sound_chip.c include/nitro_port_sound_chip.h $(LIB) $(SDAT_NNS_LIB) $(SDAT_VOLUME_TABLE)\r\n\t@test \"$(TARGET)\" = host32 || { echo \"sdat_render needs TARGET=host32\"; exit 1; }\r\n\t@test -n \"$(SDAT_NNS_LIB)\" || { echo \"set SDAT_NNS_LIB=<libnitrosystem.a> (tools/hgss_nitro.py sdat-render does)\"; exit 1; }\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(NNS_INCLUDES) -DNITRO_SOUND_STATS $(LDFLAGS) $< src/port_sound_chip.c $(SDAT_VOLUME_TABLE) \\\r\n\t\t-Wl,--start-group $(SDAT_NNS_LIB) $(LIB) -Wl,--end-group -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n$(SDAT_RENDER_RELEASE_BIN): tests/sdat_render.c $(LIB) $(SDAT_NNS_LIB) $(SDAT_VOLUME_TABLE)\r\n\t@test \"$(TARGET)\" = host32 || { echo \"sdat_render_release needs TARGET=host32\"; exit 1; }\r\n\t@test -n \"$(SDAT_NNS_LIB)\" || { echo \"set SDAT_NNS_LIB=<libnitrosystem.a> (tools/hgss_nitro.py sdat-render does)\"; exit 1; }\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(NNS_INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(SDAT_VOLUME_TABLE) \\\r\n\t\t-Wl,--start-group $(SDAT_NNS_LIB) $(LIB) -Wl,--end-group -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# Unit tests run on the PC only.\r\nTEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_nitro\r\n\r\n$(TEST_BIN): tests/test_nitro.c $(LIB)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(LIB) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# An independent FS_* integration test uses only synthetic bytes produced by\r\n# the project's real Python pack writer (no ROM contents are checked in).\r\nFS_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_fs_pak\r\nFS_FIXTURE_DIR := $(OUT)/fs_fixture\r\nFS_FIXTURE_STAMP := $(FS_FIXTURE_DIR)/.generated\r\n\r\n$(FS_TEST_BIN): tests/test_fs_pak.c $(LIB)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(LIB) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n$(FS_FIXTURE_STAMP): tests/make_fs_fixture.py ../../builder/pack.py\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(FS_FIXTURE_DIR)\r\n\tpython3 tests/make_fs_fixture.py $(FS_FIXTURE_DIR)\r\n\t@touch $@\r\n\r\n# Threads, interrupts with threads, timers: a program of their own, since\r\n# once the SDK's threads start the program's thread is theirs for good.\r\nTHREAD_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_threads\r\n\r\n$(THREAD_TEST_BIN): tests/test_threads.c $(LIB)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(LIB) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# Call the actual ARM9 CARD/RTC/PM/TP APIs against virtual ARM7 handlers.\r\n# The integration executable creates its own temporary .sav and removes it.\r\nARM7_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_arm7\r\n\r\n$(ARM7_TEST_BIN): tests/test_arm7.c $(LIB)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(LIB) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# The software 2D renderer, set up through the SDK's own display functions.\r\nRENDER_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_render\r\n\r\n$(RENDER_TEST_BIN): tests/test_render.c tests/render2d_reference.c $(LIB)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $< tests/render2d_reference.c $(LIB) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# DS geometry command decoder + software PC triangle raster reference.\r\n# Tests use invented geometry and texture bytes, never the ROM or data pack.\r\nGX3D_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_gx3d\r\n# Compile the *patched original* NitroSystem gecom.c into this synthetic\r\n# test, so a real reg_G3X_GXFIFO store (not our decoder $(LIB) -lm -pthread -o $@\r\n\r\n# NitroSystem's VRAM transfer manager (the *patched original*) with the\r\n# port's OS_Halt: the 3D transfers done when the frame ends.\r\nVRAM_TRANSFER_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_vram_transfer\r\n$(VRAM_TRANSFER_TEST_BIN): tests/test_vram_transfer.c $(NNS)/libraries/gfd/src/VramTransferMan/gfd_VramTransferManager.c $(LIB)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(NNS_INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) tests/test_vram_transfer.c $(NNS)/libraries/gfd/src/VramTransferMan/gfd_VramTransferManager.c $(LIB) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# Race-test the three-slot scene handoff and the pure-C vertex builder.\r\nGX3D_PLUMBING_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_gx3d_plumbing\r\n$(GX3D_PLUMBING_TEST_BIN): tests/test_gx3d_plumbing.c $(LIB)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(LIB) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# The lower screen as a menu: its drawing and its touches (port_lowermenu.c).\r\nLOWERMENU_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_lowermenu\r\n$(LOWERMENU_TEST_BIN): tests/test_lowermenu.c $(LIB)\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(LIB) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# The port's own settings (port_options.c): plain C, no SDK.\r\nOPTIONS_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_options\r\n$(OPTIONS_TEST_BIN): tests/test_options.c src/port_options.c include/nitro_port_options.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t$(CC) $(PORT_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -Iinclude tests/test_options.c src/port_options.c -o $@\r\n\r\n# The pixel-art upscaler and texture tiler: plain C, no SDK.\r\nUPSCALE_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_upscale\r\n$(UPSCALE_TEST_BIN): tests/test_upscale.c src/port_upscale.c include/nitro_port_upscale.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t$(CC) $(PORT_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -Iinclude tests/test_upscale.c src/port_upscale.c -o $@\r\n\r\n# xBRZ at 2x (the 3D's textures, filter3d xbrz): plain C, no SDK. SSE for\r\n# the doubles on a 32-bit PC, as the 3DS's VFP and a 64-bit PC do them (the\r\n# x87's wider ones could decide an edge's way otherwise, and the hashes of\r\n# the original xBRZ's output wouldn't match).\r\nXBRZ_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_xbrz\r\n$(XBRZ_TEST_BIN): tests/test_xbrz.c src/port_xbrz.c include/nitro_port_xbrz.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t$(CC) $(PORT_CFLAGS) $(if $(filter host32,$(TARGET)),-msse2 -mfpmath=sse) $(LDFLAGS) -Iinclude tests/test_xbrz.c src/port_xbrz.c -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# Sun shadows' setup (port_shadow.c): plain C, no SDK.\r\nSHADOW_TEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_shadow\r\n$(SHADOW_TEST_BIN): tests/test_shadow.c src/port_shadow.c include/nitro_port_shadow.h\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t$(CC) $(PORT_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -Iinclude tests/test_shadow.c src/port_shadow.c -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# Same scenes with and without the geometry thread, for a recording of the\r\n# game (the PC runner's --gx-record FILE): make replay, then\r\n# build/host/gx3d_replay FILE. Not run by `make test`.\r\nGX3D_REPLAY_BIN := $(OUT)/gx3d_replay\r\n$(GX3D_REPLAY_BIN): tests/gx3d_replay.c $(LIB)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(LIB) -lm -pthread -o $@\r\nreplay: $(GX3D_REPLAY_BIN)\r\n\r\ntest: $(TEST_BIN) $(FS_TEST_BIN) $(FS_FIXTURE_STAMP) $(THREAD_TEST_BIN) $(ARM7_TEST_BIN) $(SOUND_CHIP_TEST_BIN) $(SOUND_SEQ_TEST_BIN) $(RENDER_TEST_BIN) $(GX3D_TEST_BIN) $(GX3D_PLUMBING_TEST_BIN) $(VRAM_TRANSFER_TEST_BIN) $(UPSCALE_TEST_BIN) $(XBRZ_TEST_BIN) $(SHADOW_TEST_BIN) $(LOWERMENU_TEST_BIN) $(OPTIONS_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(FS_TEST_BIN) $(FS_FIXTURE_DIR)\r\n\t./$(THREAD_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(ARM7_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(SOUND_CHIP_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(SOUND_SEQ_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(RENDER_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(GX3D_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(GX3D_PLUMBING_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(VRAM_TRANSFER_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(UPSCALE_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(LOWERMENU_TEST_BIN)\r\n\tcd $(OUT) && ./test_options\r\n\t./$(XBRZ_TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(SHADOW_TEST_BIN)\r\n\r\nclean:\r\n\trm -rf build\r\n"

                "text": "# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n# libnitrosystem: Nintendo's NitroSystem (3D models, 2D sprites, VRAM\r\n# managers, the sound archive player, heaps), compiled with GCC for the 3DS,\r\n# and for PC so it can be unit tested. \\\r\n\tload/g2d_NAN_load.c load/g2d_NOB_load.c load/g2d_NMC_load.c \\\r\n\tload/g2d_NEN_load.c load/g2d_NCG_load.c load/g2d_NCL_load.c \\\r\n\tload/g2d_NSC_load.c load/g2d_Load.c load/g2d_NFT_load.c \\\r\n\tg2d_Softsprite.c g2d_Animation.c g2d_OAM.c g2d_OAMEx.c \\\r\n\tg2d_PaletteTable.c g2d_Image.c g2d_SRTControl.c g2d_Node.c \\\r\n\tg2d_CullingUtility.c g2d_CellAnimation.c g2d_MultiCellAnimation.c \\\r\n\tg2d_Entity.c g2d_Renderer.c g2d_CellTransferManager.c \\\r\n\tg2d_OamSoftwareSpriteDraw.c g2d_Screen.c g2d_RendererCore.c g2d_Font.c \\\r\n\tg2d_CharCanvas.c g2d_TextCanvas.c \\\r\n\tinternal/g2di_Mtx32.c internal/g2di_debug.c internal/g2di_BitReader.c \\\r\n\tinternal/g2di_SplitChar.c internal/g2di_BGManipulator.c\r\n\r\nG3D_SRCS := \\\r\n\tkernel.c glbstate.c anm.c cgtool.c sbc.c 1mat1shp.c gecom.c util.c mem.c \\\r\n\tmodel.c \\\r\n\tbinres/res_print.c binres/res_print_nsbca.c binres/res_print_nsbma.c \\\r\n\tbinres/res_print_nsbta.c binres/res_print_nsbtp.c binres/res_print_nsbva.c \\\r\n\tbinres/res_struct.c binres/res_struct_accessor.c \\\r\n\tbinres/res_struct_accessor_anm.c \\\r\n\tanm/nsbca.c anm/nsbma.c anm/nsbta.c anm/nsbtp.c anm/nsbva.c \\\r\n\tcgtool/basic.c cgtool/maya.c cgtool/si3d.c cgtool/3dsmax.c cgtool/xsi.c\r\n\r\nGFD_SRCS := \\\r\n\tVramManager/gfd_TexVramMan.c VramManager/gfd_PlttVramMan.c \\\r\n\tVramManager/gfd_FrameTexVramMan.c VramManager/gfd_FramePlttVramMan.c \\\r\n\tVramManager/gfdi_LinkedListVramMan_Common.c \\\r\n\tVramManager/gfd_LinkedListTexVramMan.c VramManager/gfd_LinkedListPlttVramMan.c \\\r\n\tVramTransferMan/gfd_VramTransferManager.c\r\n\r\nSND_SRCS := main.c resource_mgr.c waveout.c player.c stream.c capture.c \\\r\n            sndarc.c heap.c sndarc_loader.c sndarc_player.c sndarc_stream.c \\\r\n            output_effect.c seqdata.c fader.c\r\n\r\n# Not built: mcs, the link to Nintendo's PC debugging tools (the game\r\n# doesn't use it).\r\n\r\nNNS_SRCS := $(FND_SRCS:%=fnd/src/%) $(G2D_SRCS:%=g2d/src/%) \\\r\n            $(G3D_SRCS:%=g3d/src/%) $(GFD_SRCS:%=gfd/src/%) \\\r\n            $(SND_SRCS:%=snd/src/%)\r\n\r\nNNS_OBJS := $(NNS_SRCS:%.c=$(OUT)/nns/%.o)\r\nGEN      := $(OUT)/gen\r\nLIB      := $(OUT)/libnitrosystem.a\r\nLIBNITRO := $(NITRO)/build/$(TARGET)/libnitro.a\r\n\r\n# --- Flags $(SDK_INCLUDES)\r\n\r\n# --- Rules -----------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n.PHONY: all lib test clean libnitro\r\n\r\nifeq ($(IS_HOST),yes)\r\nall: test\r\nelse\r\nall: lib\r\nendif\r\n\r\nlib: $(LIB)\r\n\r\n# libnitro is built by its own Makefile (it also generates a header the\r\n# SDK includes, so it has to come first).\r\nlibnitro:\r\n\t@$(MAKE) --no-print-directory -C $(NITRO) TARGET=$(TARGET) lib\r\n\r\n$(LIBNITRO): libnitro\r\n\r\n# The list of NitroSystem's header inline functions (see ../common.mk):\r\n# compile a file that includes every header and keep the functions it exports.\r\nNNS_HEADERS := $(shell find $(NNS)/include $(NNS)/libraries -name '*.h')\r\n\r\n$(GEN)/nns_all_headers.c: $(NNS_HEADERS) $(ROOT)/tools/game/nns_inline_symbols.py\r\n\t@python3 $(ROOT)/tools/game/nns_inline_symbols.py $@\r\n\r\n$(GEN)/nns_all_headers.o: $(GEN)/nns_all_headers.c | libnitro\r\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@\r\n\r\n# Replaced only when the list changes: every object of NitroSystem and the\r\n# game depends on it, so a rewrite with the same names would rebuild them all.\r\n$(NNS_INLINE_SYMS): $(GEN)/nns_all_headers.o\r\n\t@$(NM) -g --defined-only $< | awk '$$2 == \"T\" { print $$3 }' > $@.new\r\n\t@if cmp -s $@.new $@; then rm -f $@.new; else mv $@.new $@; fi\r\n\t@echo \"  $$(wc -l < $@) NitroSystem header inline functions\"\r\n\r\n$(OUT)/nns/%.o: $(NNS)/libraries/%.c $(NNS_INLINE_SYMS) | libnitro\r\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\r\n\t@echo \"  CC  $(notdir $<)\"\r\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@\r\n\t@$(WEAKEN_NNS_INLINE)\r\n\r\n$(LIB): $(NNS_OBJS)\r\n\t@rm -f $@\r\n\t@$(AR) rcs $@ $^\r\n\t@echo \"built $@\"\r\n\r\n# Unit tests run on the PC only.\r\nTEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_nitrosystem\r\n\r\n$(OUT)/test_nitrosystem.o: tests/test_nitrosystem.c $(NNS_INLINE_SYMS)\r\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@\r\n\t@$(WEAKEN_NNS_INLINE)\r\n\r\n$(TEST_BIN): $(OUT)/test_nitrosystem.o $(LIB) $(LIBNITRO)\r\n\t$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $< $(LIB) $(LIBNITRO) -lm -o $@\r\n\r\n# The tests load the game's own 3D and 2D files from the decompilation.\r\ntest: $(TEST_BIN)\r\n\t./$(TEST_BIN) $(ROOT)/build/upstream/res\r\n\r\nclean:\r\n\trm -rf build\r\n=== pak ===\r\n# Standalone portable C99 reader for docs/PAK_FORMAT.md.\r\n#   make                Build host library and run synthetic tests\r\n#   make TARGET=host32  Build and run 32-bit tests (gcc-multilib required)\r\n#   make TARGET=3ds     Build ARM11 libpak.a (devkitARM required)\r\n#   make clean\r\n\r\nTARGET ?= host\r\nOUT := build/$(TARGET)\r\nINCLUDES := -Iinclude\r\nCFLAGS := -std=c99 -O2 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic $(INCLUDES)\r\n\r\nifeq ($(TARGET),3ds)\r\n  ifeq ($(strip $(DEVKITARM)),)\r\n    $(error Set DEVKITARM to your devkitPro devkitARM installation)\r\n  endif\r\n  CC := $(DEVKITARM)/bin/arm-none-eabi-gcc\r\n  AR := $(DEVKITARM)/bin/arm-none-eabi-ar\r\n  # Match 3ds_port/common.mk: 4-byte enums (ARM GCC shrinks them otherwise,\r\n  # so PakResult would disagree with the game's code) and the same ABI flags.\r\n  CFLAGS += -march=armv6k -mtune=mpcore -mfpu=vfp -mfloat-abi=hard -mtp=soft \\\r\n            -fno-short-enums -mword-relocations -ffunction-sections\r\n  DEFAULT_TARGET := lib\r\nelse ifeq ($(TARGET),host32)\r\n  CC := gcc\r\n  AR := ar\r\n  CFLAGS += -m32\r\n  LDFLAGS += -m32\r\n  DEFAULT_TARGET := test\r\nelse ifeq ($(TARGET),host)\r\n  CC := gcc\r\n  AR := ar\r\n  DEFAULT_TARGET := test\r\nelse\r\n  $(error TARGET must be host, host32 or 3ds)\r\nendif\r\n\r\nLIB := $(OUT)/libpak.a\r\nTEST_BIN := $(OUT)/test_pak\r\nPYTHON_FIXTURE := $(OUT)/python-fixture.pak\r\n\r\n"

On a 64-bit PC a few more are left out\r\n# (blocked_sources_64bit.txt). Fix a cause, delete its lines, and those files\r\n# join the library.\r\nblocklist = $(shell sed -e 's/\\#.*//' -e '/^[[:space:]]*$$/d' $(1))\r\nGAME_BLOCKED := $(call blocklist,blocked_sources.txt)\r\nifeq ($(TARGET),host)\r\nGAME_BLOCKED += $(call blocklist,blocked_sources_64bit.txt)\r\nendif\r\n# The sources the original build compiles (src/meson.build's lists).\r\nGAME_ALL_SRCS := $(shell python3 $(ROOT)/tools/game_sources.py $(GAME))\r\nGAME_SRCS := $(filter-out $(GAME_BLOCKED),$(GAME_ALL_SRCS))\r\nGAME_OBJS := $(GAME_SRCS:%.c=$(OUT)/src/%.o)\r\n\r\n# The game's own libraries that the original links into the same program\r\n# (meson.build: libcrypto, libgds, libspl). libdwcppwlobby/libdwcenc are\r\n# left out with the rest of online play.\r\nGAME_LIBS := crypto gds spl\r\nGAME_LIB_SRCS := $(sort $(foreach l,$(GAME_LIBS),$(wildcard $(GAME)/lib/$(l)/src/*.c)))\r\nGAME_OBJS += $(GAME_LIB_SRCS:$(GAME)/%.c=$(OUT)/%.o)\r\n\r\n# The trainer AI script: data written with assembler macros, which the\r\n# original assembles with GNU as (meson.build: trainer_ai_o). It is only\r\n# data, so any target's assembler builds it the same way.\r\nTRAINER_AI_O := $(OUT)/src/battle/trainer_ai/script.o\r\nGAME_OBJS += $(TRAINER_AI_O)\r\n\r\n# Game headers (inlines.h, pokemon_sprite.h, NitroDWC's dwc_friend.h ...)\r\n# define functions with plain `inline`. The linker then keeps one copy, as Metrowerks did.\r\n# The host test object is counted too, since it includes the same headers.\r\nGAME_HEADER_DEFS := $(OUT)/gen/game_header_defs.syms\r\nTEST_OBJ := $(OUT)/tests/test_game.o\r\nCENSUS_OBJS := $(GAME_OBJS) $(if $(IS_HOST),$(TEST_OBJ))\r\n\r\n# Use the actual Meson/Metang rules from the pinned decompilation for ALL\r\n# 107 generated enum/mask headers, including TextBank.             "content": [
              {
                "type": "text",
                "text": "/*\r\n * kj_bridge.h: the only interface between the DS side (the original game,\r\n * NitroSDK and the compat layer, compiled with 4-byte enums and NitroSDK's\r\n * types) and the 3DS side (libctru/citro3d, compiled with libctru's ABI).\r\n *\r\n * Rules:\r\n *   - fixed-width C types and plain structs only; no enums cross this line\r\n *     (the two halves disagree on enum size);\r\n *   - no NitroSDK or libctru header is included here;\r\n *   - functions prefixed kj_ds_ are implemented on the DS side, kj_ctr_ on\r\n *     the 3DS side.\r\n */\r\n\r\n#ifndef KJ_BRIDGE_H\r\n#define KJ_BRIDGE_H\r\n\r\n#include <stdbool.h>\r\n#include <stddef.h>\r\n#include <stdint.h>\r\n\r\n#ifdef __cplusplus\r\nextern \"C\" {\r\n#endif\r\n\r\n/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */\r\n\r\ntypedef struct kj_game_settings {\r\n    uint16_t nickname[11];   /* UTF-16, 0-terminated */\r\n    uint8_t language;        /* NVRAM language code (1 = English) */\r\n    uint8_t birth_month;\r\n    uint8_t birth_day;\r\n    uint8_t favorite_color;\r\n} kj_game_settings;\r\n\r\n/* Open the content pack (both paths are full paths, e.g. romfs:/... or\r\n * sdmc:/...). Returns NULL on success or a human-readable reason. */\r\nconst char *kj_ds_open_pack(const char *pak_path, const char *manifest_path);\r\n\r\n/* Write the cartridge/firmware state and run the original NitroMain on the\r\n * calling thread. Does not return while the game runs. */\r\nvoid kj_game_main(const kj_game_settings *settings);\r\n\r\n/* Back the game's 512 KiB save chip with a raw file (compat port_card).\r\n * Must be called before kj_game_main. */\r\nvoid kj_ds_set_save_path(const char *path);\r\n\r\n/* Edition identity compiled into this program. */\r\nconst char *kj_ds_edition_name(void);     /* \"heartgold\" / \"soulsilver\" */\r\nconst char *kj_ds_pack_build_id(void);    /* pack builder ID the program expects */\r\n\r\n/* -------------------------------------------------------- DS memory view */\r\n\r\n/* Read-only pointers into the emulated DS memory the renderer translates.\r\n * They are valid for the program's lifetime. The renderer reads them only\r\n * inside kj_ctr_publish_frame (on the game thread, while the game is\r\n * stopped at its frame boundary), so every read is coherent with one\r\n * published frame. */\r\ntypedef struct kj_ds_memory {\r\n    const uint8_t *io;            /* 0x04000000.. I/O registers (engine A at +0, B at +0x1000) */\r\n    const uint8_t *pltt;          /* 0x800: BG A, OBJ A, BG B, OBJ B */\r\n    const uint8_t *oam;           /* 0x800: engine A, engine B */\r\n    const uint8_t *bg_vram_a;     /* 0x80000 engine A BG view */\r\n    const uint8_t *bg_vram_b;     /* 0x20000 engine B BG view */\r\n    const uint8_t *obj_vram_a;    /* 0x40000 engine A OBJ view */\r\n    const uint8_t *obj_vram_b;    /* 0x20000 engine B OBJ view */\r\n    const uint8_t *lcdc_vram;     /* 0xA4000 banks A..I in LCDC order */\r\n    size_t io_size;\r\n} kj_ds_memory;\r\n\r\nconst kj_ds_memory *kj_ds_get_memory(void);\r\n\r\n/* VRAM bank -> use mapping, decoded from VRAMCNT_A..I. For each bank:\r\n * offset into lcdc_vram, size, and the MST/OFS fields. */\r\ntypedef struct kj_vram_bank {\r\n    uint32_t lcdc_offset;\r\n    uint32_t size;\r\n    uint8_t enabled;\r\n    uint8_t mst;\r\n    uint8_t ofs;\r\n} kj_vram_bank;\r\n\r\n/* ---------------------------------------------------- per-line registers */\r\n\r\n/* When the game uses H-blank effects, the per-scanline register copies\r\n * (0x70 bytes from 0x04000000 and 0x04001000 for each line) are valid for\r\n * this frame. NULL / 0 when no H-blank effect ran. */\r\n#define KJ_LINE_REG_BYTES 0x70\r\ntypedef struct kj_line_regs {\r\n    const uint8_t (*regs)[192][KJ_LINE_REG_BYTES];   /* [engine][line] */\r\n    bool active;\r\n} kj_line_regs;\r\n\r\n/* -------------------------------------------------------------- 3D stream */\r\n\r\n/* One frame of decoded 3D geometry, produced by the DS-side geometry engine\r\n * (kj_g3.c) and consumed by the PICA backend. The geometry engine does the\r\n * DS's matrix work, texture-coordinate generation and readable tests on the\r\n * CPU with exact fixed-point semantics. NORMAL latches transformed normals\r\n * and lighting inputs for the PICA; literal colours remain supported.\r\n * Positions stay in object space for the GPU clip-matrix palette. */\r\n\r\n#define KJ_G3_MAX_MATRICES 4096\r\n#define KJ_G3_MAX_VERTS 32768\r\n#define KJ_G3_MAX_INDICES 65536\r\n#define KJ_G3_MAX_BATCHES 2048\r\n\r\ntypedef struct kj_g3_vertex {\r\n    int16_t x, y, z;     /* object space, 4.12 fixed */\r\n    uint8_t mtx;         /* index into the batch's matrix palette */\r\n    uint8_t pad;\r\n    uint8_t r, g, b, a;  /* 0..255 (DS 5-bit expanded); a = polygon alpha */\r\n    int16_t s, t;        /* texel units, 12.4 fixed (after DS texgen) */\r\n} kj_g3_vertex;          /* 16 bytes */\r\n\r\n/* A clip matrix (projection x position), row-major 4x4 floats in the\r\n * PICA's row order (rows = output components). */\r\ntypedef struct kj_g3_matrix {\r\n    float m[4][4];\r\n} kj_g3_matrix;\r\n\r\ntypedef struct kj_g3_batch {\r\n    uint32_t first_index;\r\n    uint32_t index_count;\r\n    uint16_t first_matrix;     /* palette slice for this batch */\r\n    uint16_t matrix_count;\r\n    uint32_t poly_attr;        /* DS POLYGON_ATTR at the BEGIN */\r\n    uint32_t tex_param;        /* DS TEXIMAGE_PARAM */\r\n    uint32_t tex_pltt;         /* DS PLTT_BASE */\r\n    uint32_t viewport;         /* VIEWPORT x1 | y1 << 8 | x2 << 16 | y2 << 24 */\r\n    uint32_t flags;            /* KJ_G3_BATCH_* */\r\n} kj_g3_batch;\r\n\r\n/* Matrices one draw can address (the vertex shader's uniform palette). */\r\n#define KJ_G3_PALETTE 16\r\n#define KJ_G3_LIT_PALETTE 6\r\n#define KJ_G3_MAX_LIGHTING 512\r\n\r\n#define KJ_G3_BATCH_TRANSLUCENT 0x1u   /* goes to the translucent list */\r\n#define KJ_G3_BATCH_SHADOW      0x2u   /* DS shadow polygon */\r\n#define KJ_G3_BATCH_LIT         0x4u   /* lighting context index in flags >> 16 */\r\n\r\ntypedef struct kj_g3_frame {\r\n    const kj_g3_vertex *verts;\r\n    const uint16_t *indices;\r\n    const kj_g3_matrix *matrices;\r\n    const kj_g3_batch *batches;\r\n    uint32_t vert_count;\r\n    uint32_t index_count;\r\n    uint32_t matrix_count;\r\n    uint32_t batch_count;\r\n    /* DS state at SwapBuffers */\r\n    uint32_t disp3dcnt;\r\n    uint32_t clear_color;      /* CLEAR_COLOR */\r\n    uint32_t clear_depth;      /* CLEAR_DEPTH (15 bit) */\r\n    uint32_t swap_params;      /* SWAP_BUFFERS argument */\r\n    uint32_t viewport;         /* VIEWPORT x1,y1,x2,y2 bytes */\r\n    uint8_t alpha_test_ref;\r\n    uint16_t fog_color_hi;\r\n    uint32_t fog_color;\r\n    uint16_t fog_offset;\r\n"
              }

        {

          "text": "While the build runs, adapt kj_boot.c for Platinum and add the overlay/boot pieces. Let me edit kj_boot.c.",
          "time": {

        {
          "type": "tool",
          "id": "call_32d9de8c141c45bfa2a70974",
          "name": "write",
          "executed": false,
          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "/*\n * kj_boot.c: what the DS firmware and cartridge loader did before the\n * game's NitroMain, on the DS side of the bridge.\n *\n * Writes the cartridge header and firmware settings the SDK reads, hands the\n * compat layer the overlay table, registers the virtual ARM7 services and\n * runs the original NitroMain. Cartridge-header values and the fixed MAC\n * address follow pokeplatinum-3ds's game start (3ds_port/game/app/platinum.c,\n * GPL-3.0); the boot sequence is kohjoh's.\n */\n\n#include \"kj_bridge.h\"\n\n#include <nitro.h>\n#include <nitro_port.h>\n#include <nitro_port_fs.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\nextern const NitroPortOverlay gPlatinumOverlays[];   /* gen/overlay_table.c */\nextern const u32 gPlatinumOverlayCount;\n\nvoid NitroMain(void);\n\n#define KJ_EDITION \"platinum\"\n#define KJ_PAK_BUILD_ID \"platinum-nitrofs-1\"\n\n/* The game stores the console's MAC address in the save and compares it on\n * load; one fixed address keeps every save \"from this DS\". 00:09:BF is one\n * of Nintendo's prefixes. */\nstatic const u8 MAC_ADDRESS[6] = { 0x00, 0x09, 0xBF, 0x50, 0x33, 0xD5 };\n\nconst char *kj_ds_edition_name(void)\n{\n    return KJ_EDITION;\n}\n\nconst char *kj_ds_pack_build_id(void)\n{\n    return KJ_PAK_BUILD_ID;\n}\n\nvoid kj_ds_set_save_path(const char *path)\n{\n    NitroPort_SetSavePath(path);\n}\n\nconst char *kj_ds_open_pack(const char *pak_path, const char *manifest_path)\n{\n    switch (NitroPort_OpenPak(pak_path, manifest_path, KJ_PAK_BUILD_ID)) {\n    case PAK_OK:\n        return NULL;\n    case PAK_ERR_IO:\n        return \"cannot read the data pack or its manifest\";\n    case PAK_ERR_FORMAT:\n        return \"the data pack or its manifest is damaged, or they do not belong together\";\n    case PAK_ERR_VERSION:\n        return \"the data pack was made by a different version of the pack builder\";\n    case PAK_ERR_BUILD_ID:\n        return \"the data pack is for the other edition (wrong build ID)\";\n    case PAK_ERR_ROM_SHA1:\n        return \"the data pack was made from a ROM this version does not support\";\n    case PAK_ERR_MEMORY:\n        return \"out of memory opening the data pack\";\n    default:\n        return \"cannot open the data pack\";\n    }\n}\n\nvoid kj_game_main(const kj_game_settings *settings)\n{\n    CARDRomHeader header;\n    NitroPortFirmware firmware;\n\n    /* The cartridge header, as far as the game and the SDK read it: the\n     * game checks the maker code at boot (boot.c). Files come from the data\n     * pack, so the cartridge offsets mean nothing here. */\n    memset(&header, 0, sizeof(header));\n    memcpy(header.game_name, \"POKEMON PL\\0\\0\", 12);\n    header.game_code = 'C' | ('P' << 8) | ('U' << 16) | ((u32)'E' << 24);\n    header.maker_code = '0' | ('1' << 8);\n    header.device_size = 10;   /* 128 MB */\n    header.game_version = 1;\n\n    memset(&firmware, 0, sizeof(firmware));\n    firmware.romHeader = &header;\n    firmware.romHeaderSize = sizeof(header);\n    firmware.nickname = settings->nickname;\n    firmware.language = settings->language;\n    firmware.birthMonth = settings->birth_month;\n    firmware.birthDay = settings->birth_day;\n    firmware.favoriteColor = settings->favorite_color;\n    memcpy(firmware.macAddress, MAC_ADDRESS, sizeof(MAC_ADDRESS));\n    firmware.rtcOffset = 0;\n    NitroPort_BootFirmware(&firmware);\n\n    NitroPort_SetOverlays(gPlatinumOverlays, gPlatinumOverlayCount);\n\n    /* The ARM7's services: the save chip, the clock, the touch screen and\n     * power management (sound, microphone and wireless are handled by the\n     * port's own virtual ARM7). */\n    NitroPort_InitArm7Services();\n\n    NitroPort_Log(\"[kj] starting %s\", KJ_EDITION);\n    NitroMain();\n    NitroPort_Log(\"[kj] NitroMain returned\");\n    OS_Terminate();\n    for (;;) {\n    }\n}\n",
              "path": "C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\sinjoh\\engine\\runtime\\kj_boot.c"
            },

SDK sources are not\r\n    compiled here: the archives own them, and compiling them twice would\r\n    duplicate every symbol at link time.\r\n    \"\"\"\r\n    c = list(data[\"c_sources\"])\r\n    cpp = list(data[\"cpp_sources\"])\r\n    for rel in data[\"port_lib_sources\"]:\r\n        if rel.startswith(GAME_LIB_PREFIXES) and not rel.startswith(SKIP_LIB_PREFIXES):\r\n            if rel.endswith(\".cpp\"):\r\n                cpp.append(rel)\r\n            else:\r\n                c.append(rel)\r\n    return {\"c\": sorted(set(c)), \"cpp\": sorted(set(cpp)),\r\n            \"asm\": sorted(set(data[\"asm_sources\"]))}\r\n\r\n\r\ndef app_sources(target: str) -> list[Path]:\r\n    \"\"\"kohjoh's DS-side objects: compiled with the game's flags and NitroSDK\r\n    headers (4-byte enums). They are the bridge between the original game and\r\n    the 3DS runtime; they never include libctru (see ctr_sources).\"\"\"\r\n    if target not in (\"host32\", \"3ds\"):\r\n        raise ValueError(f\"unknown target {target!r}\")\r\n    compat = REPO / \"src\" / \"compat\"\r\n    sources = [compat / \"stubs\" / \"cpp_runtime.c\",\r\n               compat / \"hgss\" / \"src\" / \"msl_runtime.c\",\r\n               compat / \"hgss\" / \"src\" / \"nns_volume_table.c\",\r\n               compat / \"stubs\" / \"wm_stubs.c\",\r\n               compat / \"stubs\" / \"dsprot_stubs.c\",\r\n               compat / \"stubs\" / \"mb_stubs.c\"]\r\n    sources += sorted((REPO / \"src\" / \"runtime\").glob(\"*.c\"))\r\n    return sources\r\n\r\n\r\n#: 3DS-side directories: compiled with libctru's ABI (short enums), never\r\n#: with NitroSDK headers.                 "text": "# Builder\r\n\r\nThe builder extracts NitroFS files from **your own legally dumped Pok�mon\r\nPlatinum cartridge**, entirely on your computer. No ROM or extracted data\r\nis uploaded, committed or included in the project's releases.\r\n\r\n## Verify your ROM first\r\n\r\n```sh\r\npython builder/verify_rom.py /path/to/platinum.nds\r\n```\r\n\r\nOnly the supported, clean USA revisions pass the SHA-1 check. Modified,\r\ntrimmed or other-region dumps are rejected.\r\n\r\n## Extract the NitroFS data pack\r\n\r\nFrom the repository root:\r\n\r\n```sh\r\npython builder/extract_rom.py /path/to/platinum.nds\r\n```\r\n\r\nBy default, the output goes to `data_pack/` (gitignored). To choose\r\nanother directory:\r\n\r\n```sh\r\npython builder/extract_rom.py /path/to/platinum.nds --output data_pack/\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe extractor verifies the ROM itself before extracting. It reads the NDS\r\nheader, NitroFS file-name table (FNT), and file-allocation table (FAT);\r\nrecreates the directory tree and writes `manifest.json`. The manifest contains\r\na top-level `rom_sha1` (40 lowercase hex characters, from the verified source\r\nROM) alongside `files`. Each file entry has `id` (NitroSDK file ID), `path`\r\n(relative to the data pack), and `size` (bytes). File IDs are preserved for\r\nthe 3DS filesystem port.\r\n\r\nThe ROM is opened read-only and never modified. Keep the output private:\r\n**never add ROMs, extracted files, data packs or game assets to Git**.\r\n\r\n## Pack for the 3DS\r\n\r\nAfter extraction, the source ROM's SHA-1 is already in `data_pack/manifest.json`.\r\nYou do **not** need to supply the ROM again:\r\n\r\n```sh\r\npython builder/pack.py data_pack/ -o platinum3ds.pak\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe pack carries a build ID that the game program checks (default\r\n`platinum-nitrofs-1`, what the program expects; `--build-id` sets another).\r\nCopy `platinum3ds.pak` and `data_pack/manifest.json` to\r\n`sdmc:/3ds/pokeplatinum/` on the SD card (see `3ds_port/game/README.md`).\r\n\r\n`--rom /path/to/platinum.nds` or `--rom-sha1 <verified-40-hex-sha1>`\r\nmay optionally supply the verified source digest. If an override is supplied,\r\nit **must agree** with the manifest's digest. The packer CLI rejects hashes\r\noutside the supported ROM revisions, including manifest-supplied hashes.\r\n\r\nBoth `data_pack/` and the generated `.pak` are private outputs; never commit them.\r\n\r\n## The web builder's build\r\n\r\n`builder/web.py` makes the same data pack and `manifest.json` from the ROM's\r\nbytes, in memory (no folder of extracted files, no other programs), so the\r\nweb builder can run it in your browser with Pyodide. It also makes the HOME\r\nMenu banner's pieces (the 3D scene, with pycgfx, and the flat fallback). On a\r\nPC:\r\n\r\n```sh\r\npython builder/web.py /path/to/platinum.nds out/ --pycgfx build/pycgfx\r\n```\r\n\r\nA release's files (the program and the web builder's payload, no game data)\r\nare made by `tools/build_web_payload.py`; CI publishes them when a version is\r\ntagged.\r\n\r\n## Tests\r\n\r\n=== pack usage ===\r\n8: import argparse\r\n146: supported: Collection[str] | None = None,\r\n150: If `supported` is given, the ROM SHA-1 that would be written (from the\r\n175: if supported is not None and digest.hex() not in supported:\r\n176: raise ValueError(\"Unsupported ROM: run builder/verify_rom.py first\")\r\n228: raise ValueError(f\"Unsupported pak format version: {version}\")\r\n265: def main() -> int:\r\n266: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\r\n267: parser.add_argument(\"data_pack\", type=Path, help=\"Directory containing manifest.json\")\r\n268: parser.add_argument(\"-o\", \"--output\", type=Path, default=Path(\"platinum3ds.pak\"))\r\n269: parser.add_argument(\"--build-id\", default=DEFAULT_BUILD_ID,\r\n273: rom.add_argument(\"--rom\", type=Path, help=\"Read-only verified source ROM to obtain SHA-1\")\r\n274: rom.add_argument(\"--rom-sha1\", help=\"40-character SHA-1 of the verified source ROM\")\r\n275: parser.add_argument(\"--followers\", type=Path,\r\n304: supported=verify_rom.SUPPORTED, extra=extra)\r\n"

<sys/stat.h>\r\n\r\nstatic kj_paths s_paths;\r\n\r\nstatic bool file_exists(const char *path)\r\n{\r\n    struct stat st;\r\n    return stat(path, &st) == 0 && S_ISREG(st.st_mode);\r\n}\r\n\r\nstatic void ensure_dir(const char *path)\r\n{\r\n    if (mkdir(path, 0777) != 0 && errno != EEXIST) {\r\n        kj_log(\"[paths] cannot create %s (errno %d)\", path, errno);\r\n    }\r\n}\r\n\r\nconst kj_paths *kj_paths_init(void)\r\n{\r\n    const char *edition = kj_ds_edition_name();\r\n\r\n    snprintf(s_paths.root, sizeof(s_paths.root), \"sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh\");\r\n    ensure_dir(\"sdmc:/3ds\");\r\n    ensure_dir(s_paths.root);\r\n    {\r\n        char dir[128];\r\n        snprintf(dir, sizeof(dir), \"%s/data\", s_paths.root);\r\n        ensure_dir(dir);\r\n        snprintf(dir, sizeof(dir), \"%s/saves\", s_paths.root);\r\n        ensure_dir(dir);\r\n        snprintf(dir, sizeof(dir), \"%s/logs\", s_paths.root);\r\n        ensure_dir(dir);\r\n    }\r\n    snprintf(s_paths.log_file, sizeof(s_paths.log_file), \"%s/logs/%s.log\", s_paths.root, edition);\r\n\r\n    if (R_SUCCEEDED(romfsInit()) && file_exists(\"romfs:/data/game.pak\")) {\r\n        s_paths.bundled = true;\r\n        snprintf(s_paths.pack_file, sizeof(s_paths.pack_file), \"romfs:/data/game.pak\");\r\n        snprintf(s_paths.manifest_file, sizeof(s_paths.manifest_file),\r\n                 \"romfs:/data/game.manifest.json\");\r\n    } else {\r\n        s_paths.bundled = false;\r\n        snprintf(s_paths.pack_file, sizeof(s_paths.pack_file), \"%s/data/%s.pak\", s_paths.root,\r\n                 edition);\r\n        snprintf(s_paths.manifest_file, sizeof(s_paths.manifest_file),\r\n                 \"%s/data/%s.manifest.json\", s_paths.root, edition);\r\n    }\r\n    snprintf(s_paths.save_file, sizeof(s_paths.save_file), \"%s/saves/%s.sav\", s_paths.root,\r\n             edition);\r\n    return &s_paths;\r\n}\r\n"

A private copy\r\n# with a different executable name also survives older harnesses that kill\r\n# all processes named azahar. Never stage into another instance's SD card.\r\n$portable = Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $Emulator) \"user\"\r\n$userRoot = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $portable -PathType Container) {\r\n  $portable\r\n} else {\r\n  Join-Path $env:APPDATA \"Azahar\"\r\n}\r\nif (Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Path -eq $Emulator }) {\r\n  throw \"This emulator executable is already running. $i -lt 50; $i++) {\r\n  Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 100\r\n  $proc = Get-Process -Id $p.Id -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\r\n  if ($proc -and $proc.MainWindowHandle -ne 0) { [N.W]::MoveWindow($proc.MainWindowHandle, 0, 0, 840, 1100, $true) | Out-Null; break }\r\n"

      "text": "Instructions from: C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\sinjoh\\AGENTS.md\n# AGENTS.md\r\n\r\nRepository-wide rules for agent sessions working on kohjoh.\r\n\r\n## READ THE WIKI \r\n\r\nYou're not expected to have deep technical knowledge of the 3DS platform or how to program efficiently for it. This information has been collected for you already. If it isn't already on disk, clone https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot.git. Always refer to coffeepot's CTR section when you're writing code or planning project changes - read the relevant hardware, firrmware or engineering articles, so you understand what you're working with. If you can't justify a change with real-hardware evidence or a citation from the wiki, you probably should not do it. Never edit coffeepot yourself. If you notice something genuinely incorrect, PR and tell the user. Always follow the wiki's C style guide.\r\n\r\nThe coffeepot wiki is provided locally on this machine in workdir/coffeepot/.\r\n## Delegating to subagents\r\n\r\nA lead agent must give every subagent it calls **explicit instructions, explicit deliverables and explicit avoidables**. This is not optional, and it matters most for implementer agents: they edit files and cannot rely on chat context the lead has not written down.\r\n\r\nEvery subagent brief must state, in the prompt itself:\r\n\r\n1. **Objective** — the one bounded slice to complete, and why it exists.\r\n2. **Allowed paths** — the exact files or directories the subagent may read and edit.\r\n3. **Deliverables** — the concrete output: code, patch files, tests, docs, and the required report format (files changed, commands run, results, open questions).\r\n4. **Acceptance checks** — the commands or observations that prove the work is done, and the expected result.\r\n5. **Avoidables** — what not to touch or do: paths outside the slice, unrelated refactors, the decomp checkout in place, commits/pushes unless explicitly assigned, and any known traps from `kohjoh.md` or `docs/troubleshooting.md`.\r\n6. **Stopping point** — when to stop and report instead of guessing, for example if the slice grows, the brief conflicts with `kohjoh.md`, or an acceptance check cannot pass.\r\n\r\nDo not send a subagent a vague goal and let it infer scope. If the lead cannot fill in all six items, the slice is not ready to delegate. A brief that is broader, vaguer or in conflict with `kohjoh.md` should be revised before the call, not discovered by the subagent mid-edit.\r\n\r\nImplementer subagents hold `docs/status.md`, `docs/lessons.md` and `kohjoh.md` as required reading; the brief adds the slice-specific detail those files cannot contain. When this file disagrees with an agent definition under `.opencode/agents/` or `.claude/agents/`, this file wins.\r\n\r\n## Git identity\r\n\r\nThe only git identity an agent may use in this repository is:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nterezi <jules@foxtails.me>\r\n```\r\n\r\nSet it in the repository itself before the first commit, and do not rely on a\r\nmachine-wide default or invent a placeholder:\r\n\r\n```sh\r\ngit config user.name terezi\r\ngit config user.email jules@foxtails.me\r\n```\r\n\r\nEvery agent commit carries both fields. Do not use `A4`,\r\n`a4@example.invalid`, the host's auto-detected address, or any other\r\nidentity, and do not author on someone else's behalf. If a commit already\r\nexists under another identity, report it to the lead rather than rewriting\r\nhistory: an artifact's `build-info` names the commit it was built from, and\r\nre-authoring a commit changes that name.\r\n\r\n## Writing Style Rules\r\n\r\nThese rules apply to both chat responses, and to written documentation.\r\n\r\n- **Be direct.** Answer the question immediately. No introductions, filler, or unnecessary conclusions.\r\n- **Use natural language.** Write like a competent engineer, not a marketer, consultant, or chatbot.\r\n- **Be concise, not shallow.** Keep explanations short where possible, but never sacrifice technical detail, accuracy, or important nuance.\r\n- **Avoid AI-sounding prose.** No artificial contrasts, dramatic fragments, forced profundity, rhetorical questions, or rules of three.\r\n- **Don't flatter or validate.** Skip praise, excessive agreement, performative empathy, and conversational pleasantries.\r\n- **Be specific.** Prefer concrete facts, mechanisms, measurements, examples, and actionable steps over vague abstractions.\r\n- **Don't overstructure.** Use headings, lists, and tables only when they genuinely improve readability.\r\n- **Be honest about uncertainty.** Distinguish verified facts, reasonable inferences, and speculation. Don't manufacture confidence.\r\n- **Think critically.** Challenge incorrect assumptions, identify tradeoffs, and explain disagreements without hedging unnecessarily.\r\n- **Prioritize substance.** Every sentence should contribute useful information.
