The work so far, in order:\r\n\r\n1. **Day one (2026-11-12).** Vendored hgss-3ds's patch stack and build driver\r\n   (the decomp compiled under GCC, ~90 verified fixes), wrote the runtime and\r\n   renderer, and had Goldenrod rendering in Azahar from a prior bench save.\r\n   Found and fixed the PICA tile row-order bug; added frame stepping, state\r\n   dumps and an offline DS reference renderer.\r\n2. **Correctness (11-12 to 11-13).** Title-screen Ho-Oh: DS W-buffer depth,\r\n   direct G3 command-register writes routed to the geometry engine (patch\r\n   0302/2004), a crash handler, an offline projector and a zero-matrix trace.\r\n   A complete Windows build guide.\r\n3. **O3DS performance, sessions 2 and 3 (11-13 to 11-14).** Read the first\r\n   hardware logs, capped present skipping, shrank the G3 decode loop under the\r\n   I-cache, made Pok�mon crypto word-wide (game patch 2006), batched geometry\r\n   DMA, fixed the display-list cache and made it default, found the sound\r\n   mixer thread was never profiled, and added a scene-level profiler.\r\n4. **Audio, session 4 (11-15).** chatlog11's software audio plan in five\r\n   passes ([worklog](worklog/2026-11-15-audio.md)): measurement, ordinary-\r\n   routing fast path, ADPCM decoded as a run then resampled, exact `div127`,\r\n   PKHBT output, 192-frame blocks, held samples by default, a decoded-ADPCM\r\n   cache with a verify build, and kernel cache flush for wave buffers.\r\n   Azahar Goldenrod mixer 107.6 \u001a 48-49 ticks per channel-sample (14.8% \u001a\r\n   5-7% of the core), every step bit-exact. New tests: `sound_arm.py`\r\n   (Unicorn full-chip differential), `div127_test.c`, `sndprof.py`.\r\n5. **Geometry PR stack #6/#7/#8 (11-15).** Cheaper FIFO cache-hit keys,\r\n   skipping discarded field/title scene production, DS lighting moved to the\r\n   PICA with cached expanded lit geometry. Merged into `main` with origin/main;\r\n   integration testing found a cache hang (`037e134`) before the push.\r\n6. **Hardware cuts (11-15 to 11-16).** Baked stable lit lists, culled retained\r\n   blocks outside the picture, restored the NNS GLB state list from a prefix\r\n   snapshot, and skipped disabled lights. Azahar Goldenrod logic 25.35 \u001a\r\n   13.38 ms, triangles 5.02M \u001a 1.94M per 600 pictures, with pixel-identical\r\n   held frames. Still **O3DS_UNTESTED** on hardware.\r\n7. **Tooling and release.** Junction targets compared through `cygpath`, a\r\n   serial variant builder, GitHub Actions edition builds, edition asset\r\n   preparation, CIA forwarders, `prepare.py`/`prepare.bat` one-step ROM prep,\r\n   a README install walkthrough, and a null-BTP guard (patch 0307, issue #9).\r\n\r\n## 2. What worked\r\n\r\n**Strategy**\r\n- **Reuse the game-compile layer, rewrite the slow parts.** Vendoring the\r\n  hgss-3ds patch stack (with provenance) gave a linking game in hours; the\r\n  time went to the runtime and renderer, where hgss-3ds had lost its speed.\r\n- **One thread, one publish point.** Rendering at a single coherent point in\r\n  the game loop (patch 2001) removed the drawer/game races hgss-3ds spent\r\n  weeks on. No locks, no torn frames.\r\n- **GPU transform with a matrix palette.** DS matrix, lighting and test\r\n  semantics stay on the CPU; object-space vertices go to the PICA. 3D worked\r\n  first try, widescreen included (one fixup matrix).\r\n- **Doing less instead of doing it faster.** Baking stable lit lists, culling\r\n  offscreen retained blocks and restoring the GLB prefix removed work outright\r\n  and beat every micro-optimization.\r\n- **Read the docs first.** The coffeepot wiki already held \"never skip two\r\n  pictures in a row\" (frame-pacing) and the 16 KiB I-cache cliff\r\n  (cpu-optimization, icachebench).\r\n\r\n**Finding the truth**\r\n- **An independent oracle.** The GBATEK reference renderer found the tile\r\n  row-order bug in one comparison after guessing had failed.\r\n- **Read the hardware log before the code.** o3ds-log-0's `[pace]` and\r\n  `[frame]` lines showed presentation starvation; the per-opcode G3 profile\r\n  (probe cost of ~440 ticks, the empty END opcode, subtracted) ranked the\r\n  decoder's real costs.\r\n- **Real profiling.** Azahar's GDB stub plus a 150-line PC sampler found the\r\n  true hotspots, including Pok�mon crypto, which no reasoning predicted. A\r\n  Unicorn per-address count mapped with `addr2line` later found register\r\n  spills stage timers could only hint at.\r\n- **Calibrating the emulator.** A 4-instruction loop showed Azahar charges one\r\n  tick per instruction: its times are instruction counts, not O3DS time, and\r\n  it models neither caches nor PMU.\r\n- **Count before you build.** `[sndadpcm]` showed >95% of ADPCM decoding\r\n  repeats the same 15-20 sounds and sized the cache arena (256 KiB thrashed).\r\n  `[sndlock]` and `[sndout]` showed the game never waited on the sound lock\r\n  and the \"1 underrun\" in every hardware log was start-up, which removed two\r\n  planned changes.\r\n- **Verify modes.** `KJ_DL_VERIFY` (decode live, compare with replay) found\r\n  the display-list bug in one run, and, as a bisector, showed an image diff\r\n  did not come from the snapshot restore.\r\n\r\n**Keeping changes safe**\r\n- **Exact rewrites, checked by counters.** Every decoder change kept the same\r\n  batches, draws and triangles per 600 frames.\r\n- **A differential harness first.** `sound_arm.py` ran reference and working\r\n  mixers on identical random register programs, so every later change was\r\n  checked bit for bit in a minute.\r\n- **Mutation before trust.** Each new cache got a host test, then the test was\r\n  broken on purpose (dropped invalidations, a wrong plane) until it failed.\r\n  This exposed weak test designs before they could pass bad code.\r\n- **Commit each verified pass.** Every regression stayed bisectable to one\r\n  change.\r\n- **Test the merged tree before pushing.** The full native suite on the merge\r\n  found a hang no single branch showed.\r\n\r\n## 3. What went wrong, and how we recovered\r\n\r\n### Process\r\n\r\n| Problem | Recovery / rule |\r\n| --- | --- |\r\n| **Committing late.** Verified improvements sat uncommitted while riskier work piled on top. | Commit every verified step; gate risky features behind `--define` switches. |\r\n| **Building before measuring.** The display-list cache was written before its hit rate was known; most lists straddled DMA bursts or varied per frame. | Measure the opportunity first. |\r\n| **Measuring the wrong thing.** The cache replayed 4% of words; the first guess (lists left with BEGIN open) explained 13%. A coverage counter (`[dlcov]`) showed 65% were split mid-command by NitroSDK's 118-word DMA bursts. | Count where the work goes before fixing a guessed cause. |\r\n| **Guessing at render state.** Four Ho-Oh experiments (cull, depth, alpha test, blend) changed nothing. Dumping the scene and projecting it on the CPU (`g3_reference.py`) showed 41 all-zero clip matrices per frame: the geometry was wrong, not the GPU path. | Split the pipeline at a dump before toggling GPU state. |\r\n| **\"Ported\" is not \"complete\".** Patch 0302 converted GXFIFO stores but not the direct command-register stores beside them; the writes vanished silently. | When a hardware access class is ported, scan the whole tree for it (game patch 2004). |\r\n| **Misreading a counter.** `[ds] per frame` divides by presented frames; with skips it overstated per-game-frame costs, and a note wrongly claimed \"near full speed\". | Fixed the docs; counter semantics are written in testing.md. |\r\n| **Azahar hid a regression.** PR #8 doubled the O3DS captured frame (36 \u001a 57 ms) while Azahar still showed 30 FPS. | Compare work counts (instructions, triangles, draws, shader instructions per vertex), never Azahar FPS. |\r\n| **An unprofiled thread.** The DS sound mixer took 20-30% of the O3DS app core, but Azahar lacked DSP firmware, so `ndspInit` failed and the mixer never ran under test. | Every thread the device runs must run under test (`dspfirm.cdc` is now in Azahar's sdmc). |\r\n\r\n### Performance traps\r\n\r\n- **Timing probes that dominate.** Per-call `svcGetSystemTick` pairs cost ~390\r\n  ticks and nested DMA callbacks inflated the timed region. Prefer sampling.\r\n- **\"Uninstrumented\" builds still carried probes.** `PORT_NOW` in the H-blank\r\n  walk ignored `HGSS_PROFILE_OFF` (~800 tick calls a frame). Probes are now\r\n  opt-in (`HGSS_PROFILE=on`).\r\n- **Sampler bias.** Tight loops (the crypto XOR) looked bigger in samples than\r\n  in `[perf]` time. Cross-check with stage times.\r\n- **An uncapped present skip starves the screen.** \"Skip when two refreshes\r\n  behind\" never presents while the game runs slightly over budget: O3DS\r\n  Goldenrod ran at half speed but skipped 1606 of 2206 pictures. Skip at most\r\n  one picture in a row.\r\n- **Azahar cannot see code size.** Force-inlining the vertex fast path made\r\n  the decode loop 14.6 KiB against a 16 KiB I-cache (CPI hits 5.6 past\r\n  32 KiB). Check hot-function sizes with `nm -S`.\r\n- **Bump arenas that flush.** Re-recording into fresh space filled the arena\r\n  and flushed it twice per 600 frames (29.6 ms spikes). Reuse an entry's\r\n  storage when it re-records.\r\n- **Snapshot what repeats, not what nearly repeats.** A full GLB snapshot never\r\n  hit because its last word changes per model; splitting at the last command\r\n  word made the rest a constant prefix.\r\n- **Synthetic workloads mislead caches.** The first audio bench's instruments\r\n  were too large to repeat and showed the cache as a loss. Size synthetic data\r\n  from logs of the real workload.\r\n- **PICA bool uniforms read as false in Azahar** though the shbin, libctru and\r\n  citro3d looked correct. Unused `.w` components of float uniforms plus\r\n  `cmp`/`jmpc` work. The lit shader has no float uniform space left for new\r\n  arrays (91 + 7 of 96).\r\n\r\n### Code bugs\r\n\r\n- **Struct layout.** `memset(&s, 0, offsetof(s, array))` left counters after\r\n  the array unreset. Reset fields explicitly.\r\n- **State valid only after a reset.** The ADPCM cache's bucket table used -1\r\n  for empty, set by the reset; `sound_diff.c` skips the reset and hung in\r\n  `cache_find`. Links are now index + 1, so the zeroed table is empty. Make\r\n  the zeroed state valid.\r\n- **A cache check in the wrong path.** An early header comparison in the fill\r\n  path compared the wrong bytes. The verify build and harness caught it; every\r\n  check belongs where the entry is used.\r\n- **A digest that hashed raw addresses** reported a block-size change as a\r\n  behaviour change. Hash addresses relative to their buffer.\r\n- **A harness `memset` compiled into a call to itself** (GCC loop-pattern\r\n  distribution), a hang that looked like a slow emulator. Freestanding\r\n  helpers need `no-tree-loop-distribute-patterns`.\r\n- **Gaps found only by mutation.** The first coverage programs never shared a\r\n  sound between channels or rewrote bytes inside a playing sound, so breaking\r\n  cache invalidation still passed. Mutate each safety check once and confirm\r\n  the harness fails.\r\n\r\n### Build and environment\r\n\r\n- **An unverified build-system change regressed saves.** Switching the SDK shim\r\n  from copies to junctions changed what compiled; only a save check caught it.\r\n- **A path compare ignored MSYS2's mount spellings.** `Path.resolve()` spells\r\n  one directory `/c/...` or `/home/<user>/...` depending on which side of a\r\n  junction it starts from, so `link_points_to()` called a correct junction\r\n  missing and `_link()` re-ran `mklink /J`. Four parallel variants made three\r\n  lose the race. Compare through `cygpath -w` and serialize the variants\r\n  (`tools/game/build_variants.py`).\r\n- **A shared `build/upstream` checkout carries branch state.** It held\r\n  `wip/savestore`'s SDK patch 2003 while building `master`; `check_patches.py`\r\n  only detects missing patches, not extra ones. Re-created with\r\n  `bootstrap.py --clean` (2026-11-12); do the same after switching branches.\r\n- **Stacked PRs (#6 \u001b #7 \u001b #8)** target each other's branches; merging into\r\n  `main` by push does not close them on GitHub. A PR that adds a game patch\r\n  also needs `git -C build/upstream am` before it builds.\r\n- **Two harnesses for one module.** `sound_arm.py` resets the chip;\r\n  `check_hotpaths.py`'s `sound_diff.c` does not. Run both after mixer changes.\r\n\r\n### Test discipline\r\n\r\n- **Contaminated tests.** Live input reached scripted runs. Tests own their\r\n  input.\r\n- **Harness races.** A second `run.ps1` killed the first's emulator (three\r\n  lost runs). Stop the old harness first; one Azahar harness at a time.\r\n- **Lost samples.** gdbprof printed nothing when Azahar closed; it now prints\r\n  what it has.\r\n- **Stale reference images.** A wandering NPC moves with the emulated clock, so\r\n  an unchanged binary stopped matching references captured hours earlier;\r\n  three bisection builds chased it. Rerun the baseline binary first when only\r\n  character positions differ.\r\n- **Killing a test that was working.** A host check looked idle (Python at\r\n  1.7 s CPU, no children) but its binary ran under another parent. List every\r\n  process created since the start, with CPU time, before calling it hung.\r\n- **Cygwin signals in a tight loop.** An `alarm()` watchdog never fired; a\r\n  watchdog thread with `-finstrument-functions` named the looping function in\r\n  one run.\r\n\r\n### Shell and editing hazards\r\n\r\n- **Fragile command lines.** Multi-line heredocs with nested quotes were\r\n  mangled by the shell wrapper; complex edits belong in script files.\r\n- **Escapes through Git Bash.** A `sed` insertion turned a backslash-n in\r\n  `hgss_game.py` into a real newline (SyntaxError at build time) and\r\n  happened twice more. Use the editor tool, or avoid the escape (`putc(10)`).\r\n- **Windows Python turned LF into CRLF** (a 900-line diff). Write with\r\n  `newline=''`.\r\n- **A stray `cat >` with no input** stalled a command for a minute and left its\r\n  scripts unwritten.\r\n\r\n"

                "text": "\r\n## 4. Themes\r\n\r\n1. **Measure, then change.** Nearly every wasted effort (cache before hit rate,\r\n   render-state toggles, sampler or counter misreads) was a guess that a\r\n   counter, dump or oracle would have settled in one step.\r\n2. **The emulator is not the device.** Azahar counts instructions. It hides\r\n   cache cliffs, PICA cost, missing threads and real timing, so it ranks\r\n   instruction-count changes and nothing else.\r\n3. **Trust nothing you have not tried to break.** Verify modes, differential\r\n   harnesses and mutation testing caught more bugs than review did.\r\n4. **Small verified commits.** They made bisection cheap and risk containable.\r\n5. **Remove work first, speed it up second.**\r\n\r\n## Rules\r\n\r\n1. Commit each verified step; keep `master` building and verified.\r\n2. Check the Coffeepot wiki and `docs/engineering/hgss-remaster/` before\r\n   inventing a technique; cite it.\r\n3.               "newString": "There is one frame loop: the game's. O3DS is the design floor: the program\nnever enables the New 3DS clock or L2, and it runs in the ordinary 64 MB\napplication memory mode.\n\nPresentation is 30 Hz on O3DS by contract: the DS game ticks at 60 Hz, the\nrenderer presents every second coherent frame, and a late frame is dropped\nrather than delaying the game. 60 Hz frame interpolation, if added, is an\nopt-in New 3DS enhancement with its own thread budget; it is not part of the\nO3DS baseline and must never consume O3DS memory or CPU."

Real O3DS cost is higher wherever code misses caches.\r\n\r\n    python tools/azahar/gdbprof.py build/kj/pokeheartgold-3ds.elf \\\r\n        --samples 2000 --interval 0.01 --delay 140\r\n\r\nSpeaks the GDB remote serial protocol directly (devkitARM's gdb has no\r\nPython): interrupt (0x03), read the PC (register 15), continue.\r\n\"\"\"\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport argparse\r\nimport bisect\r\nimport collections\r\nimport socket\r\nimport subprocess\r\nimport sys\r\nimport time\r\n\r\n\r\nclass Rsp:\r\n    def __init__(self, host: str, port: int):\r\n        self.s = socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=10)\r\n        self.buf = b\"\"\r\n\r\n    def _read_packet(self) -> str:\r\n        while True:\r\n            while b\"$\" not in self.buf:\r\n                self.buf += self.s.recv(4096)\r\n            start = self.buf.index(b\"$\")\r\n            while b\"#\" not in self.buf[start:] or len(self.buf) < self.buf.index(b\"#\", start) + 3:\r\n                self.buf += self.s.recv(4096)\r\n            end = self.buf.index(b\"#\", start)\r\n            data = self.buf[start + 1:end]\r\n            self.buf = self.buf[end + 3:]\r\n            self.s.sendall(b\"+\")\r\n            return data.decode(\"latin-1\")\r\n\r\n    def send(self, data: str) -> None:\r\n        csum = sum(data.encode(\"latin-1\")) & 0xFF\r\n        self.s.sendall(f\"${data}#{csum:02x}\".encode(\"latin-1\"))\r\n        # wait for ack\r\n        while True:\r\n            if not self.buf:\r\n                self.buf += self.s.recv(4096)\r\n            c, self.buf = self.buf[:1], self.buf[1:]\r\n            if c == b\"+\":\r\n                return\r\n            if c == b\"-\":\r\n                self.s.sendall(f\"${data}#{csum:02x}\".encode(\"latin-1\"))\r\n\r\n    def request(self, data: str) -> str:\r\n        self.send(data)\r\n        return self._read_packet()\r\n\r\n    def interrupt(self) -> str:\r\n        self.s.sendall(b\"\\x03\")\r\n        return self._read_packet()\r\n\r\n\r\ndef load_symbols(elf: str, nm: str):\r\n    out = subprocess.run([nm, \"-n\", \"-C\", elf], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout\r\n    addrs, names = [], []\r\n    for line in out.splitlines():\r\n        parts = line.split(None, 2)\r\n        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1].lower() in (\"t\", \"w\"):\r\n            addrs.append(int(parts[0], 16))\r\n            names.append(parts[2])\r\n    return addrs, names\r\n\r\n\r\ndef sample(a, r, hist, callers, watch, sym, pcs):\r\n    for _ in range(a.samples):\r\n        time.sleep(a.interval)\r\n        r.interrupt()\r\n=== usage ===\r\n203: - **PC sampling**: with Azahar's GDB stub enabled (`use_gdbstub=true`, port\r\n204: 24689), `python tools/azahar/gdbprof.py build/kj/pokeheartgold-3ds.elf\r\n"

                "type": "text",
                "text": "\r\n\u001b[32;1mName\u001b[0m\r\n\u001b[32;1m----\u001b[0m\r\n2d-tile-renderer.md\r\n3d-scene-optimisation.md\r\nasset-pipeline.md\r\nframe-pacing.md\r\ngpu-rendering.md\r\npica200-command-pipeline.md\r\npica200-shader-programming.md\r\nrenderer-architecture.md\r\nrendering-2d.md\r\nstereo-engineering.md\r\n3: Making a 3DS program fast is mostly about finding out *which* part is slow before changing anything. The console has a slow CPU (268 MHz on an Old 3DS; **New 3DS:** up to 804 MHz), a capable but unusual GPU, and a small amount of fast memory; a frame can be late because the CPU ran out of time, because the GPU did, because one waited for the other, or because something stalled on a file or a system service. This page shows how to measure each of those with the libraries homebrew already uses, how to pace frames, how to use the second CPU core, and which CPU-side habits pay off on this processor.\r\n5: Related pages: [memory and cache](memory-and-cache.md) (where buffers live and what flushing costs), [GPU rendering](PICA200/gpu-rendering.md) (draw-call and state costs), [testing on hardware](testing-on-hardware.md) (how to run a benchmark you can trust).\r\n15: At 60 frames per second a frame lasts 16.7 ms. The ARM11 application core on an Old 3DS runs at 268,111,856 Hz ([CPU](../hardware/cpu.md#clocks-and-core-counts)), so one frame is about 4.47 million clock cycles - before the operating system, cache misses, waiting for the GPU and interrupt handling take their share.\r\n17: > **New 3DS:** with the fast mode enabled the core runs at 804 MHz (3x) with a 2 MB L2 cache, so a frame is about 13.4 million cycles at 60 fps.\r\n19: | Target | Frame time | Old 3DS core-0 cycles per frame |\r\n21: | 60 fps | 16.7 ms | � 4.47 M |\r\n22: | 30 fps | 33.3 ms | � 8.94 M |\r\n52: /* in the frame loop */\r\n63: Report the **worst** frame and percentiles, not only the average: an average of 12 ms can hide a 200 ms hitch every few seconds, and the hitch is what players notice.\r\n71: | `C3D_GetProcessingTime()` | Elapsed time from the successful `C3D_FrameBegin` after queue wait to the counter update in `C3D_FrameEnd`, including the end hook and command-list split. It is wall time, including any intervening work or preemption | Work before the timer starts, the default whole-linear-heap flush, render-target transfer setup and queue start; those occur after the counter update |\r\n72: | `C3D_GetDrawingTime()` | Wall-clock time from `C3D_FrameEnd` starting the GX command queue until the queue-finished callback runs: the GPU executing the command list **plus** the display transfers to the LCD framebuffers queued for that frame, plus the latency of the completion interrupt reaching your process | Anything that happened on a frame that has not finished yet: the value refers to the most recently *completed* frame |\r\n74: `C3D_FrameEnd` also flushes the CPU data cache over the whole linear heap unless you pass `GX_CMDLIST_FLUSH` (below and in [memory and cache](memory-and-cache.md#the-c3d_frameend-flush)); that flush happens after the processing counter is updated and before the GPU timer starts, so it appears in neither timer. Time the whole `C3D_FrameEnd` call separately; it includes the hook and command-list split as well as later flush and submission work, so do not add all of it to `C3D_GetProcessingTime` without accounting for overlap. After `C3D_FrameEnd`, the processing sample is for that CPU frame; the drawing value is the latest completed queue measurement, which can belong to a different submission. Associate GPU results with queue completion, not merely the current loop index. [documented: citro3d `renderqueue.c` at the pinned commit; libctru `os.h` and `os.c`]\r\n76: ### Per-operation GPU times: the GSP performance log\r\n78: Since libctru 2.5.0, `GSPGPU_SetPerfLogMode(true)` and `GSPGPU_GetPerfLog(&log)` read a performance log kept by the system's GPU service (**[GSP](../glossary.md#gsp)**): for each GPU operation type (`GSPGPU_EVENT_P3D` command-list processing, `GSPGPU_EVENT_PPF` display transfer/texture copy, `GSPGPU_EVENT_PSC0`/`PSC1` memory fills, `VBlank0/1`), the duration of the last one and a running total in microseconds [documented: libctru `gspgpu.h`]. This separates \"the GPU is slow drawing\" (P3D) from \"copying to the screen is slow\" (PPF) from \"clearing is slow\" (PSC). The header's notes matter:\r\n80: - Use differences of `totalDurationUs` between two points you choose; a frame contains several operations of each type, and the total can overflow.\r\n82: - The first frame after enabling the log has nonsense VBlank entries; very short fills may finish before the system records their start.\r\n83: - Enable it while no GPU operation is in progress.\r\n85: ### Reliability of GPU timers (measured)\r\n87: **Tie a GPU sample to its frame before reading it** [documented: citro3d `renderqueue.c` and `base.c` at `9f21cf7`, libctru `gxqueue.c` at `62b7c42`]:\r\n89: - `C3D_FrameSync()` waits for V-blank counters, not for the GPU. A timer read straight after `C3D_FrameEnd` plus `C3D_FrameSync` is from this frame only if the GPU happened to finish before that V-blank, and nothing tells you whether it did.\r\n90: - To sample one submission, wait until its queue is idle, then read `C3D_GetDrawingTime()` and the perf log. citro3d has no public call for that; `gxCmdQueueWait` (libctru) waits for the running GX queue, or read the timers after the next `C3D_FrameBegin` returns and attribute them to the previous frame.                 "type": "text",
                "text": "3: Frame pacing is about *when* frames appear, not only how many: a game that shows a new picture at a steady 30 per second feels smoother than one that alternates between 60 and 40. On the 3DS both screens refresh at about 60 Hz, the GPU works asynchronously from the CPU, and **[citro3d](../../glossary.md#libctru)** decides when to wait for each. This page explains the timing model, how to structure the main loop so CPU and GPU overlap, how to lock to 60 or 30 fps, how to keep game speed independent of rendering speed, and how to detect missed frames.\r\n30: The GPU draws one image per render target per frame, not a fixed three. With the 3D slider off, a typical frame is a top image plus a bottom image (two); with 3D on, a left-eye and a right-eye top image plus the bottom (three) ([GPU](../../hardware/gpu.md)). A screen whose contents did not change needs no image at all: citro3d swaps a screen's framebuffer only if a target for it was drawn that frame (see Technical details), so a mostly static bottom screen can be skipped by not drawing its target [documented: citro3d `renderqueue.c`; the saving is unmeasured]. Check `gfxIs3D()` or the slider and skip the right-eye target when it is off. The 2DS family has no stereoscopic 3D, so this path is always the two-image case there.\r\n49: Putting game logic between `C3D_FrameBegin` and `C3D_FrameEnd` serialises the two processors: the GPU idles while the CPU updates, then the CPU idles in the next `C3D_FrameBegin` [documented mechanism; the size of the gain depends on the workload and is unmeasured here]. If you must prepare GPU-visible data before `C3D_FrameBegin`, write it into a second copy of the buffer (double-buffering) and swap.\r\n53: A more aggressive pipeline can prepare a later command buffer while an earlier frame executes. Keep each command buffer and every referenced texture or vertex buffer immutable until GPU completion; separately keep a framebuffer unavailable for reuse while it is pending presentation or scanout. Track these as distinct ownership transitions and measure CPU wait, GPU completion, presentation and input latency. More buffers can improve overlap but can also increase latency and memory use; the net result is [hypothesis] until measured on the target.\r\n59: For the conservative loop above, prepare ordinary CPU-only state while the previous frame executes, wait for the library's synchronization point, then write GPU-visible data, submit and preserve it until the next completion. Cache visibility and lifetime are separate: flushing makes CPU writes visible but does not grant permission to overwrite data still in use. Track display presentation separately from GPU completion when reusing scanout buffers.\r\n61: For a ring or double-buffered design, assign each slot an owner and a completion condition: CPU-free \u001a CPU-writing \u001a submitted/GPU-reading \u001a GPU-complete \u001a CPU-free. Use a distinct slot when building ahead; wait or skip safely if no slot is free. Record which submission each timing value describes, and ensure a result from the previous frame is not attributed to the current one. An audio or loading worker needs bounded queues and must not hold a lock across blocking I/O; the system core also runs services, so thread placement needs [its own validation](../threading.md#proving-a-worker-improves-frame-time). These ownership rules do not constitute a tested asynchronous implementation; the advanced citro3d-internal approach in the case study is version-sensitive.\r\n68: | Steady 30 fps (or 20, 15) | `C3D_FrameRate(30.0f)` once, then `C3D_FRAME_SYNCDRAW` as usual: the V-blank counters `C3D_FrameSync` waits on now advance only every second V-blank |\r\n70: | Never block the game thread on the GPU | `C3D_FrameBegin(C3D_FRAME_NONBLOCK)`; when it returns `false`, skip rendering this iteration (keep simulating) |\r\n72: `C3D_FrameRate(fps)` accepts values above 0 and up to 60 and returns the previous setting. It works by a per-screen accumulator: each V-blank subtracts `fps` from it, and whenever it drops to zero or below, 60 is added back and the frame counter advances, so non-divisor rates such as 45 produce an uneven cadence [documented: `renderqueue.c`]. Prefer 60, 30, 20 or 15.\r\n74: **Choose 30 deliberately.** If the slowest target cannot hold 60, a locked 30 avoids the judder of a rate that drifts between 40 and 60.\r\n132: - **Skip the picture, keep the tick.** sm64ds-enhanced's \"dry\" mode skips building a frame (no raster, no compose, no present) when a tick starts more than half a period behind the game clock, never two in a row, so logic catches up while the screens keep the last frame; the default on an Old 3DS with 60 fps off is \"when behind\" `[documented]` (`port3ds/game/main_game.cpp` near line 1236; [case study](../case-studies/case-study-sm64ds-enhanced.md)).\r\n133: - **One gate can pace video, audio and frameskip.** Daedalus treats a change of the emulated video origin as a finished frame, derives a sync ratio from it, enters frameskip when the ratio is below 0.965, and clamps its audio sync rate to 1,500-4,000 `[documented]` (`GraphicsPluginCTR.cpp` lines 46, 202-206, 227; [case study](../case-studies/case-study-daedalus-3ds.md)).\r\n134: - **Vsync through a library, no governor.** DXX's `gr_flip` blits and calls `SDL_Flip`; Quake2CTR's loop has an empty `Sys_Sleep` and swaps through picaGL. Neither skips frames, so a missed vsync is a visible hitch `[documented]` ([DXX](../case-studies/case-study-dxx-3ds.md), [Quake2CTR](../case-studies/case-study-quake2ctr.md)).\r\n137: - **An uncapped \"skip when behind\" rule starves the screen.** The kohjoh DS port skipped a picture whenever it was two refreshes behind. A game running only slightly over budget was then always behind: an Old 3DS log showed the game at about half speed but only about 4 pictures a second shown (1,606 of 2,206 pictures skipped), which looked like a much slower game. Skip at most one picture in a row; the fix is the same rule sm64ds-enhanced uses above [reported: kohjoh project notes, 2026-11-13, private repository; Old 3DS log, build and firmware not recorded in the notes; `docs/lessons.md`].\r\n151: - **Assuming one frame = 1/60 s in game logic** while the game runs at 30: everything moves at half speed.\r\n163: - kohjoh project notes (private repository, no public revision yet; `docs/lessons.md`, read 2026-11-13) - uncapped present skip and V-blank locking.\r\n"

$i -lt 60; $i++) {\n    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 100\n    $p.Refresh()\n    if ($p.MainWindowHandle -ne 0) { $h = $p.MainWindowHandle; break }\n  }\n  if ($h -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) { throw \"no emulator window\" }\n  [P.T]::MoveWindow($h, 0, 0, 840, 1100, $true) | Out-Null\n  [void][P.T]::SetForegroundWindow($h)\n  function Shot([string]$name) {\n    $r = New-Object P.T+RECT\n    [P.T]::GetWindowRect($h, [ref]$r) | Out-Null\n    $w = $r.Right - $r.Left; $hh = $r.Bottom - $r.Top\n    $bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $w, $hh\n    $g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bmp)\n    $dc = $g.GetHdc(); [P.T]::PrintWindow($h, $dc, 2) | Out-Null\n    $g.ReleaseHdc($dc); $g.Dispose()\n    $bmp.Save((Join-Path $out \"$name.png\"), [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)\n    $bmp.Dispose()\n    Write-Output \"shot $name\"\n  }\n  Start-Sleep -Seconds $WaitSeconds\n  Shot \"before\"\n  $r = New-Object P.T+RECT\n  [P.T]::GetWindowRect($h, [ref]$r) | Out-Null\n  for ($i = 0; $i -lt $Clicks; $i++) {\n    [void][P.T]::SetCursorPos($r.Left + $ClickX, $r.Top + $ClickY)\n    [P.T]::mouse_event(0x0002, 0, 0, 0, [UIntPtr]::Zero)  # left down\n    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 120\n    [P.T]::mouse_event(0x0004, 0, 0, 0, [UIntPtr]::Zero)  # left up\n    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds $IntervalMs\n    if ($i -eq 2 -or $i -eq 7) { Shot (\"click{0}\" -f $i) }\n  }\n  Shot \"after\"\n} finally {\n  if (-not $p.HasExited) { Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }\n}\n",
